tests.title: Convex sizing — does reallocating the SAME gross planned risk from correlated tickets to independent ones raise dollar P&L?
tests.name: Convex sizing — correlation-weighted stake at constant gross risk
tests.origin: Operator standing directive: 'risk little to gain a lot'. The board sizes FLAT — a 0.25% policy stake on every ticket, whether it is the ninth correlated energy short of the session or the only independent bet on the board. Measured context: 81% of the stop tail is correlated exposure and ticket-to-episode inflation is 3.1x, so the ninth ticket in a factor group is not a ninth bet.
tests.rule: Per session, order tickets by openedAt. For each, nPriorCorrelated = tickets already open that share a factor-group token (lib/enforcement-gates.js groupTokens) AND point the same direction; an opposing ticket is a hedge and never counts. Weight w = 1/sqrt(1 + nPriorCorrelated), floored at 0.25, capped at 1.0. Weights are renormalised per session so TOTAL PLANNED RISK EQUALS the flat book's — this is a reallocation, not a de-risking, and the runner exits non-zero if that identity ever breaks. Conviction multiplier is wired into the formula and PINNED AT 1.0: sizing up requires a score with measured forward skill, and the daily board has none (ridge day-corr t -0.21, gbm -1.64).
tests.hypothesis: NEUTRAL, and stated after an unflattering retrospective. The motivating sample runs NEGATIVE and is recorded as such below.
tests.whyItCanBeMeasuredExactly: R-multiples are size-invariant (rMult = pnl/riskDollars), so pnlConvex = rMult x riskConvex is arithmetic, not a simulated fill. Every registered test on this board reads R, so a sizing change cannot move any registered statistic — it moves dollar P&L only.

bar.statistic: per-session dollar difference (convex minus flat), day-clustered t
bar.confirmIf: day-clustered t >= 2.0 over at least 30 forward sessions
bar.decisionRule: CONFIRMED -> propose convex sizing as live policy, recorded as a risk-policy change. NOT CONFIRMED -> flat sizing stands and the rule is retired.
bar.formsNote: ONE pre-specified form is under test: exponent 0.5 from the independent-bets argument, floor 0.25. Nothing was tuned on the ledger. If a grid of exponents or floors is ever searched, that search owes a best-of-N bar from lib/null-bar.js and this field must be updated before the read.

tests.priorSample: RETROSPECTIVE, MOTIVATING, NEGATIVE — and recorded because it is unflattering. Over the 26 clean-era sessions (875 tickets, gross planned risk identical every session): flat +$2,689 vs convex -$4,304, a difference of -$6,993, improved on 9 of 26 sessions, day-clustered t -1.02. The result is dominated by two sessions: convex CUT the worst day (2026-08-20) by +$3,448 and CUT the best day (2026-08-24, the 20-ticket crypto cluster) by -$5,462. It clips both tails, which is what it is designed to do; on this sample the win tail it clipped was the larger one.
tests.bothTailsNote: Recorded under the standing both-tails rule: any rule that clips a loss tail must be measured for the win tail it also clips. Here the loss-tail clip is +$3,448 and the win-tail clip is -$5,462 on the two sessions that dominate the sample.
tests.relatedFinding: Splitting the clean era by correlation-at-entry: independent tickets (nPrior = 0) ran n 357, -$9,502, mean R -0.0564; correlated tickets ran n 518, +$12,191. Day-clustered, the independent bucket is -0.1030R at day-t -1.30 and the paired independent-minus-correlated gap is -0.1069R at day-t -1.60 — BELOW ANY BAR, established as nothing. The ticket-level t was -2.08 and is NOT quotable: effective-N inflation is 3.1x and the session is the unit. If that direction survives forward it says the board has no independent-bet edge and its P&L is directional clustering, which would be a finding about the signal, not about sizing.
tests.doNotFlipTheSign: The inverse rule (concentrate risk INTO correlated tickets) would score positively on this same sample. Adopting it now would be choosing a rule after seeing its result on the data it is measured against — the exact defect this registry exists to prevent. If it is ever tested it enters as a declared family of 2 with a best-of-2 bar, and it is a leverage story rather than an edge story: it would have made 2026-08-20 materially worse.
tests.enforcement: NOT ENFORCED. The twin stamps both sizings and accrues; live sizing stays flat until this clears its bar. Same shadow-then-wire path R49 and R53 completed on 2026-08-27.
tests.status: REGISTERED 2026-08-28 — bar fixed in advance; retrospective disclosed as negative and excluded from the read

amendments.what: Added the `script` field. The entry named no runner, so the test was unlocatable and had never accrued a row.
amendments.finding: On building the writer, the rule turns out to have almost no population on this book. Implemented verbatim, nPriorCorrelated is ZERO on every session of the evidence window: of ~40 tickets a day only ~17 carry a factor-group token, exactly one token+direction group per session holds more than one ticket, and the pair that does share a group opens at the SAME INSTANT — so neither is 'already open' relative to the other. The rule assumes sequential entry; this book enters in batches. Convex therefore equals flat to the cent and the statistic cannot discriminate.
amendments.disposition: NOT amended. Changing 'already open' to 'concurrently open' would give the rule a population and is legal pre-evidence (nothing has accrued), but it is a change to what the test MEASURES and belongs to the operator, not to the night the writer was built. The writer ships as specified and reports $0.00 per session honestly.

preregistered.parent: alerts cron scanner (backend/traids-alerts.js)
preregistered.rule: The Alerts scanner's 7-model ensemble produces directional calls (BUY above vote +0.3, SELL below -0.3) on 100 large caps. R7 asks whether those calls carry forward edge, and whether the number the panel labels 'Confidence' predicts anything. NOTHING TRADES on this; the collector records and settles only.
preregistered.mechanism: The scanner is a second view of the same MACD/RSI/Bollinger/EMA/ROC family the board already runs, which measured +0.0040R against random over 338 settles. The prior is therefore that it has no edge. It is being measured rather than deleted because it is cheap to grade and because its 'Confidence' column is currently an UNCALIBRATED unanimity ratio being displayed to a human as a percent — that specific claim is falsifiable and worth falsifying.
preregistered.origin: 2026-07-30, operator: 'what is this; how is it calculated; how is this applied to our signals'. Audit found the scanner feeds only the panel and the (inert) email/SMS path — no trade log, not a weighted-board contributor, zero calls ever graded, alert history empty.

design.cohortA: UNBIASED DAILY SNAPSHOT — all 100 rows recorded once per ET trading day, first scan of the day wins. Recorded regardless of signal, so there is no selection on the call being interesting. This is the primary cohort.
design.cohortB: FLIP EVENTS — rows where the scanner's own alert gate fires (confidence>=0.6 AND |vote|>=0.4 AND flipped). This is what it would have texted. Secondary cohort; graded separately and NOT pooled with A.
design.horizons: +1, +3, +5 TRADING days, settled close-to-close from the entry bar. Fixed in advance; no horizon may be added after seeing a result.
design.primaryEndpoint: Cohort A, +3 trading days, MARKET-RELATIVE signed return (dirRet - dir*SPY over the same window). Market-relative because a directional call on 100 correlated large caps is mostly a bet on the tape; the raw number would grade the market, not the scanner.
design.directionSign: BUY -> +ret, SELL -> -ret. NEUTRAL rows are recorded and settled but excluded from the directional endpoint; they are used only to test whether NEUTRAL is distinguishable from the directional buckets.

threshold.sidakFamily: 3 horizons x 2 cohorts = 6 tests. Šidák-corrected two-sided alpha per test = 1-(1-0.05)^(1/6) = 0.0085, i.e. |t| >= 2.71 for a secondary cell to count. The PRIMARY endpoint alone is tested at t>=2.0.
threshold.why: Thresholds chosen structurally before any evidence. They may never be re-tuned to fit a result — a change means abandoning R7 and registering R8.

effectiveN.rule: MANDATORY day-clustering. 100 symbols scanned on the same morning are ONE observation of one tape, not 100 independent ones. The t-statistic is computed across DAILY MEANS; effective N is the number of trading days, never the number of calls.
effectiveN.why: This is the error that made the pocket sweep look significant before correction. Pooling calls would report t~10 on pure noise.

calibration.claim: The panel prints 'Confidence' as a percent next to a BUY/SELL. R7 tests it as a stated probability.
calibration.method: Bucket every directional call by its confidence value (the ratio is degenerate — only 0, .14, .2, .33, .5, .6, 1.0 are reachable). For each bucket report n, days, claimed confidence, and ACTUAL hit rate with a Wilson 95% interval.
calibration.bar: Confidence is CALIBRATED only if actual hit rate rises monotonically with the claimed value across buckets holding n>=50, and the 100% bucket's interval excludes 50%. Anything else and the column is renamed to 'Model Agreement' in the UI, because displaying an uncalibrated ratio as a confidence percent is a defect regardless of whether the scanner has edge.

knownWeaknesses: Confidence's denominator is the count of NON-SILENT models, so a row where 4 of 7 models abstain can read 100%. The calibration test will likely fail on this alone; that is the expected result, not a surprise.
Cohort B may never accrue - the gate has fired zero times in the panel's history. If it stays under 30 by the Aug 14 checkup it is reported UNMEASURABLE, not assumed correct.
100 large caps are heavily correlated; even market-relative returns share sector factors. Day-clustering handles the tape but not sector concentration.

The universe is a fixed hardcoded list, so it carries survivorship bias by construction - these are 100 companies that are large caps TODAY. This biases toward the long side and is why the primary endpoint is market-relative and both directions are reported separately.
Daily closes only. Any intraday edge in a flip signal is invisible to this design.

preregistered.parent: earnings events (origin: operator 2026-07-30, 'our system should have caught MSFT +16%, META -9%, NOW -5% before it happened')
preregistered.rule: Two separable questions about scheduled earnings prints, both observe-only. R8a DIRECTION: does anything the system already measures predict the SIGN of an earnings gap? R8b PEAD: after a large gap, does price drift in the gap's direction (post-earnings-announcement drift)? Nothing trades on either until its bar is met.
preregistered.mechanism: R8a prior: NO. Gap direction is the most heavily arbitraged single-number prediction in finance — straddle sellers price magnitude and take no directional view profitably. Registering it anyway because the observers are already collected, the test is nearly free, and a NULL result permanently retires the recurring 'we should have caught X' conversation with data. R8b prior: WEAK YES. PEAD is among the oldest documented anomalies (Ball & Brown 1968; Bernard & Thomas 1989) — underreaction causes drift for days to weeks after the print. It requires no prediction: the information exists before the position would.

design.universe: lite-scan universe ∩ Finnhub earnings calendar (/api/finnhub/earnings), US listings only
design.freeze: nightly in the close chain, BEFORE the print: for every name reporting within the next 2 calendar days, freeze {newsScore, svrZ, mom20} — news and svrZ from market-lite-scan.json as-of that night, mom20 from real daily bars. Frozen values are sealed; a freeze after the print is discarded.

directionMappings.note: FIXED NOW, mechanism-first, never re-signed after results
directionMappings.newsScore: sign(newsScore) predicts gap sign — pre-print tone reflects information flow
directionMappings.mom20: sign(20d return) predicts gap sign — drift into the print continues through it
directionMappings.svrZ: sign(svrZ) predicts gap sign — EXPLORATORY, no strong mechanism; carried because it is the one observer with any earned (inverted) weight elsewhere

design.gapDefinition: close-to-close spanning the print (amc: report-day close → next close; bmo: prior close → report-day close), MARKET-RELATIVE (minus SPY same window)
design.peadEndpoint: post-gap close → +1/+5/+20 TRADING days, signed by gap direction, market-relative, day-clustered by PRINT DATE (an earnings cluster night is one observation, not twenty)

r8a.bar: per-observer hit rate vs 50%, day-clustered; 3 observers x 1 endpoint → Šidák two-sided |t|>=2.39 each. Below the bar at n>=60 → observer PERMANENTLY retired from direction claims.
r8a.note: betting-against: the registered prediction is that ALL THREE fail

r8b.bar: +5d drift (PRIMARY): day-clustered t>=2.0 at >=30 gaps across >=10 print dates. +1d/+20d are secondary at Šidák |t|>=2.39.
r8b.note: if the bar is met, the NEXT step is a paper sleeve with entry at the post-gap close — never a live wire from one clearing

effectiveN.rule: cluster by PRINT DATE. Mega-cap earnings nights put 5-20 prints on one macro tape; pooling them is the pocket-sweep error again.

knownWeaknesses: Finnhub free-tier calendar can miss or mis-time small caps; a print observed at settle with no freeze row is logged as MISSED, never backfilled — backfilling would peek.
Earnings cluster ~4x/year: R8a needs ~2 quarters to reach 60 prints; interim reads are labelled interim.
5% PEAD trigger interacts with market cap (a 5% MSFT move is enormous, a 5% OTLK move is Tuesday); market-relative settle helps, cap-bucketing is NOT registered and would be an R9.
The +20d horizon overlaps subsequent macro events; day-clustering handles shared tape, not idiosyncratic follow-on news.

preregistered.parent: R8 earnings shadow (extends its freeze; origin: operator — 'its not about this one trade; its about capturing trades like this before they happen')
preregistered.rule: Two pre-print capture hypotheses, both frozen BEFORE each print by the R8 collector. R9a EVENT-VOL: is the realized earnings move systematically LARGER than the option market's implied move in an identifiable cohort? If yes, the capture is buying the event straddle — direction-free; no forecast of sign required. R9b PEER READ-THROUGH: when a mega-cap peer posted a large surprise earlier in the same cycle (MSFT's cloud blowout the night before AMZN's), does the next related print drift the same direction?
preregistered.mechanism: R9a: implied move is a real traded price, so beating it requires the market to systematically underprice event risk in a cohort — plausible in theme-concentrated cycles (AI capex), and cleanly falsifiable since both numbers are observable. Prior: WEAK/NO — sellers of event vol are profitable on average (test #41 family); the question is whether a cohort exists where they are not. R9b: intra-industry information transfer is documented (Foster 1981 onward): the first big reporter in a theme re-prices the whole theme for the rest. MSFT->AMZN this week is the live example — the signal EXISTED Wednesday night.

design.r9aFreeze: impliedMovePct — nearest-expiry ATM straddle (call mid + put mid) / spot, frozen pre-print with the R8 observers. Realized = |raw gap| at settle. Endpoint: mean(realized − implied) and the ratio, day-clustered by print date; cohort splits allowed ONLY along pre-declared lines: megacap-optionable vs rest.
design.r9bFreeze: peerSignal — at freeze time, the signed mean relGap of settled prints from the SAME cycle in the prior 3 trading days, and megaPeer: the sign of any |relGap|>=5% print among the OPTIONABLE megacap set in the prior 3 trading days (0 if none). Predicts sign(relGap) of the frozen print.
design.honesty: Both freeze fields obey the hour-aware guard — a post-print freeze is contaminated and never graded. Sector-refined peers (matching by industry, not the megacap set) are NOT registered; adding them later is an R9c amendment, not a re-tune of R9b.

r9a.bar: mean(realized−implied) day-clustered t>=2.0 overall, OR >=2.39 (Šidák, 2 cohorts) in a pre-declared cohort. A NEGATIVE result (implied > realized) is the seller's edge and routes to the gated VRP sleeve instead — both signs are actionable.

r9b.bar: sign hit rate vs 50%, day-clustered t>=2.0, counting only prints where megaPeer!=0 or |peerSignal|>0.5% — a prediction of 'no information' is not a prediction.

knownWeaknesses: Implied move from an indicative feed's nearest chain is noisier than a broker straddle quote; wide quotes bias implied UP, which biases R9a AGAINST finding realized>implied — the conservative direction.
Chain fetches are rate-limited; nights with partial coverage stamp null for the missing names — coverage is reported, never silently assumed.

R9b's megacap peer set is the OPTIONABLE list — a theme proxy, not a sector map. It will miss non-megacap read-throughs and dilute across unrelated themes; that dilution makes it HARDER to pass, not easier.
Earnings cycles cluster: ~2 quarters to the bars.
preregistered.status: REGISTERED — observe-only. Freeze fields live in r8-earnings-shadow.js; graded beside R8 in its report.

paperSleeve.added: 2026-07-31 (operator: 'why is our system not paper trading them now') — rules fixed BEFORE the first entry; adding a sleeve does not touch R9's thresholds
paperSleeve.rules: EVENT-STRADDLE PAPER SLEEVE, 1 contract per event, mechanical: for every MEGA-or-lite name frozen pre-print with a usable ATM chain, BUY the nearest ATM call and put at their real ASKS at freeze time (both legs must quote <=4%/side or the event is skipped and counted); SELL both legs at their real BIDS on the first nightly run at least one trading day after the print; $0.65/contract/leg commissions (4 legs round trip). No sizing discretion, no selection beyond the quoted-spread policy, no early exits.
paperSleeve.grading: net $ and % per event, day-clustered by print date, reported beside R9a's shadow numbers. The sleeve P&L is the ALL-IN version of R9a (it pays the real spread toll the shadow can only estimate); R9a's registered bar still governs promotion, and sleeve results never justify re-tuning it.
paperSleeve.promotion: nothing auto-promotes. If R9a's bar is met AND the sleeve is net positive after costs over the same window, the decision to size it goes to the operator with both numbers on the table.

preregistered.dteDefect: DISCLOSED 2026-08-26, bug fixed, bar UNCHANGED. R9a's registered rule specifies a NEAREST-EXPIRY ATM straddle. backend/r8-earnings-shadow.js omitted the dte parameter when calling /api/option-chain-pick, which silently applied that endpoint's 35-day default, so every frozen impliedMovePct was a ~35-DTE straddle measured against a ONE-SESSION realised gap. A 35-day straddle prices five weeks of uncertainty; comparing one session of realised move to it is guaranteed to come in short, which is why the reported realized-minus-implied was -8.99pp at a day-clustered t of -8.52 — the largest t in this registry and entirely a units error. THE FIX IS A BUG FIX, NOT AN AMENDMENT: the code was brought into line with the rule as registered; the rule was not changed to fit the code. CONSEQUENCE FOR EVIDENCE: every impliedMovePct frozen before 2026-08-26 measured a different quantity and MUST NOT be pooled with post-fix freezes. R9a's usable evidence starts at the first print frozen after this date. The adjudicator flagged this before any of it was acted on, and its instruction stands: the negative sign was mechanical and was never routed to the VRP seller sleeve, which R9's own decision rule would otherwise have done.

evidenceVoid.action: The 101 pre-fix impliedMovePct prints (all frozen <= 2026-08-25T20:16Z, before the 2026-08-26T20:57:31Z nearest-expiry fix, commit 8bbb591b) are stamped voidForEvidence on their settledGaps rows in backend/data/r8-earnings-shadow.json — kept on disk with a dated per-row reason, never deleted, never silently pooled. r8-earnings-shadow.js r9a aggregation and the adjudicator R9 resolver both now exclude voided rows. report.r9a reset to 0 prints / null on 2026-08-31; R9a reads WAIT (0/40), not READY TO READ, until fresh post-fix freezes accrue.
evidenceVoid.residualDefectFoundAndFixed: The 2026-08-26 nearest=1 flag only re-sorted the rows Alpaca already returned; the fetch window (traids-server-v2.js option-chain-pick) was still dteTarget+/-18d with dteTarget silently defaulting to 35 (r8-earnings-shadow.js never passes an explicit dte), i.e. 17-53 DTE — so a weekly expiring inside 17 days, exactly the contract an earnings-adjacent straddle needs, was never even requested from the chain snapshot. Verified live 2026-08-31: nearest=1 alone still returned an 18.2-DTE AAPL/MSFT/NVDA straddle (the window floor). Fixed by widening the fetch window itself when nearest=1 is set (tomorrow through +45d, no dteTarget dependency); verified live again post-fix: 2.2-DTE AAPL/MSFT/NVDA, 1.2-DTE SPY, implied move 4-6pp lower than the old 35-DTE number for the same names at the same moment (AAPL 5.86% at 32.2dte vs 1.16% at 2.2dte). Evidence going forward is priced with the true nearest expiry.

preregistered.evidenceStart: 2026-07-20 (the clean epoch — this is an adjudication of an existing cohort, so its evidence window opens at the epoch, not at registration)
preregistered.parent: crypto asset class on the signal board
preregistered.rule: CRYPTO COHORT KILL-TEST. Does the crypto cohort of the signal board clear its costs at all? Adjudicate at >=15 clean-epoch sessions AND >=150 crypto signal settles: if the day-clustered mean R of crypto signal trades is negative with t <= -1.5, crypto is DEMOTED from the signal board — tickets still generate and settle as a tagged shadow class (evidence keeps accruing), but they stop counting toward the book, stop consuming attention, and stop bleeding the headline P&L.
preregistered.mechanism: Not an edge claim — a risk decision, which is why the demotion bar is t<=-1.5 rather than 2.0: the null prior for this board is zero edge, crypto pays wider effective spreads and trades 24/7 against the board's daily cadence, and the cohort has been the recurring donor (microscopic-stop defect class, -$1,784 on 2026-07-30, 15% win that day; clean-epoch signal cohort -0.0133R/trade so far). Removing a cohort that cannot clear costs requires less evidence than adding one that claims edge.

threshold.reinstate: same bar inverted: a demoted crypto cohort returns only if its SHADOW record posts day-clustered t>=+2.0 over >=20 sessions — harder to come back than to leave, deliberately.
threshold.note: whichever of minSessions/minSettles lands later governs. No peeking adjustments; the first read is the read.

currentState.note: HYPOTHESIS-GENERATING as of registration: ~111 clean-epoch crypto signal settles at -0.0133R/trade (not yet day-clustered), ~9 sessions. First formal read expected ~2026-08-07.

knownWeaknesses: Crypto trades weekends; the board does not — the cohort is structurally handicapped by the cadence, and demotion would partly punish the CADENCE not the class. The demotion text therefore removes the class FROM THIS BOARD, and claims nothing about crypto tradeability elsewhere.
btcCorr20 regime (currently -0.64, decoupled) may make this cohort's next 15 sessions unrepresentative of the next year. The reinstatement path exists for exactly that reason.

preregistered.rule: POWER-LAW RIDER — a paper sleeve that buys announced turns in crash survivors and exits only on trend break. ENTRY (all three, mechanical): (1) CRASH SURVIVOR — the name traded at least 50% below its trailing 3-year high at some point in the last 18 months; (2) ANNOUNCED TURN — an R8-settled earnings gap of >= +8% raw (the NVDA-May-2023 / MU-HBM signature: the market repricing the business, in public); (3) NOT ALREADY BROKEN — entry close above its own 50-day MA. Enter at the post-gap close, fixed $1,000 notional per position, max 12 concurrent. EXIT: close below the 200-day MA, nothing else — no profit target, no time stop. A target is how a 12x becomes a +30% trade.
preregistered.mechanism: Bessembinder: ~4% of stocks produce all net equity wealth — returns are a power law, so capturing tails matters more than win rate. The MU/PLTR/NVDA/NFLX anatomy is identical ex-ante: brutal drawdown, then a structural demand shock ANNOUNCED via an earnings inflection, then quarters of persistence. Each leg is separately documented (post-crash winners, PEAD at long horizon, 52-week-high/trend persistence). The sleeve does not predict the turn; it recognizes the announcement and holds through the noise that shakes everyone else out.

threshold.grading: judged on TOTAL sleeve return, skew, and max drawdown vs SPY at >=20 closed positions or 4 quarters, whichever later. EXPECTED hit rate ~25-40% — a LOW hit rate with intact tails is the design working; killing it for win rate would be killing it for succeeding.
threshold.kill: retired if sleeve total return trails SPY by >20 points at >=20 closed positions AND no open position holds >2x — i.e., the tails never showed.
threshold.sizing: $1,000 notional, equal, max 12 open. No pyramiding registered; adding on strength would be R12.

knownWeaknesses: Backtest temptation refused: our price universe is TODAY'S listings, so any historical test of 'buy crashed names' on it is survivorship-poisoned by construction (the crashed names that died aren't in it). This sleeve is FORWARD-ONLY paper; slower, but the number it produces will be real.
Entry depends on R8 gap coverage — a turn announced by a name outside the calendar feed is missed and logged, not backfilled.
200d-MA exits give back 20-30% from peaks by design; the giveback is the price of never selling a 12x at +40%.
Theme-shock eras (2023-2026 AI) may be historically unusual; the sleeve's record will span whatever regime it gets.

preregistered.rule: DISCLOSED LEGAL EXPOSURE AS A FORWARD-RETURN SIGNAL. Event = a company's FIRST appearance in EDGAR full-text carrying a weight-3 legal trigger ('civil investigative demand', 'Wells notice', 'deferred prosecution agreement', quantified probable-loss accrual) in 10-Q/10-K/8-K. ENTRY = close of the first trading day STRICTLY AFTER the filing date (filings often land after the bell; this is the no-look-ahead convention). This is PUBLIC information — a filed disclosure is visible to everyone. The claim is coverage at whole-market scale, not speed. If the effect exists it is an under-reading edge, and those decay when crowded.
preregistered.status: NOT-ESTABLISHED (corrected 2026-08-03, same day). The initial 'clears the bar' claim was WRONG and is retracted. Direction is consistent with the hypothesis (9 of 13 quarters negative) but 3 years of history yields only ~13 independent 63-day periods, which cannot resolve an effect this size. correction.what: I reported this as the first result in 58 tests to clear a pre-registered bar, then ran the overlap kill-test I had myself listed as the top open issue, and it failed. Retracted within the hour.
correction.why: Day-clustering corrects for events sharing a DAY. It does nothing about events sharing a HOLDING WINDOW: two 63-day holds beginning a day apart have 62 of 63 days in common. Across 2023-2025 there are only ~13 genuinely independent 63-day periods, so the 323 'observations' were about 25x over-counted and the standard error was understated by roughly sqrt(25).
correction.lesson: Day-clustering is NOT sufficient for overlapping-horizon studies. Any future test holding positions longer than its event spacing must report the non-overlapping block t as the headline number, not the day-clustered one. This applies to R8 PEAD, R11 and the 13F clones — all use multi-week horizons with clustered events.

whatWouldSettleIt: MORE INDEPENDENT PERIODS, which is the binding constraint and is purely a crawling problem: EDGAR full-text covers 2001+, so walking back to ~2010 would give ~60 quarterly blocks instead of 13. At the observed -3.26% per quarter and 3.4pp dispersion, ~45 blocks would be needed for t <= -2. This is the single highest-value next step.
A shorter horizon buys independence cheaply but the effect looked weaker there (21d was -1.92%, t -1.94 day-clustered, i.e. worse before any overlap correction).
Forward validation remains the only thing that could make it fundable regardless of how the history reads.

openIssues: OVERLAPPING WINDOWS — the biggest remaining statistical problem, and it inflates the t. 63-day holds from events one day apart share 62 of 63 days; across ~3 years there are only ~12 non-overlapping 63-day periods. preregistered.origin: Operator: 'we should catch the news early and capitalize on the movements even if shorter timed trades.' Measurement that motivated it: on 2026-08-03 every headline behind the day's big movers was published PRE-MARKET (04:33-08:42 ET) while the moves happened AFTER the open (09:30-09:50). Corning's Truist upgrade hit the wire at 05:30; the stock opened already repriced at 134.78 and still ran to 146.18 intraday. The information was public hours early and the continuation was available for the whole session.
preregistered.rule: PRE-MARKET NEWS → INTRADAY DRIFT. Event = a symbol with at least one news article timestamped between 04:00 and 09:25 ET on a trading day AND an opening gap of >= +2% vs the prior close. ENTRY = that day's OPEN. EXIT = the same day's CLOSE. No overnight hold. Measured market-relative: (stock open->close) minus (SPY open->close) on the same session.
preregistered.hypothesis: POSITIVE same-day excess return, direction fixed before running. Mechanism: pre-market news is absorbed by a thin pre-open book; the regular session brings the participants who move size, so a catalyst-driven repricing continues after the open rather than completing at it. This is the ONLY reading consistent with the 2026-08-03 tape, but n=1 day is an anecdote and not evidence.
preregistered.whyThisHorizon: STATISTICAL POWER, and it is the whole point. R12 died because 63-day holds overlap: 3 years of history yielded only ~13 independent periods. A same-day hold does not overlap the next session, so each trading day is one independent observation and ~2.5 years gives ~640. This is the first test in the project designed so the sample can actually settle the question.

bar.why: Uses the SEARCHED-RESULT bar from significanceBar, not the pre-registered 2.0. This hypothesis was chosen after looking at one day's movers, which is a search, and it sits on top of 58 prior tests.
bar.clustering: one observation per TRADING DAY (mean excess across that day's qualifying names). Never per-event — a day with 40 gappers is one market, not 40 independent draws.
bar.costHurdle: an intraday round trip pays the spread TWICE. Test #45 measured 10bps/side as the working assumption, so the effect must exceed ~0.20pp per trade NET before it means anything. Gross results are to be reported alongside net and neither alone.
bar.kill: if the net-of-cost mean is <= 0 or |t| < 3.5, R13 is DEAD and no intraday execution loop gets built. The cheap test comes first precisely so the expensive machinery is never built on a guess.

knownWeaknesses: THIS IS THE MOST CROWDED PATTERN IN RETAIL TRADING. 'Gap and go' on news is what every day-trading course sells. Prior expectation should be that it is arbitraged to zero net of costs, and the registered direction may simply be wrong.

Costs dominate at this horizon and are worst exactly where gaps are biggest (small, illiquid names). The 10bps/side assumption is a placeholder; a surviving result must be re-run against real quotes, which needs SIP data (#39).
Selection: conditioning on a >= +2% gap is a price filter chosen without testing alternatives. It is fixed in advance and may NOT be re-tuned; a different threshold is R14.
Alpaca's news feed is one vendor. Coverage gaps bias toward the null (missed events are simply absent), but vendor-specific tagging could correlate with liquidity.

Execution reality: TRAIDS currently scans once at 09:35 and has no intraday loop. Even a positive result requires building one, and the fill assumptions at the OPEN are the least reliable part of the pipeline (see the 2026-07-23 stale-open-print incident).
preregistered.status: STAGNANT (measured 2026-08-03, same day as registration). The registered direction was POSITIVE; the measurement is significantly NEGATIVE. preregistered.parent: test #61 (option-income ETFs) + the open #41/#42/#43 VRP-harvestability thread
preregistered.origin: Operator: mimic the option-income ETFs' options trading inside TRAIDS, rather than proxying it via their beta. Test #61 measured what their overlay contributes above a beta-matched index position: mean +1.37%/yr (QYLD -1.02, JEPI +0.91, JEPQ +1.63, SPYI +3.78, SPYT +1.58). That is the bar a replication has to clear.
preregistered.rule: REPLICATE THE QYLD RULE ON REAL CONTRACTS, AS A KNOWN-ANSWER TEST. Hold the index. Each month, sell the listed at-the-money call on the index nearest 30 days to expiry. Hold to expiry, settle intrinsic, re-strike. No discretion, no strike shopping, no rolling. QYLD is chosen deliberately over the others because its rule is the most mechanical and least discretionary of the five, so it is the only one that can be replicated without guessing at a manager's judgement.
preregistered.whyKnownAnswer: QYLD's actual live total return is 9.65% CAGR over 6.0 years against QQQ's 18.40% (measured in #61). That is a PUBLISHED ANSWER our replication must reproduce. This inverts the usual problem: we are not trying to discover whether covered calls work, we are testing whether OUR OPTIONS PIPELINE CAN REPRODUCE A KNOWN RESULT. If the replication materially beats QYLD's real record, the excess is our own optimism, quantified — most likely in fill assumptions — and that number is worth more than any strategy result.
preregistered.theKnownFlawWeAreMeasuring: Alpaca historical option data gives contract BARS (OHLC), not bid/ask. Pricing entries at a bar close assumes the print was executable, which is precisely the error the external panel identified in R13 ('treating bar prints as executable fills without auction participation'). We cannot fix that without a chain feed (task #48 Schwab OAuth, or #39 paid data). So this test is DESIGNED to measure that error rather than pretend it away: replication-minus-QYLD is an estimate of our fill optimism on index options.

bar.primaryOutput: replication CAGR minus QYLD's actual 9.65% CAGR over the same window
bar.interpretation: within +/-1.0%/yr => our options pipeline reproduces a real fund's record and can be trusted for index-option work. Above +1.0%/yr => our fills are optimistic by that margin and every prior options result (#45, #58, #59, #60) is overstated by roughly the same mechanism. Below -1.0%/yr => the replication is missing something the fund does (securities lending income, ELN structuring, an active strike rule) and the gap should be attributed before anything is concluded.
bar.secondary: only if the replication tracks within +/-1.0%/yr may we then ask whether a modified overlay beats +1.37%/yr of contribution, which is the actual investment question.
bar.kill: if replication error exceeds +/-2%/yr the pipeline is not fit for index-option research and the VRP thread stays closed until a real chain feed exists. No further VRP tests get built on bar-close pricing.

knownWeaknesses: QYLD writes on NDX and we would replicate on QQQ or SPY options; index-vs-ETF option differences (settlement style, dividend treatment, 1256 tax status) introduce error unrelated to fills. State the substitution and do not attribute all error to execution.
QYLD's real NAV includes fund expenses of ~0.60%/yr and any securities-lending income. Both must be adjusted for before the comparison means anything.

6 years of QYLD history contains no 2008 and one brief 2020 shock. A replication that tracks over this window says nothing about behaviour in a real crash, which is exactly when a call-overwrite strategy stops being income and starts being a short-vol position.
The 1256 tax treatment that motivates SPYI is a TAX advantage, not an edge. It cannot appear in a pre-tax return comparison and must never be counted as alpha.

EXPECTED OUTCOME ON THE RECORD: I expect the replication to BEAT QYLD's real record, because bar-close pricing ignores the spread we would actually cross. If it does, that is not a discovery of edge — it is the measurement this test was built to produce.
preregistered.status: MEASURED 2026-08-03 — PASS. The options pipeline reproduces a real fund record within 1%/yr.

result.substitution: XYLD (Global X S&P 500 covered call) replaced QYLD: SPXW contracts are retrievable on this key, NDX options are not. Same issuer, same mechanical rule, different index. Declared before running.
result.verdict: PASS — replication 13.52% vs XYLD actual 14.05%, error -0.53%/yr, inside the +/-1.0%/yr band fixed in advance. Our index-option data path and settlement logic reproduce a live fund with a mechanical rule. That validates the DATA PATH used by tests #45/#58/#59/#60 — it does not validate their conclusions.
result.myPredictionWasWrong: I wrote on the record that I expected the replication to BEAT XYLD because bar-close pricing ignores the spread we would cross. It came in 0.53%/yr BELOW, and roughly 1.13%/yr below once XYLD 0.60% expense ratio is added back. So bar-close pricing did NOT produce the optimism I predicted at monthly frequency. Plausible reasons the replication trails: XYLD may write slightly out-of-the-money rather than exactly at-the-money, it earns securities-lending income we do not model, and 4 of 31 cycles went unpriced. The prediction being wrong is recorded because a pre-registered expectation only means something if a miss is reported.
result.firstRunWasABug: The first execution returned 22.75% — BEATING SPY buy-and-hold at 21.54%. That is structurally impossible for a covered call in a rising market, and the impossibility is what exposed the defect: I used adjustment=all SPY x10 as the index for BOTH the equity leg and the option strike/settlement. That is a TOTAL-RETURN series, but SPXW settles on the SPX PRICE index, so ~1.3%/yr of dividends leaked into the strategy return without ever being surrendered to the call. Fixed by striking and settling on the real SPX price index while holding SPY total return. A permanent structural sanity check now fires if the replication ever exceeds buy-and-hold.
result.economicsOfTheStrategy: Replication 13.52% vs SPY buy-and-hold 21.54% over the same 2.5 years: the overwrite gave up ~8pp/yr of upside to collect premium in a strong bull market. That is the cost of the strategy, not a defect in it, and it matches the -5.47%/yr outright gap measured across all five funds in test #61.

costCorrection.prompt: Operator: "thats a ridiculous question whether its worth building; we talked about schwab charging $0.65 per trade". Correct, and the objection I raised was hand-waving rather than arithmetic.
costCorrection.myError: I carried an EQUITY-BOARD cost intuition onto an instrument where it does not apply. On the equity board we trade ~$20k positions and pay ~10bps/side ON NOTIONAL every round trip, roughly 250 round trips a year, so costs dominate and swamp any edge. Selling an index option is structurally different: you TRANSACT only the premium but are EXPOSED on the notional. So the bid/ask, measured as a percentage of the notional the strategy actually earns on, is roughly two orders of magnitude smaller. At 12 writes a year on a $612k contract the whole cost stack is 0.10-0.59%/yr against a 1.37%/yr prize.
costCorrection.empiricalBound: Independently corroborated by R15 itself: the replication priced fills at bar CLOSES with NO spread modelled at all, and still came in 0.53%/yr BELOW a real fund. Had bar-close pricing been materially optimistic we would have BEATEN XYLD. We did not, which bounds the true fill degradation small.
costCorrection.consequence: The VRP thread should NOT have been characterised as cost-killed. Tests #41/#42/#43 came back NOT-ESTABLISHED for want of chain data and a measurement, not because the arithmetic fails. It does not fail. Task #42 (VRP paper sleeve) is no longer gated on the cost question — only on wiring the sleeve.
costCorrection.RETRACTED: See registry.costRetraction (2026-08-03). The 0.20%/yr all-in cost figure used throughout this block was INVENTED, not measured, and the net 0.78-1.17%/yr conclusion drawn from it is WITHDRAWN. The commission arithmetic (/usr/bin/bash.65/contract = 0.0013% of notional) stands and was the operator's point; the spread half of the stack is unknown and remains unknown.

The exploratory reading that prompted this registration (+0.1534R high-minus-low, t 2.54 over 9 paired sessions) is an ARTIFACT and must not be cited. It was computed over ALL closed rows, where newsScore is 85% zeros, so p33 = p67 = 0 and the split (>= hi) / (<= lo) produced buckets of 998 and 900 rows OVERLAPPING BY 873. It compared two nearly identical sets. There is no prior evidence for this hypothesis; the direction below is a stated prior, not a measurement.

bar.metric: rMult, high-tercile minus low-tercile newsScore, PAIRED WITHIN SESSION, clustered on sessions never on trades
bar.why: A single named observer with the direction fixed in advance legitimately uses 2.0 per significanceBar. The 2.54 above used 5 observers at once and does not count as the test.
bar.decisionRule: Adopt news weighting ONLY at >=25 paired sessions AND t >= 2.0 in the POSITIVE direction. A negative or flat result kills it. Re-tuning the observer, the tercile cut, or the direction after seeing more evidence voids this registration.
bar.mustAssert: Before any statistic is computed the two buckets MUST be verified DISJOINT and the tercile boundaries must satisfy p67 > p33 strictly. This assertion is now enforced in backend/adjudicator.js. Its absence is what allowed the withdrawn figure to be reported at all.

knownWeaknesses: COVERAGE IS THE REAL CONSTRAINT: newsScore is 0.000 on ~85% of all rows and 31% even of settled rows. A zero currently conflates 'no headlines found' with 'headlines were balanced', which are different states and must not share a value. Until absence is recorded as null, every split on this observer is measuring coverage as much as sentiment.

The sibling observers polNews, polSent, econNews and econSent are fully DEGENERATE and produce zero pairable sessions (measured 2026-08-06 by backend/observer-independence.js). They are excluded from this test.
News arrives DURING a session. If newsScore is stamped at settle rather than at entry it is partly hindsight. Verify the stamp time before reading the bar.
At 5 of 25 paired sessions this is early. The withdrawn figure is a reminder that an encouraging number from a broken split is worse than no number.
preregistered.status: ACTIVE — the motivating figure is withdrawn, the test stands with a disjointness assertion added.
preregistered.retraction: The exploratory reading that motivated this registration (+0.1534R high-minus-low, t 2.54 over 9 paired sessions) is an ARTIFACT and is withdrawn. newsScore is DEGENERATE: 85% of its values are exactly 0.000, so the 33rd percentile, the median and the 67th percentile are all 0. The tercile split therefore assigned every zero-valued ticket to BOTH buckets (high = value >= 0, low = value <= 0), producing buckets of 596 and 545 rows out of 618 — overlapping almost completely. The measured gap was not high-news minus low-news; it was two nearly identical sets differing only in a handful of non-zero tails. Found 2026-08-06 by backend/observer-independence.js, written to fix D16, which flagged newsScore as degenerate and prompted a direct check.
preregistered.whatWouldMakeItTestable: Three things, in order. (1) COVERAGE: 85% zeros means the per-symbol news fetch returns nothing scoreable for most tickets — establish whether that is missing headlines or a headline scorer too coarse to register anything, because those have different fixes. (2) ABSENCE MUST NOT EQUAL NEUTRAL: a ticket with no headlines and a ticket with balanced headlines must not both record 0.000; absence has to be null so it is excluded rather than pooled into both tails. (3) SPLIT ON NON-DEGENERATE VALUES ONLY, with the bucket rule asserting the two sets are disjoint before any statistic is computed. Until all three hold, no news-weighting test is measurable on this ledger.
preregistered.lesson: The tercile helper never checked that its buckets were disjoint. A split defined as (>= hi) and (<= lo) is only a partition when hi > lo; when they collapse it silently becomes two overlapping supersets and every gap it reports is noise on the tails. Any future bucketed test must assert disjointness and minimum bucket separation BEFORE reporting a statistic.
preregistered.correctionOfTheCorrection: The first draft of this retraction killed the whole test. That was wrong and is itself corrected here. On the subset the bar actually specifies — SETTLED, non-control rows — the terciles are NOT degenerate (n=117, p33 0.000, p67 0.292, buckets 39 and 51, overlap ZERO) and 5 paired sessions already qualify. The observer is usable where the test reads it; it is unusable over the whole ledger because unsettled and control rows are dominated by zeros.

preregistered.origin: Operator: 'predict the run, daily market, daily news trend; should be easy to see' and 'look at the market as a whole and then dissect'. That is a falsifiable claim and cheap to test, so it gets a forecast log rather than a debate.
preregistered.rule: backend/daily-forecast.js records a mechanical UP/DOWN/FLAT call on SPY for the next session BEFORE the outcome, from real SPY bars, real sector-ETF breadth (9 sectors), and real CNBC + Yahoo + Finnhub headline counts. Graded the following session against the actual SPY move.
preregistered.hypothesis: The operator's claim is that the run is readable in advance. Registered NEUTRAL on purpose: I am not calling the direction of this result, because the honest prior on daily index direction from public inputs is that it is not predictable. The log settles it.

bar.metric: hit rate of the recorded call vs the actual next-session SPY direction
bar.why: Binomial z against the base rate. NOT against 50% — SPY is up on most days in most samples, so beating a coin flip is not the achievement. The benchmark is the up-day base rate in the SAME window.
bar.decisionRule: Adopt only at >=20 graded calls AND z >= 2.0 against the in-window up-day base rate. FLAT calls score as misses so the rule cannot buy accuracy by abstaining.

knownWeaknesses: The call rule is mechanical and simple by design so it cannot be revised after seeing outcomes. A discretionary forecast would not be gradeable.
War and political headline density is treated as a RISK damper, never as a direction. Which way geopolitics resolves is not predictable from a headline count.
20 calls is one month. Enough to catch a large effect, not a small one.
Hindsight is the thing this defends against: the days that look obvious afterwards are the ones that get remembered, and the ambiguous ones vanish. A written log has no such memory.

preregistered.origin: Measured 2026-08-11: the best 20 overnight sessions of the last 5 years carried 101% of ALL overnight gains, and 2 of the top 7 spanned scheduled CPI mornings. Direction of a macro print is unknowable; its DATE is published months in advance. So the predictable object is the NIGHT, not the direction — this is scheduling, not timing, and it is the operator's 'predicting those days' thesis in its testable form.
preregistered.rule: Overnights (close -> next open, SPY) that SPAN a scheduled US macro release morning (CPI, FOMC decision, PCE, NFP — official published calendars only, recorded before the night) vs all other overnights.
preregistered.hypothesis: POSITIVE, fixed in advance: scheduled-print overnights carry a larger mean overnight return than ordinary overnights. Mechanism: overnight risk premium is compensation for holding through information arrival, and these are the nights information arrives on schedule.

bar.metric: mean overnight return, scheduled-print nights minus ordinary nights; nights are naturally non-overlapping units
bar.why: single pre-registered comparison with a stated mechanism -> 2.0 per significanceBar. Historical read is legitimate here because the conditioning variable (release date) is exogenous and published in advance - no selection on outcomes is possible.
bar.decisionRule: If cleared: exposure stays R14-standard every night, SIZED UP modestly and systematically on scheduled-print nights only. Never leveraged conviction - the worst nights cluster in the same regimes as the best.

preregistered.dataNeeded: Official historical release calendars (BLS for CPI/NFP, Fed for FOMC, BEA for PCE). Dates must come from the publishing agencies, never reconstructed from memory or news archives - a wrong date list would grade the wrong nights.

preregistered.parent: R39 intraday family (signals) · intraday-history.js (two-year rows with signal-time features) · intraday-model.js (walk-forward) · lib/gbm.js
preregistered.origin: Operator 2026-08-23: 'need to channel our inner medallion' / 'go'. The Medallion shape is one model over many weak signals, tested out of sample, rather than one rule at a time earning its own bar. R41 is that shape on the intraday horizon: the forecast is the strategy. Registered BEFORE the two-year walk-forward result was seen (the backfill was 3% complete at registration).
preregistered.rule: Learners: the shop's GBM (60 rounds, depth 2) and ridge (lambda 50, clamp 2R) from lib/gbm.js, trained on R39 signal rows (ORB30 + VWAPR) with nine signal-time features (sigMin, dir, mag, symRetToSig, spyRetToSig, spyRet25m, gapPct, prevRet, sigBarRangePct) + variant flag; target = realized R net of the cost model's equity spread. HISTORY: monthly walk-forward, purged one session, first 4 months train-only, train capped at the most recent 150k rows. FORWARD: the model fit on all rows before session s scores session s's signals the night they are graded (never before), and the policy 'take forecast > 0' is recorded alongside the baseline 'take every signal' and 'top decile per day'.
preregistered.hypothesis: NEUTRAL. The features are cheap and public; the rules they condition lose on early history. Direction fixed: the forecast>0 policy must BEAT the baseline (mean daily R higher) AND be positive in its own right.

bar.history: IN-SAMPLE EXPLORATION (never a verdict): reported for both learners — OOS Spearman(forecast, R), and for each policy mean daily R with day-clustered t over OOS sessions, split by half-year. A 'promising' history read = forecast>0 policy mean daily R > 0 with t >= 2.0 over >= 12 OOS months AND positive in every half-year present, for at least one learner. Anything else = the model orders trades no better than chance on this horizon.
bar.forward: VERDICT from forward sessions >= 2026-08-25 only: policy 'forecast > 0' mean daily R > 0 with session-clustered t >= the best-of-2 null bar (two learners) at >= 30 sessions and >= 200 taken trades, AND higher mean daily R than the baseline over the same sessions. Interim kill-only at 16 sessions (t <= -2.0).
bar.decisionRule: Forward CLEARED -> proposal for an intraday paper sleeve that trades the forecast, with its own registered sizing; never auto-funded. Forward DID NOT PASS / KILLED -> the combined model is closed on this horizon; history promise, if any, is recorded as what it was: in-sample.

preregistered.priorSample: NONE at registration. The two-year history read arrives after this entry and is labelled in-sample wherever it is printed.
preregistered.knownWeaknesses: survivorship in the history roster (today's top 1,200 applied to the past); IEX bars; nine hand-chosen features — no feature search, so no multiple-comparison correction is owed beyond the two-learner null bar; a fixed 'forecast > 0' threshold chosen before any result; one fit per month on history vs one fit per session forward (forward is strictly more data, never less).

Every feature this shop trades on comes from price, volume, or a structured filing field; the 8,000-12,000 words of an earnings call have never been read at roster scale because reading them was priced out. 300 roster prints sit on the calendar through 2026-11-20 at roughly $14 of input tokens.

A reply missing a field or out of range is REFUSED, never coerced. Entry = the first FINAL close strictly after the call date; graded at +5 and +20 sessions close-to-close, excess vs SPY, net of the cost model's equity round trip. Model id and raw reply stamped on every row.

bar.tRequired: best-of-5 null bar from lib/null-bar.js (five scores are looked at)

PRICE BASELINE: the earnings gap and 5-day post-call momentum — what the tape already knew before any text was read

preregistered.name: Whale-overlap COMPANION — does filer-cluster weighting beat name-equal weighting on a fixed overlap rule?
preregistered.parent: #70 (whale-consensus-cohort, sealed 2026-08-19, accruing to 2026-12-31). R48 is a COMPANION, not a replacement: same overlap rule, same benchmark, ONE difference — the weighting.
preregistered.origin: The operator asked for the best-allocated sleeve buildable from overlapping institutional positions. That mechanism IS #70, and #70 is sealed, so its weights cannot be changed. The only legitimate question left is whether the weighting inside a fixed methodology can be improved — a construction question, not a new signal. Registering a fresh whale sleeve on the same universe with a different parameterisation is how tests #41-#43 all died.
preregistered.rule: Universe and filer panel from RAW EDGAR 13F-HR originals only, quarter t, CIK-resolved programmatically via the existing best-ideas-13f.js resolveCik/filingsOf pipeline. The pasted aggregator behind #70 is NOT reusable: it is documented in-file as forensically broken (Appaloosa shown at $765B, roughly 40x real AUM; puts counted as buyers; quarters mixed). OVERLAP THRESHOLD UNCHANGED from #70: retain names with >=2 fresh adds (NEW or +25%) AND adds >= 2x fresh sells. WEIGHTING is the single variable under test: two-stage cluster-equal-weight — stage 1 equal weight across FILER-OVERLAP clusters, stage 2 equal weight by name within cluster, with any one sector ETF capped at 25% of absolute gross. FORMATION at the first completed close on/after the latest qualifying filing date, forming-bar guard enforced. REBALANCE only at each quarterly filing window, never faster than the disclosure refreshes. A name is dropped at the NEXT formation if it stops qualifying, never intra-quarter, which would use undisclosed information.
preregistered.statistic: Mean excess return over each name's OWN SECTOR ETF, computed PER FILER-CLUSTER (primary). Per-name figures are context only and are never the verdict. SPY is carried as context, never as the benchmark.

bar.tRequired: nullBar({variants:<clusters actually tested>, n:<cluster-quarters>}).p95 — the cluster DEFINITION was chosen post-hoc from #70, so it counts as a search and is charged for
bar.costs: 10bps x measured turnover per rebalance, matching best-ideas-13f.js so the two constructs stay comparable
bar.decisionRule: CLEARS -> cluster weighting becomes a proposed amendment to the SUCCESSOR of #70, never an edit to #70 itself. DOES NOT PASS -> name-equal weighting was adequate and the concentration was cosmetic.
bar.controlDesign: MATCHED CONTROL, not a random draw. Each cohort name is paired with control names drawn from the same SECTOR and the same LIQUIDITY DECILE of the universe, and where computable a similar market-cap band — so the comparison isolates 'these filers chose it' from 'it is a large, liquid, surviving US name'. Added 2026-08-25 before any evidence.
bar.whyMatched: A random-draw control run on 2026-08-25 put the cohort's 5-year return at the 59th percentile against 500 random 12-name baskets. That was reported as a null and SHOULD NOT HAVE BEEN: the control's own dispersion ran p05 +28% to p95 +240%, so on twelve names over a single path it had essentially no power to detect a real effect in either direction. It was uninformative, not negative. A matched control removes most of that dispersion by construction and is the only version of this comparison worth running. The earlier random-draw figure is retained as a disclosed motivating sample with weight zero and must never be cited as evidence that 13F consensus does not work.

preregistered.knownWeaknesses: 13F is stale by construction: 45 days is the mandated floor and the cohorts on disk are 45 and 114 days stale. It omits shorts entirely, reports options inconsistently (long common only, discarded), and is blind to non-US filers. Crowding cuts both ways — the same overlap that reads as conviction also concentrates the exit — so the SIGN of the effect is an open question, not an assumption. #70's filer panel is survivorship-selected by an unknown rule; R48 rebuilds from raw EDGAR precisely to remove that. Effective N is brutal and is the reason this test exists: #70's twelve names carry an effective N near 3 once filer overlap is counted (RenTech on 9 of 12, Bridgewater on 9 of 12, both jointly on 7 of 12, HHI 0.403), and sector diversification does NOT fix it because the RenTech-linked names span 4 of the 6 sector ETFs. At name-equal weighting the two filers jointly carry 58.3% of absolute gross R. The matched control cannot remove the whole confound: filers select on characteristics we cannot fully observe or match, so a surviving difference is still 'consensus plus whatever they see that we do not', not clean selection skill.

preregistered.name: Stop-width twin — is the stop mispriced against the spread it has to clear?
preregistered.origin: Cost in R is round-trip spread divided by stop distance, so a tighter stop mechanically multiplies cost in R without changing anything about the signal. The board's equity stop runs 4.61% of price and crypto 6.36%, against a measured round-trip spread of 0.2304% — giving a per-row cost of 0.072R on equity where gross edge is approximately zero. The question is whether the stop is set where it is for a reason or by inheritance.
preregistered.rule: A paper TWIN of every Trend, Mean-Reversion and Ensemble signal in EQUITY and CRYPTO only, entered on or after 2026-08-26, identical in symbol, direction, entry and timing, with ONE difference: the ATR-based stop distance is multiplied by 1.5x and the position is sized DOWN so that dollar risk is held constant. FX and Futures are excluded because their gross edge is already negative (-0.0607R and -0.1136R) and, as cost-sensitivity.json states, a conclusion already negative gross of costs cannot be reversed by any cost assumption.
preregistered.statistic: PAIRED D = net-of-cost R(1.5x twin) - net-of-cost R(live 1.0x stop), one D per matched signal, costed per-row from each ticket's OWN obs.spreadBps, with EPISODE-level day-clustered t.

bar.why: ONE fixed multiplier is registered, not a swept range. A sweep over 1.25x/1.5x/2x/3x would be a search this book cannot currently afford to pay for — the honest bar would rise faster than the effect.
bar.decisionRule: CLEARS -> a proposed stop-width amendment for the successor spec, never an edit to a live sleeve mid-flight. DOES NOT PASS -> the stop is not the lever and the cost problem must be attacked at the spread, not the denominator.

preregistered.knownWeaknesses: A wider stop changes the trade, not only its cost: it converts some stop-outs into holds, which shifts the return distribution as well as the cost denominator, and the paired D therefore measures both effects together and cannot separate them. Arithmetic already bounds the upside — to zero out cost on equity the stop would have to widen from 4.6% to about 31% of price, so a 1.5x multiplier can only shrink the leak by roughly a third, not close it. This is registered as a measurable lever on the SIZE of the leak, explicitly not as a fix for the SIGN of the edge.

read.statistic: paired D net-of-cost R(1.5x twin) - R(live 1.0x stop): mean +0.03946R/episode, episode-level day-clustered t 1.525, 95 episodes / 15 sessions (155 costed twins, 46 uncosted excluded per the registration, 3.9% unresolved; crypto carries no spread stamp, so the read population is effectively the equity signals); origin -0.0856R vs twin -0.0452R net

preregistered.name: Gap exposure — flat at the session close vs held overnight
preregistered.origin: Today's PYPL loss (-4.16R on a book capped at 0.5R, a -13.57% overnight gap) prompted the question. The motivating retrospective is disclosed in the script header and is WEIGHTLESS.
preregistered.multiplicityFamily: gap-exposure-2026-08 — single variant. The rule was not searched: 'flat at the session close' is the one obvious form of the hypothesis and no threshold was tuned.
preregistered.rule: FROZEN 2026-08-28. For every non-sleeve, non-control, non-shadow ticket whose ET entry day differs from its ET exit day, compute a twin that exits at the CLOSE of the session it was opened in, priced from the daily bar for that symbol and date (Alpaca stocks bars for Equity, Alpaca crypto bars for Crypto). Twin R = (sessionClose - entry) * dir / stopDist. D = twinR - actualR. A ticket whose session close cannot be obtained is DROPPED AND COUNTED, never interpolated. Futures, FX and Options are OUT OF SCOPE in v1 and counted as not covered.
preregistered.statistic: Mean D per OVERNIGHT EPISODE, where an episode is one ET entry date. One-sample t on the per-episode mean. CLUSTERING UNIT = OVERNIGHT EPISODES, never tickets — the motivating sample's 15 tickets were only about 5 episodes, and that is the whole reason this entry exists rather than a wired rule.

bar.source: backend/lib/null-bar.js nullBar({variants:1, n:20, trials:20000}) computed 2026-08-28 before evidence
bar.unit: overnight episodes — matches the clustering unit of the statistic

preregistered.interimKill: Kill-only at 10 episodes: if mean D is negative with t <= -1.0, the hypothesis is DEAD and overnight exposure is not revisited on this evidence.

decisionRule.pass: t >= 1.732 at 20 episodes: flat-at-close beats holding, and a registered enforcement gate may be SPECIFIED — not wired. Wiring is a separate operator decision.
decisionRule.fail: t < 1.732 at 20 episodes: DID NOT PASS. Overnight exposure is not shown to be costly on this population and no gap rule is built. The gap-stop tail is then understood as a selected tail, not an actionable defect.

preregistered.readCondition: 20 overnight episodes from 2026-08-31.
knownWeaknesses: THE MOTIVATING NUMBER WAS AN ARTEFACT AND I ALMOST SHIPPED A RULE ON IT. Selecting tickets that resolved via gap-stop conditions on the outcome and guarantees a population of losses (-$16,078, 18 of 18). On the correct population — every overnight-held ticket — the preview reads mean D -0.0371R at t -0.359, i.e. flat-at-close is NOT better. This entry exists to settle that forward, not to rescue the original claim.

COVERAGE IS BAD IN v1: 89 of the covered pairs were dropped for a missing session close, and 162 tickets (FX 84, Futures 78) are out of scope entirely — including the ZC and 6E gap losses that motivated the question. A read on Equity and Crypto alone does not settle Futures or FX.
Overnight gains and overnight losses are both real. The twin forfeits favourable overnight moves as well as adverse ones, which is exactly why the paired form is the only honest test.
The session close is a real, knowable price, but a real flat-at-close order would cross a spread the twin does not charge. The twin is therefore slightly FLATTERED relative to a tradeable version.
Episodes are ET entry dates, so several tickets opened the same day share one episode. That is correct for clustering but means 20 episodes may take many more than 20 sessions to accrue.

preregistered.name: Gap-aware sizing twin — does a minimum overnight risk distance beat sizing off the stop?
preregistered.origin: Three demonstrations on 2026-08-28 that a stop does not bound an overnight loss: PYPL sized to risk $250 lost $1,038 (4.16R) on a 13.57% gap; the day's 41 signals were +$209 without it and -$829 with it; and across the clean era 18 gap-resolved tickets produced 18 losses, 0 gains, -$16,078 against a whole-book P&L of +$2,648. Retrospective in data/gap-sizing-retro.json, DISCLOSED AND WEIGHTLESS.
preregistered.parent: Distinct from R62. R62 asks whether to HOLD overnight at all (and its preview reads against the hypothesis). This asks, given that we do hold, whether the SIZE should be set against the risk actually carried rather than the stop.
preregistered.multiplicityFamily: gap-risk-2026-08 — FOUR configurations were examined (percentile 0.95/0.99 x class-floor multiple 1/2). The registered configuration is floor multiple 1, and the bar is a best-of-4 bar. Sibling: R62, same family of motivating observations, separate hypothesis and separate bar.
preregistered.rule: FROZEN 2026-08-28. For every non-sleeve, non-control, non-shadow ticket, compute both arms from the SAME entry, stop, exit and risk budget: (A) AS-TRADED, qty = riskDollars / stopDist; (B) GAP-AWARE, qty = riskDollars / max(stopDist, floorPct x entry) where floorPct is 3% for Equity, 5% for Crypto, 2% for Futures, 1% for FX and 0 for Options (defined risk — the debit is already the maximum loss). A ticket whose ET entry day equals its ET exit day carries no gap risk and is UNCHANGED in arm B. Per-ticket P&L in arm B is the as-traded P&L multiplied by stopDist / effectiveStopDist. Implemented in backend/lib/gap-aware-sizing.js with the percentile machinery retained but NOT load-bearing — see knownWeaknesses.
preregistered.statistic: Mean per-SESSION dollar difference, arm B minus arm A, summed within each ET session and then averaged across sessions. One-sample t on the per-session difference. CLUSTERING UNIT = SESSIONS. Tickets are never the unit: this is one book re-weighted, and every ticket in a session shares that session's tape.

bar.source: backend/lib/null-bar.js nullBar({variants:4, n:30, trials:20000}) computed 2026-08-28 before any forward session
bar.rule: day-clustered t >= 2.378 at 30 sessions. The prediction is POSITIVE — the gap-aware arm earns more dollars per session.
bar.unit: sessions — matches the clustering unit of the statistic
bar.note: The retrospective reached t 1.611 over 26 sessions, which is BELOW this bar. The forward test therefore has to do better than the sample that motivated it, which is the correct standard.

preregistered.interimKill: Kill-only at 15 sessions: if the mean per-session difference is NEGATIVE with t <= -1.0, the hypothesis is dead and no sizing change is built. No positive reading at 15 sessions adjudicates anything.

decisionRule.pass: At 30 sessions with t >= 2.378: a minimum overnight risk distance is ESTABLISHED as improving per-session dollars on this book. That authorises a SPECIFICATION and an operator decision to change live sizing — it does not change sizing by itself.
decisionRule.fail: At 30 sessions with t < 2.378: DID NOT PASS. Sizing stays as it is. No re-cut by floor percentage, percentile, class or horizon — those are new tests in a larger family, and the floor multiple in particular has already been searched.

preregistered.readCondition: 30 ET sessions with settled tickets from 2026-08-31.
knownWeaknesses: IT DOES NOT FIX THE CASE THAT MOTIVATED IT, AND THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT LINE HERE. PYPL's stop was 3.3% of price and its measured p95 adverse overnight gap was 3.0%, so the rule leaves it completely untouched and the same -13.57% gap still costs $1,038. Percentile-based sizing misses tails by construction. Only DEFINED RISK bounds a tail gap — which the same day demonstrated: XOM -$222, UEC -$81 and IWM -$42 all took full losses that could not exceed their debit. This test measures an ordinary-gap improvement, not a fix for the disaster.

THE PERCENTILE MACHINERY IS NOT LOAD-BEARING. p95 and p99 produced identical results, which means max(floor, measured) resolves to the FLOOR on essentially every ticket. The honest description of the registered rule is 'a class-level minimum risk distance for overnight holds', and the per-symbol gap distribution is decoration. It is retained in the code because removing it would be a rule change, but no claim rests on it.

THE PARAMETER SITS NEXT TO A CLIFF. At floor multiple 1 the retrospective nets +$2,607; at multiple 2 it nets -$3,233, giving up $24,067 of winners to save $20,835 of losers. A rule whose sign flips when its one parameter doubles is fragile, and that fragility is not something more sessions will resolve.

THE TWIN RESCALES THE SAME TICKETS, so it measures arithmetic rather than trading. It cannot capture second-order effects of trading smaller: different fills, different portfolio interaction, different circuit-breaker behaviour, or the different trades a smaller book would have been allowed to take.

The retrospective's +$2,607 is dominated by a handful of large tickets; 191 of 890 were resized at all. A per-session dollar statistic is sensitive to those, which is why the read is clustered on sessions and why the bar is above what the retrospective achieved.
Options are excluded by construction (floor 0). If the book's mix shifts toward options the test quietly loses sample, and that is not currently monitored.
preregistered.ipNote: None — this is the house's own book and its own risk mechanics.
