preregistered.name: News-conditioned refusal gate — do the tickets a low-newsScore veto would refuse actually lose?
preregistered.seat: news-trader — this is the seat's FIRST gradeable rule. It held escrowed authority from 2026-08-29 with no rule attached to it, so it could not accrue and could not unlock.
preregistered.script: backend/news-gate.js (population: new tickets carrying a finite obs.newsScore; graded from veto shadows)
preregistered.multiplicityFamily: news-gate-scan (12 news observation fields examined in backend/news-gate-scan.js on 2026-08-31; ONE registered)
preregistered.origin: MOTIVATED BY A SEARCH, AND SAID SO. backend/news-gate-scan.js scanned all 12 finite news observation fields on the canonical clean-era ledger (2,105 settled rows via lib/reconcile.js) for association with realised net rMult, day-clustered. Every number it produced is IN-SAMPLE and weightless. newsScore was chosen NOT because it was the strongest — it was not — but because it was the ONLY field whose two arms each span enough SESSIONS to be a per-ticket rule at all (25 bottom / 19 top). The apparently strongest result, polNews at t -4.27, spans FOUR sessions in its top arm: polNews is a market-level count that barely varies between tickets on the same day, so gating on it gates days, not tickets. econNews (8/9 sessions) and sectorNewsAvg (5/6) fail the same way.
preregistered.whyAGateAndNotADirectionalRULE: Every public news-trading source the operator supplied on 2026-08-31 (daytrading.com, chartmini.com) contained NO testable mechanic — no window, no threshold, no direction; chartmini explicitly refuses to claim either fade or follow. Meanwhile this house has already measured the two things they recommend. R20: overnights spanning scheduled macro releases (CPI/FOMC/PCE/NFP — their exact list) show +0.6bp at t 0.08, DID NOT PASS. R13: buying pre-market-news gappers loses -0.708pp net at t -5.86 over 290 independent days, robust to day-weighting (287 of 290 days carry n>=20; dropping the one thin day strengthens it to t -4.58). The FADE of R13 is not registered here because its entire margin sits inside an unmeasured cost assumption of 10bps/side — break-even is ~51bps round trip against 30.8bps measured on LIQUID names — and it is the short leg of gapping news names, the hardest borrow on the tape. A REFUSAL escapes all of it: it pays no spread, borrows nothing, crosses no market, and is graded on whether what it declined lost.
preregistered.rule: REFUSE (shadow only, never block) any new ticket whose obs.newsScore <= 0.
preregistered.definition: Threshold FIXED IN ADVANCE at 0, the measured p20 of newsScore over the 507 clean-era rows carrying it. It is an absolute constant, never a rolling quantile — a threshold recomputed each session would drift with the population and could not be falsified. Tickets with no finite newsScore are EXCLUDED and counted, never imputed and never assigned zero: the scan measured coverage at 24.1%, so this gate can judge roughly a quarter of tickets and is silent on the rest, which is a stated limitation rather than a hidden one.
preregistered.enforcement: SHADOW ONLY. It writes ctrl:true, vetoShadow:true and changes no live entry. Nothing about this rule reaches the entry POST unless it clears its bar and the operator then approves it.
preregistered.statistic: PAIRED within-session gap on realised net rMult: (mean rM of ALLOWED) - (mean rM of REFUSED), computed INSIDE each session, then a one-sample t across sessions. The paired form removes the good-day/bad-day effect by construction. A working gate makes this POSITIVE — the tickets it refused did worse than the ones it allowed.
preregistered.clusteringUnit: SESSIONS. Ticket counts are never sample sizes on this board, and this rule in particular would look far stronger on tickets than it is: the scan's own session counts are what disqualified four other fields.

bar.note: best-of-12 because TWELVE fields were examined in the motivating scan, not one. The family is the scan, not the registration. Interim at 16 sessions is KILL-ONLY at t <= -2.0; it adjudicates nothing upward.

decisionRule.pass: paired t >= 2.859 at >= 30 sessions -> low-newsScore tickets are genuinely worse; the gate is PROPOSED to the operator as a live refusal, never auto-applied, and the news-trader seat has its first cleared claim.
decisionRule.fail: anything else -> DID NOT PASS. Combined with R13 (dead on cost) and R20 (t 0.08), a third independent negative would say plainly that news carries nothing tradeable on this board — which is a finding worth having, and worth more than a fourth attempt to find one.

knownWeaknesses: THE IN-SAMPLE READ IS ALREADY WEAK. The motivating arms are t -1.58 (bottom) and +1.64 (top). This is not a strong candidate being confirmed forward; it is a marginal one being tested honestly, and the prior should be that it fails.
COVERAGE IS 24.1%. Three of four tickets carry no finite newsScore and are excluded, so the gate is silent on most of the book and the paired statistic is computed on a minority of each session.

The threshold 0 is the measured p20 of a field whose distribution is heavily massed at zero — 'newsScore <= 0' may be closer to 'has no news at all' than to 'has bad news', in which case a pass would be a liquidity or coverage artifact rather than a news effect. If it clears, that alternative must be ruled out before any live use.

newsScore's own provenance is a vendor sentiment composite; it is not point-in-time verified, and news-stamp.js is forward-only from 2026-08-26, so the clean-era rows underlying the scan and the forward rows are not stamped by identical code paths.

One field was registered from twelve examined. The best-of-12 bar prices the search, but a reader seeing R85 alone without the scan will over-read it — the scan file is the family and must be read beside it.

A refusal gate cannot profit; the best outcome is avoided loss. Its value is bounded by what the refused tickets would have lost, which on a book whose canonical edge is -0.0003R is a small number even if the rule is real.
preregistered.readCondition: >= 30 evidence sessions from 2026-09-01 (~2026-10-14 at 5 sessions/week). Read BESIDE R13 and R20 as the third and last news attempt on this board.
preregistered.ipNote: None. The idea comes from our own ledger; the public sources the operator supplied contained no mechanic to borrow, which is itself recorded in origin above.
preregistered.status: PENDING — no forward evidence yet

preregistered.name: Noise-scaled ratchet — arm the floor a fixed multiple of the instrument's own 1-minute noise outside entry, in liquid names only
preregistered.script: backend/r86-noise-ratchet.js (forward writer, in the close chain; writes data/r86-noise-ratchet.json per class). The retrospective twin is backend/equity-ratchet-twin.js and is not the registered writer.
preregistered.multiplicityFamily: ratchet-arming (see origin: 12 fixed-R arms + 5 noise buckets + 3 population splits examined on 2026-09-01 before this rule was written)
preregistered.origin: MOTIVATED BY A SEARCH THAT I RAN SEVEN WAYS IN ONE SITTING, AND SAID SO. The operator asked whether the ratchet should arm earlier than 1R on equities and crypto. Sequence, in order, each cut chosen AFTER seeing the previous result: (1) 12 fixed-R arms replayed on real 1-minute paths, all negative, tightest worst; (2) split by hold length; (3) split by class — which revealed the pooled number was 115 crypto multi-day holds swamping 446 equity tickets, a pooling defect of mine; (4) excluding target hits; (5) equity-only session-clustered, where the sign FLIPPED versus ticket-weighted; (6) noise-ratio bucketing, which produced a clean monotonic gradient; (7) a degeneracy check on that gradient, which found 46% of tickets have a median 1-minute range of ZERO and 44.5% of minutes carry no trade at all. EVERY NUMBER FROM THAT SEQUENCE IS IN-SAMPLE AND WEIGHTLESS.
preregistered.whatTheSearchActuallyEstablished: Two things survive the degeneracy check and two do not. SURVIVES: (a) across the three buckets with a real, non-zero noise measure, the ratchet's harm is monotonic in how close the floor sits to the instrument's noise — delta -0.8010 at 1-2x, -0.1933 at 2-4x, -0.0269 at 4-8x; (b) crypto sits in the harmful zone (median ratio 5.36, and 11 of the 12 tickets in the worst bucket), so its floor is inside its own chop. DOES NOT SURVIVE: (c) the +0.0699 in the >8x bucket, because that bucket is where the degenerate names live — a ratchet 'works' on a name that barely trades, which is true and useless since it could not be filled; (d) the operator's equity-at-0.10R proposal, whose only supporting evidence was that same contaminated bucket.
preregistered.rule: ARM the ratchet floor at the first favourable excursion that places the floor at least K x NOISE outside the entry price, where NOISE is the median 1-minute bar range over the ticket's own hold so far, K = 4. Thereafter the floor trails the operator's integer-R ladder (1R->0R, 2R->1R, ...). REFUSE to arm at all on any ticket failing the liquidity screen.

parameters.kChosenHow: MOTIVATED, NOT DERIVED. 4x is where the measured harm gradient reaches approximately zero (-0.0269) in the last bucket that is not degeneracy-contaminated. It was chosen after seeing that gradient, which is why the bar below is best-of-20 rather than single-variant. A K fitted to this data is a searched parameter and is priced as one.
parameters.liquidityScreen: EXCLUDE any ticket where more than 20% of its 1-minute bars carry h == l (no trade in that minute), measured over the hold. Directly targets the artifact that invalidated the >8x bucket: 44.5% of bars were empty on average, and 46% of tickets had a median range of exactly zero.
parameters.noiseWindow: median 1-minute bar range over the ticket's hold-to-date, recomputed as the hold extends — never the full-hold range, which would look ahead.

armReachEligibility.rule: A sleeve (strategy x class) is ELIGIBLE for the ratchet only if its measured arm-reach rate — the share of its tickets whose favourable excursion reaches the arm threshold — is >= 10%, on >= 30 tickets. Ineligible sleeves are EXCLUDED and counted, never scored as neutral.
armReachEligibility.why: R86 gated on noise and liquidity but never asked whether a sleeve produces runners AT ALL. Measured 2026-09-01 on the clean era: only 2 of 10 sleeves reach 1R on >=10% of tickets. Trend/Equity reaches it on 0.9% of 111 tickets; Ensemble/Equity, the largest sleeve at 232 tickets, on 1.7%. A ratchet armed at 1R is structurally INERT on 8 of 10 sleeves, which means most of R86's population could never have produced an observation either way and would have diluted the paired statistic with zeros.
armReachEligibility.theTrapThisAlsoCloses: The ONLY sleeve comfortably clearing the gate is Breakout/Crypto at 88.9% reach and meanR +1.3773 on n=18 — and that is the same population already shown (R44) to be TWO crypto rally days, 96% of its P&L from 2026-08-21 and 2026-08-24. An eligibility gate fitted to the clean-era record would hand ratchet authority straight to a regime artifact. Eligibility is therefore measured FORWARD from evidenceStart on each sleeve's own accruing record, never from the clean-era history that contains those two days.
armReachEligibility.thresholdIsMotivated: 10% and 30 tickets were proposed by an external review as an operational range (10-15%) and adopted at the low end. They are not derived and are inside the best-of-20 family already priced into this bar.
armReachEligibility.unit: strategy x class x DIRECTION — not strategy x class.
armReachEligibility.whyDirectionSplits: Measured 2026-09-01 on equity+crypto: LONGS reach 1R on 8.0% of 429 tickets, SHORTS on 3.2% of 313 — a 2.5x gap, alongside shorts giving back MORE (+0.3365R vs +0.2943R). Pooling directions lets a marginal sleeve qualify on its longs while admitting shorts on which the rule can essentially never fire. Shorts are simultaneously the population with the most to protect and the fewest chances to arm.

preregistered.population: Every EQUITY and CRYPTO signal-arm ticket with a finite entry, a positive stopDist, and a recoverable 1-minute path, from evidenceStart forward. GRADED SEPARATELY BY CLASS and never pooled — pooling equity with crypto is precisely the defect that produced the first, wrong answer on 2026-09-01.
preregistered.statistic: PAIRED within-session delta: (mean rMult of the ratchet arm) - (mean rMult as actually settled) on the SAME tickets, computed inside each session, then a one-sample t across SESSIONS. Reported per class.
preregistered.clusteringUnit: SESSIONS. Ticket-weighting and session-weighting gave OPPOSITE SIGNS on the equity motivating sample (+0.0193 vs -0.0553), which is the clearest possible demonstration that the unit matters here.

bar.whyTwenty: 12 fixed-R arms + 5 noise buckets + 3 population splits were examined before this rule existed. The family is the whole search that produced it, not the one rule that came out. K was also chosen from that search, so it is inside the family rather than beside it.

decisionRule.pass: paired t >= 3.125 at >= 30 sessions IN A GIVEN CLASS -> the noise-scaled arm beats the book's own exits for that class; PROPOSED to the operator, never auto-applied, and never generalised to the other class on the strength of one.
decisionRule.fail: anything else -> DID NOT PASS. Combined with the retrospective (every fixed-R arm negative) this would say the give-back of +0.3115R per trade, while real, is not capturable by a trailing floor on this book — which is a finding worth having, because it redirects the effort to entry and target selection instead.

knownWeaknesses: THE STRONGEST-LOOKING EVIDENCE FOR THIS RULE IS THE PART THAT DID NOT SURVIVE. The >8x bucket that turned positive is contaminated by illiquid names; the liquidity screen exists to remove exactly those, which means the forward test runs on a population the motivating sample barely covered. The honest prior is that this fails.
K = 4 was read off the motivating gradient. A forward pass does not make it out-of-sample of the idea, only of the fit.

The motivating sample is 27 sessions and 561 replayed tickets, of which 181 (24%) had no recoverable 1-minute path and were excluded — and the survivors' baseline (+0.0168R) did not match the population's (-0.0046R), so even the retrospective ran on a better-behaved slice.
Crypto n is small: 115 tickets, and 11 of the 12 worst-bucket tickets. A per-class read on crypto will be underpowered for a long time.
Nothing in the whole retrospective was statistically significant in either direction — best |t| was 1.44. This registers a mechanism, not a confirmed effect.

The noise measure is median 1-minute RANGE, which conflates volatility with tick size and spread. On a wide-spread name the range is large without the price actually moving, which would push K x NOISE out and suppress arming for the wrong reason.
preregistered.readCondition: >= 30 evidence sessions from 2026-09-02, read SEPARATELY for equity and crypto (~2026-10-15 at 5 sessions/week for equity; crypto will take materially longer).
preregistered.ipNote: None. The rule is the operator's own integer-R ratchet re-expressed in noise units; the noise scaling and liquidity screen come from our own measurement.
preregistered.status: PENDING — no forward evidence yet

amendments.why: Without it, 8 of 10 sleeves contribute tickets on which the rule can never fire, diluting the paired statistic toward zero and making a null result uninterpretable — indistinguishable from 'the ratchet does nothing' versus 'the ratchet never got the chance'.

amendments.why: Longs and shorts differ by 2.5x in arm-reach inside the same sleeves (8.0% vs 3.2%), so a pooled gate admits a direction that cannot arm.

preregistered.name: momPctile entry filter — skip the bottom quintile of momentum percentile
preregistered.multiplicityFamily: entry-observer-scan (26 numeric observer fields examined 2026-09-01 in the inert-entry scan; ONE registered)
preregistered.origin: MOTIVATED BY A SEARCH, AND BY A PREMISE THAT TURNED OUT TO BE PARTLY WRONG. The day's exit work (ratchet, take-profit ladder, hold-horizon twin) all landed inside the noise, and the exit-reason mix showed 87% of equity/crypto tickets ending on the clock rather than at a bracket. That was read as 'entries produce trades that go nowhere' and prompted a scan of 26 observer fields for association with movement. The premise was PARTLY WRONG: 78% of tickets do travel >= 0.25R, they simply never reach brackets set at 1R and 2R, and much of that travel is adverse. Of the 26 fields scanned, all but two had top quintiles collapsing to 3-5 SESSIONS — market-level fields that gate days rather than tickets, the same defect that disqualified polNews from R85. momPctile was the only field with genuine session coverage on both sides.
preregistered.theCorroborationDidNotHold: When first proposed to the operator this was described as the one field surviving two independent questions — the movement scan and the observer ledger's +0.100R gap. RECOMPUTED ON THE CANONICAL LEDGER BEFORE REGISTERING, it does not: the two momPctile quintiles move almost identically (mean max-excursion +0.547 vs +0.567) and win at 45.6% vs 44.6%. The movement separation seen in the scan was on the equity/crypto subset with a binary 0.25R threshold and does not reproduce on the full ledger. Only the R gap survives, and it is weak.
preregistered.rule: SKIP any new ticket whose obs.momPctile is at or below 0.223; TAKE the rest.
preregistered.definition: Threshold FIXED IN ADVANCE at 0.223, the measured p20 of momPctile over the 905 clean-era rows carrying the field. An absolute constant, never a rolling quantile — a threshold recomputed each session drifts with its own population and cannot be falsified. Tickets with no finite momPctile are EXCLUDED and counted, never imputed.
preregistered.enforcement: SHADOW ONLY. Writes ctrl:true, vetoShadow:true; changes no live entry. Nothing reaches the entry POST unless it clears its bar and the operator then approves it.

preregistered.name: Cross-sectional selection — can the scanner's score RANK, with market direction removed?
preregistered.script: backend/r106-cross-sectional.js (reader over data/r7-scanner-shadow.json settled horizons; runs nightly in the close chain)
preregistered.parent: The R7 scanner's ensemble vote, already stamped daily on a fixed 100-name universe in data/r7-scanner-shadow.json with settled +1/+3/+5 day horizons.
preregistered.origin: Operator 2026-09-08, after a strategy roadmap proposed more exit twins, cost gates and conditioned VRP: the board's measured problem is not its exits. Signal minus control is -0.016R over 32 sessions on the whole board and -0.041R in crypto, where our picks lose to coin flips. Adding a better exit to a signal with no selection edge optimises the tail of something with no head. This asks the head question directly.
preregistered.question: Every directional result on this board confounds SELECTION with DIRECTION. Longs made money and shorts lost money in the sample for our picks AND for the coin flips, almost identically, so what looked like an edge was net exposure times tape (the R44 finding). A long-short book built from the same score cancels market direction by construction, so whatever remains is ranking skill or nothing.
preregistered.multiplicityFamily: SINGLE VARIANT. K and the horizon are both fixed before evidence and are NOT searched: K = 10 is the conventional decile of a 100-name universe, and +3 days is the horizon R7's own primary cleared on 2026-09-03, taken verbatim from that existing measurement rather than chosen here. The retrospective preview below was computed at K = 5, 10 and 20 and is disclosed in full; K = 5 is the only non-negative one and is deliberately NOT the registered choice, because picking it after seeing it is the search this bar exists to price.
preregistered.rule: FROZEN. Each session the R7 scanner stamps a vote for every name in its fixed 100-name universe before the outcome. Rank that session's names by vote, descending. LONG the top 10, SHORT the bottom 10, equal count and equal dollar risk per name. Hold exactly 3 trading days and exit at the close. The session's result is mean(return of the 10 longs) - mean(return of the 10 shorts), minus one equity round trip on each leg (2 x 0.2242% from the measured cost model). Sessions where the scanner stamped fewer than 20 usable names are skipped and counted. Nothing is booked to the board; this is a paper reader over an existing collector.
preregistered.statistic: mean net long-short spread per session, in percent. CLUSTERING UNIT: sessions. t is the one-sample t on the per-session spreads.

bar.metric: mean net session spread, one-sample t on sessions
bar.why: single-variant because K and horizon are both taken from prior fixed choices rather than searched here

preregistered.interimKill: at 15 evidence sessions, t <= -2 KILLS it — that would say the score ranks backwards, which is itself a finding worth having early
preregistered.decisionRule: PASS -> the scanner's score ranks cross-sectionally, and selection is real independently of direction. That would be the first such result on this board and it routes to the operator as a proposal for a market-neutral sleeve, not an automatic adoption. DID NOT PASS -> the score does not rank. Combined with the existing long/short decomposition that would close the question: the board's directional results are exposure, not selection, and no exit twin or cost gate can fix that. Either answer is worth the 30 sessions.

retrospectivePreviewWeightless.note: Computed 2026-09-08 on the 24 already-settled +3d sessions BEFORE registration. It is exploratory, carries zero weight, and is recorded here so it cannot be quietly re-run later and presented as forward evidence.
retrospectivePreviewWeightless.K10: mean -0.452% per session, t -1.15, 11/24 positive  <- the registered choice
retrospectivePreviewWeightless.reading: The wider the decile the worse it gets, which is the signature of no ranking information at all rather than a weak one.

preregistered.expectedOutcomeOnTheRecord: I expect DID NOT PASS. The preview is negative at the registered K, the monotone worsening from K=5 to K=20 is what no-information looks like, and the scanner's own per-name separation on the board is about two hundredths of an R either way. Registering it anyway because 'we cannot pick' is currently an inference from a confound, and this measures it directly.
knownWeaknesses: The universe is 100 mega-caps, so a pass would say the score ranks LIQUID LARGE CAPS and would not transfer to the board's 4,000-name roster without a separate read.

Equal dollar risk per name is not equal risk: a 3-day hold on a high-beta name carries more variance than on a low-beta one, so the spread carries residual beta even though gross exposure nets to zero.
Cost is charged at the measured equity round trip, which is a median. Short legs also carry borrow, which is NOT modelled and would make a marginal pass fail.
Three-day holds overlap across sessions, so consecutive session spreads are not independent; the session t therefore overstates certainty and a block-bootstrap would be the stricter reading.
The collector has stamped every session since 2026-07-31, so the forward sample and the preview sample come from the same market period and the same 100 names.

preregistered.name: The impact-charged book — does the equity book survive its own footprint?
preregistered.script: backend/r107-impact-twin.js (nightly in the close chain; stamps a modelled impact charge on each settled equity ticket and reads the charged book)
preregistered.parent: The equity signal book on the canonical clean-era ledger, and its existing coin-flip controls.
preregistered.origin: Operator 2026-09-08 asked to register a participation/capacity rule from a strategy roadmap. I intended to decline it as unfireable at paper size, measured it first, and was wrong: the median equity ticket already participates at 0.115% of its symbol's median daily volume, and a square-root impact model at C = 1.0 charges 0.032R per ticket at TODAY's size. The board's whole measured signal-minus-control gap is 0.016R. The omission is the same size as the thing being measured, so this is a live question and not a distant one.
preregistered.whyItIsNotAlreadyMeasured: A paper order moves no price, so rMult on this ledger cannot contain impact and never will, however many sessions accrue. The cost model charges spread and commission only. Every result this apparatus has produced is therefore measured in a world where our own trading has no price effect. This test does not fix that; it prices it.
preregistered.multiplicityFamily: SINGLE VARIANT for the primary. The impact coefficient C = 1.0 is the declared central value of the square-root law and is fixed before evidence; C = 0.3 and C = 1.5 are computed every night as DISCLOSED SENSITIVITIES and can never be substituted for the primary. Size multiples 1x/10x/100x are reported as a capacity curve, not as variants of the claim.
preregistered.rule: FROZEN. For every settled equity ticket, participation p = shares / median daily volume over the trailing 30 sessions of that symbol, and sigma = the standard deviation of that symbol's daily log returns over the same window. The modelled impact charge is impactR = 2 x C x sigma x sqrt(p) / stopPct, charged once on entry and once on exit, expressed in R using the ticket's own stop. The CHARGED book is the same ticket with rMultCharged = rMult - impactR. No ticket is refused, resized or reordered: the charge is applied after the fact to the identical tickets, so the charged book and the live book differ only by the charge.
preregistered.statistic: mean rMultCharged per session for the signal book, one-sample t on the per-session means, against zero. CLUSTERING UNIT: sessions. Reported beside it, never in place of it: the same figure for the controls, the uncharged book, and the capacity curve at 1x/10x/100x.

bar.metric: mean charged R per ticket, session-clustered t vs zero
bar.why: single-variant: C is declared in advance at the square-root law's central value, not searched

preregistered.interimKill: at 15 evidence sessions, t <= -2 KILLS the claim that the charged book is viable at current size
preregistered.decisionRule: PASS -> the equity book is positive net of its own modelled footprint at current size, and the capacity curve then says how far it scales. DID NOT PASS -> the book does not survive its own footprint, and every net figure this apparatus reports is overstated by roughly the charge. That would be a first-order caveat on the whole record, not a defect in this test, and it would mean funding decisions must use the charged number.

measuredAtRegistration.note: Computed 2026-09-08 on 333 settled equity tickets across 209 symbols, BEFORE registration. Exploratory and weightless; recorded so it cannot be re-run later and presented as forward evidence.
measuredAtRegistration.medianParticipation: 0.115% of median daily volume at current size
measuredAtRegistration.reading: Impact at current size is already about twice the magnitude of the board's entire measured gap, and the charge grows with the square root of size, so a ten-fold scale-up costs a tenth of an R per ticket.

preregistered.expectedOutcomeOnTheRecord: I expect DID NOT PASS, because the uncharged book is already at -0.023R per ticket and this only subtracts. The value is not the verdict but the number: it converts 'the book is roughly flat' into 'the book is flat before its own footprint and negative after it', which is the figure a funding decision needs.
knownWeaknesses: C = 1.0 is DECLARED, not measured on our own fills, because we have no live fills to measure it from. The whole result scales with C, and the disclosed C = 0.3 case cuts the charge to under a third. This is the weakest joint in the test and the sensitivities exist because of it.

The square-root law is an empirical regularity from institutional execution data, mostly at participation levels far above ours; extrapolating it down to 0.1% participation is an assumption, and at that level real impact may be closer to zero than the model says.
Median daily volume over 30 sessions is a crude liquidity measure and ignores intraday distribution: a ticket filled at the open faces different depth than one filled at 14:00.

Impact is charged identically to signals and controls, so it CANNOT change the signal-minus-control gap. This test is about the absolute book, and any reading of it as evidence about selection would be wrong.
It says nothing about options, futures, FX or crypto tickets, which have different microstructure and are excluded.

preregistered.name: Let winners run past the close — does a ticket green at the end-of-session flatten beat the flatten if held one more session?
preregistered.script: backend/r109-hold-past-close.js (nightly in the close chain); store data/r109-hold-past-close.json
preregistered.parent: The exit-reason decomposition of 2026-09-09: 66% of clean-era exits are 'close', the end-of-session flatten, at avgWin +0.247R against avgLoss -0.216R. Only 1.4% of tickets ever reached a target and the ratchet armed once in 201 tickets, because almost nothing lives long enough to trail.
preregistered.origin: Operator, 2026-09-09, reading that decomposition: 'so we should let winners run past the close'. A real proposal, so it gets measured rather than agreed with.
preregistered.question: The flatten exits at an arbitrary clock time, which produces near-symmetric outcomes — noise harvested at a random point. If the book's winners carry momentum, holding them one more session should pay. If they mean-revert, the flatten is protecting the book rather than costing it. Either answer changes how every position is managed; neither is currently known.

motivatingPreview.weight: NONE. Exploratory, computed 2026-09-09 on the same exits that generated the hypothesis. Disclosed in full so it cannot later be described as prospective.
motivatingPreview.population: 453 close-flattened Equity tickets across 26 sessions; 236 green at the close, 217 red.
motivatingPreview.reading: The point estimate for the proposal is NEGATIVE at every horizon and gets monotonically worse — a ticket green at the close and held five more sessions decays from +0.233R to -0.006R. Nothing cleared any bar (|t| 0.16 to 0.75 against bars near 1.7), so the preview decides nothing. It is registered anyway BECAUSE the estimate points against the operator's expectation: a hypothesis is worth testing precisely when the cheap look disagrees with the intuition, and refusing to register it on the strength of a weightless backward look would be the same error in the opposite direction.
motivatingPreview.selectionNote: NINE cells were previewed (3 horizons x 3 subsets). All nine are disclosed above. None was favourable, so this cell cannot have been chosen for looking good — but the horizon was nonetheless SEARCHED, and the bar below pays for it.

preregistered.multiplicityFamily: THREE VARIANTS — the horizon only (+1, +3, +5 sessions). The subset is fixed at 'green at the close' because that is the operator's stated rule, named before the sweep, and the all/losers arms were diagnostic context rather than adoption candidates. The registered PRIMARY is +1 session; +3 and +5 accrue alongside as declared members of the same family and share its bar. Any other subset, any other exit condition, or a size-weighted version is a NEW test with its own registration.
preregistered.rule: FROZEN. At the end-of-session flatten, every position closed with reason 'close' and a positive booked rMult is recorded as a SHADOW with its symbol, direction, entry, floored stop distance and booked R. Nothing about the live flatten changes: the position is still closed, the ledger still records the flatten, and no capital is held overnight. On the Nth trading session after the flatten (N = 1 primary, 3 and 5 secondary), the shadow is graded as ((close_N - entry) * direction) / stopDist — the same entry and the same stop distance the real ticket used, so the counterfactual is measured in the ticket's own R. The statistic is the DELTA: held-R minus booked-R. Cost is charged to NEITHER arm, because the position is opened and closed exactly once either way and extending a hold adds no round trip; the comparison is cost-neutral by construction.
preregistered.statistic: Mean session-clustered delta (held minus booked) in R. CLUSTERING UNIT: the SESSION of the flatten — every ticket flattened on one day shares that day's overnight tape, so a session contributes the mean of its own shadows and the t is computed across sessions, never across tickets.

bar.metric: mean session-clustered delta R, held minus booked
bar.why: best-of-3: the horizon was searched across +1/+3/+5 in the motivating preview

preregistered.interimKill: At 15 sessions, a session-clustered t <= -2 KILLS it. That would say holding is actively worse than flattening, which is worth knowing early because it is the direction the preview already points and it would close the question rather than leave it open for months.
preregistered.decisionRule: PASS (t >= bar AND mean delta > 0) -> holding green tickets one session beats the flatten, and the finding routes to the operator as a PROPOSAL to change the flatten rule — never an automatic adoption, and never before a capacity and overnight-gap-risk reading accompanies it. DID NOT PASS -> the end-of-session flatten is not costing the book its winners, and 'let them run' is retired as an explanation for the payoff ratio; the 0.72 payoff and the 54% shortfall against breakeven are then an ENTRY problem and must be pursued there rather than in exit management.
knownWeaknesses: The preview already points negative at all three horizons. If the forward read agrees, this test will have spent 30 sessions confirming something a backward look suggested — that is the honest price of not acting on a weightless preview, but it should be stated rather than dressed up as discovery.

Equity only in the preview, because daily bars and a real stopDist are needed to grade the counterfactual. The forward test will grade whatever classes carry those fields, so the population may drift class-mix over the accrual and a late composition shift could move the estimate for reasons unrelated to the rule. The class mix is recorded per session so that can be checked at the read.

SHADOW ONLY. It measures what holding WOULD have returned at the next close, and a real overnight hold is not free of everything: it carries gap risk, an overnight margin treatment, and the possibility that the operator would not in fact have held through a gap down. A PASS therefore establishes the price path was favourable, not that the position was survivable.

'Green at the close' is measured on the booked rMult, which is GROSS of cost. A ticket fractionally green gross may be red net. The threshold is the operator's stated rule as given, and moving it to a net threshold later would be a new variant owing a wider bar.

Grading uses the CLOSE of session N. A position held overnight could be exited anywhere in session N; the close is one arbitrary point chosen because it is the only one the flatten rule itself would use. It is not the best available exit and does not claim to be.
The 30-session bar means a read no earlier than roughly mid-November on the current ~1 flatten-session-per-trading-day rate, and the interim kill at 15 sessions is the only early exit.

Overlapping holds: a +5d shadow spans sessions that later shadows also span, so the +3 and +5 arms are serially dependent in a way the +1 arm is not. The primary is +1 for that reason; the secondaries are reported with the overlap stated and must not be read as independent confirmations.

preregistered.question: Over the two years before the sleeve went live, did the R25 rule — 25-delta same-day put and call spreads, one strike wide, entered ~09:50 ET, held to the close — make money after crossing and commissions?

preregistered.multiplicityFamily: SINGLE — the frozen R25 rule, replayed, no parameter examined. Reported weightless beside it and never read as the result: puts vs calls, the OP4b 2x wing cap on the 1-minute path, the DIA/GLD/TLT extension, per-year splits.
preregistered.rule: DAYS: every NYSE session in the window (Alpaca /v2/calendar), early closes included. UNDERLYINGS: SPY, QQQ, IWM (weighted); DIA, GLD, TLT (weightless). ENTRY PRICE: for each same-day OCC contract on a $1 strike grid within 3% of spot, the close of its last 1-minute trade bar from 09:45 to 09:50 ET inclusive; a contract with no print in that window does not exist for the day. SPOT: the underlying's 09:50 ET 1-minute close (SIP). DELTA: Black-Scholes implied from that price, r = 4.5%, no dividend, time to the session close. SELECTION (R25 verbatim): per side, the strike whose delta is nearest 0.25 within 0.10; long leg = the adjacent strike further out ($1 wide); width <= 3% of spot. CREDIT: short price - long price (a trade-price stand-in for the mid). CROSSING: the median (creditMid - creditCross) R25 recorded live for that underlying through 2026-09-15 (live anchors if the underlying has fewer than 5 live wings); creditCross = credit - crossing; skip if creditCross <= 0 or crossing > 35% of credit. SETTLE: intrinsic at the underlying's last regular-session 1-minute close (16:00, or the early close), exactly as options-settle.js; P&L per contract = (creditCross - cost) x 100 - 2 x $0.65; R = P&L / maxLoss where maxLoss = (width - creditCross) x 100.
preregistered.statistic: Per SESSION: mean R of that session's weighted wings (SPY/QQQ/IWM, both sides). Mean across sessions with session-clustered t. CLUSTERING UNIT = sessions. Reported beside it, weightless: net $ per contract and at the live 4 contracts, win rate, per-year and per-month net, worst sessions, max drawdown, puts vs calls, the 2x-cap path replay, the extension line.

bar.source: R25's own frozen bar (day-clustered t >= 2), stricter than nullBar({variants:1}).p95 ~ 1.65
bar.interim: none — one run over a fixed sample; the writer refuses to overwrite its store
bar.decisionRule: CLEARED (t >= 2.0, mean > 0, >= 250 sessions) -> memo: the rule made money over two years at modelled cost; R66's forward read stays the contract for any change; the replay supplies the session distribution (worst days, drawdown) for OP4c's size. DID NOT PASS -> memo: the live run is not supported by two years of history; OP4c (4 contracts, extension) is the operator's to reconsider with this in hand. Either way nothing is wired, sized or changed by this read.

preregistered.knownAnswer: Before reading, the same code path re-selects R25's live anchor wings for 2026-08-20..2026-09-15 and compares with what R25 recorded: the short strike must be the same or adjacent in >= 70% of wings, and the median |replay credit - live creditMid| must be <= $0.03. A failure means the replay is not R25 and the run is not read.
knownWeaknesses: PRICES ARE TRADES, NOT QUOTES: the last print can sit at the bid or the ask; selection and credit carry that noise. The live 09-14 wing-cap misfire came from exactly this kind of noise.
CROSSING IS BORROWED from four weeks of live wings in one calm regime; wider books on stress days are not modelled.
LIVE LIQUIDITY FILTERS CANNOT BE REPLAYED: R25 drops legs with wide quotes; history has no quotes, so the replay keeps some wings live would have skipped.
DELTA IS MODELLED (flat r, no dividend, calendar time); Schwab's live greeks differ slightly. The known-answer check bounds the effect.
EARLY ASSIGNMENT and pin risk at the close are ignored, as options-settle.js ignores them.
THREE ~0.9-CORRELATED INDICES: effective N per session is about two; sessions, not wings, are the unit.
SAME-DAY EXPIRIES for QQQ and IWM were not daily across the whole window; days without a contract are skipped, so the underlying mix shifts over time.

preregistered.evidenceStartNote: Retrospective over a fixed sample. The signal list was built from SEC filings alone (outcome-free) before registration; no price for any signal had been read.

preregistered.origin: Operator 2026-09-20: a social-media reel pitching Form 4 monitoring, then 'run it'.
preregistered.question: Do cluster open-market purchases by officers and directors, bought the day after they become public and held six months, beat holding SPY over the same dates?

dataAvailability.source: SEC Insider Transactions Data Sets, 2019q1..2025q4 (sec.gov structured Form 3/4/5 data)

preregistered.rule: SIGNAL (frozen in r137-insider-signals.js): original Form 4, non-derivative, code P, acquired, price and shares > 0, common/ordinary stock, reporting owner an Officer or Director, the insider's purchases in the filing totalling >= $10,000; a signal is the filing that brings DISTINCT such insiders at one issuer to three within 30 calendar days by FILING date; one signal per issuer per 180 days; signals filed 2019-01-01..2025-03-31. TRADE: buy at the OPEN of the first trading day after the signal's filing date; sell at the CLOSE 126 trading days later; SPY bought and sold on the same two days. Prices: Alpaca daily bars, total-return adjusted, consolidated tape. No cost is charged (one round trip in six months). ONE variant; nothing is searched.
preregistered.statistic: PRIMARY: mean EXCESS return (stock minus SPY) per signal, averaged within the calendar MONTH of entry, then a t across months. CLUSTERING UNIT = entry months (six-month holds overlap heavily, so signals are not independent). WEIGHTLESS: median excess, share of signals beating SPY, raw stock and SPY means, by year, by buyer count (3 / 4+), by dollar size, the best and worst 5% share of the total, and the count of signals with NO usable price history.

bar.metric: mean monthly-averaged excess return over SPY, t across entry months
bar.source: lib/null-bar.js nullBar({variants:6,n:60,trials:20000}).p95 = 2.472. One variant is run; it is charged as best-of-6 because the buyer count (3), the window (30 days) and the hold (6 months) are each a choice among the two or three values the literature uses.
bar.decisionRule: PASSES iff >= 40 entry months, mean excess > 0, t >= 2.472, AND the mean excess is still > 0 when every signal with no usable price history is counted as a 30% LOSS against SPY. A PASS adopts nothing: it would be a candidate tilt for the operator's core portfolio to discuss with his adviser, never a TRAIDS trade. Otherwise DID NOT PASS.

preregistered.knownAnswer: SPY's own six-month return computed by this script for entries on 2020-03-24 and 2022-01-04 must match an independent recomputation from the same bars to 1e-9 (plumbing), and a signal list with its dates SHUFFLED across tickers must show a mean excess within 2 standard errors of zero.
knownWeaknesses: SURVIVORSHIP, AND IT FLATTERS. The price vendor mostly serves companies that still exist; insiders who bought into a company that later failed drop out. Missing signals are counted and the pass condition includes a penalised lens, but the true delisting return is unknown.
TICKER REUSE AND CHANGES. The SEC file carries the ticker at filing time; a ticker later reassigned to another company would attach the wrong prices. Not corrected; small caps are most exposed.
JOINT FILINGS. One Form 4 can list several reporting owners (a fund and its principals); each counts as a distinct insider, so some 'clusters' are one economic buyer.
THE EFFECT IS KNOWN AND HAS DECAYED in the literature; 2019-2025 includes the 2020 crash and rebound, when cluster buying near the lows was unusually rewarded. A pass here may be one regime.
SMALL COMPANIES DOMINATE the signal list; next-open fills at size are not realistic for many of them, and no cost or slippage is charged.
EQUAL-WEIGHTED per signal within a month, which is not an investable portfolio.
OVERLAPPING HOLDS: month clustering understates the dependence; the true t is lower than the one reported.
NOT INDEPENDENTLY AUDITED. New code, written today.
EXPECTATION, stated before the read: a small positive excess that does not clear the bar, or clears it only through 2020.
preregistered.readCondition: One read, once prices are fetched and both known-answer checks pass.
preregistered.ip: Public data; ours.
preregistered.status: READ 2026-09-20 — DID NOT PASS. 3182 cluster insider-buy signals over 76 entry months, 2019-01..2025-03, bought next open and held 126 trading days: mean monthly-averaged excess over SPY -2.81% per six months, t -1.536 against a bar of +2.472; median excess -9.95%, 37.5% of signals beat SPY; stocks 7.53% vs SPY 9.7%. 304 signals (8.7%) had no usable price history; counted as a 30% loss the excess is -5.81% (t -3.534). Baseline (same tickers, dates shuffled) -1.42%. By year: only 2020 (+13.16%) and the partial 2025 were positive; 2021 -16.26%. Survivorship flatters this sample, so the true figure is lower. The cluster-insider-buy question is closed as registered; no variant is to be run on this sample.

amendments.what: Known-answer 2 restated BEFORE any price was fetched. As registered it required a date-shuffled signal list to show a mean excess within 2 standard errors of zero. That is wrong: shuffling dates across tickers keeps the ticker list's own tilt (mostly small companies) against SPY, which need not be zero. The shuffled run is therefore REPORTED as the universe's baseline excess beside the primary, and is not a pass/fail check. The plumbing check (SPY against itself) stays a hard gate. The bar, the rule and the pass condition are unchanged.

preregistered.name: Opening-range breakout on NQ — six fixed variants, one historical read
preregistered.evidenceNote: A historical test on the full NQ 1-minute sample we hold (Massive, 2025-08-19..2026-09-21, ~270 sessions). Registered before any real row was read; the leak test on scrambled sessions ran first. One read, sealed.
preregistered.status: READ 2026-09-21 — DID NOT PASS — best of six L5-midpoint: 3.969 net pts/session, t 0.492 (bar 2.399), halves 9.415 / -1.476; four of six variants negative; 270 sessions 2025-08-19..2026-09-21
preregistered.parent: R139 (ares forward) — the profile of ares' record: entries concentrated 09:30-10:30 ET, same-day exits, 36% winners, wins ~2.6x losses.
preregistered.multiplicityFamily: ORB-NQ — six variants: opening range 5 / 15 / 30 minutes x stop at the opposite side / the range midpoint. All six are run and the bar is best-of-6.
preregistered.rule: Opening range = high/low of NQ 1-minute bars 09:30 to 09:30+L ET. Signal = the FIRST 1-minute bar after the range whose close is beyond the range (long above the high, short below the low), bar starting before 12:00 ET; one trade per session. Entry at the OPEN of the next bar. Stop at the opposite side of the range or the midpoint, checked from the entry bar; exit at the stop (or that bar's open if it opened beyond). Otherwise exit at the last regular-session close. netPts = points x direction - 0.75 pt.
preregistered.statistic: Mean netPts per SESSION (a session with no signal counts 0), t across sessions. Unit: session.

leakTest.method: same pipeline on bar-shuffled sessions (each bar's shape vs the prior close kept, order shuffled within the session), seeds 1, 2, 3
leakTest.result: no variant shows a positive edge on noise; every variant-seed is negative
leakTest.note: The pipeline carries a NEGATIVE bias on noise (about -2 to -12 gross pts per trade by variant). It cannot manufacture a false positive in the pass direction; the read must report each real variant beside its noise floor.

preregistered.interimKill: none — one run over a fixed sample

decisionRule.pass: Some variant has mean netPts per session > 0 with t >= 2.399 over >= 200 sessions, AND that variant's mean is still > 0 with one extra tick (0.25 pt) each side charged, AND its mean is > 0 in BOTH halves of the sample by date. A PASS adopts NOTHING: it earns a forward paper test on NQ/MNQ at a futures-capable venue, registered separately; funding, size and venue are the operator's.
decisionRule.fail: Otherwise DID NOT PASS: the plain opening-range breakout is closed on this sample and no other variant (other range lengths, cutoffs, targets, filters) is to be run on it.

preregistered.readCondition: Immediately after registration: node backend/r140-orb-nq.js (refuses unless R140 is registered).
knownWeaknesses: ONE YEAR: ~270 sessions of one regime (a strong Nasdaq uptrend with sharp corrections). An ORB can pass or fail on a single trend year.
MOTIVATED BY A WINNER: the rule family was chosen because ares, a leaderboard survivor, trades this way. That is why the bar is best-of-6 and the halves must agree.
FRONT MONTH BY VOLUME: bars are stitched to the most-traded NQ contract per day; roll days can carry a price discontinuity that is not a trade.
BAR RESOLUTION: stops are filled at the stop price when a 1-minute bar trades through it; real fills on fast moves are worse. The extra-tick condition only partly covers this.
SIZE IGNORED: one contract per trade; risk per trade varies with the range width, unlike ares' fixed 1% risk.
preregistered.ip: Our own rule, built from public knowledge of opening-range breakouts; ares' rules are not known and not used.

preregistered.parent: R13 (STAGNANT 2026-08-03): buying the gappers LOST 0.508pp gross vs SPY per trade (t -4.20) over 290 days 2024-01..2025-02. Screen of the 29 'reliable losers' (corpus read) on 2026-09-21: R13 is the only one whose PRE-cost loss exceeds the round-trip cost.
preregistered.multiplicityFamily: FADE-R13 — two entry timings (09:35, the open). The direction is fixed by R13's in-sample result; the holdout has never been read.
preregistered.rule: Event: a 1-5 letter symbol tagged on >= 1 Alpaca news article created 04:00-09:25 ET on day d, whose SIP daily open is >= 1.02 x the prior SIP close and >= $5. PRIMARY '0935': short at the open of the 09:35 SIP 1-minute bar, cover at the SIP daily close; SPY hedged over the same interval. SECOND 'open': short at the SIP daily open, cover at the close (R13's timing, which selects on the price it enters at). Fade excess = -[(exit/entry-1) - (SPY exit/SPY entry-1)] x 100 pp. Cost per event = half the SIP quoted spread at entry + half at exit (median over 09:35:00-09:35:30 [09:30:30-09:31:00 for 'open'] and 15:59:00-15:59:30) + 0.05pp fees/slippage + 0.10pp one-day borrow; no two-sided quote = 1.00pp + borrow.

bar.source: lib/null-bar.js nullBar({variants:2, n:380, trials:20000}).p95 = 1.964, floored at the house 2.0

leakTest.plan: Before the real read: the same selection with each event's open->close replaced by the same symbol's open->close on a random other holdout day (seeds 1, 2, 3). Must show |t| < 2 on the gross fade; otherwise the pipeline, not the market, is producing the result and the read is not taken.
leakTest.result: LEAK TEST FAILED 2026-09-22 — read NOT taken, per the registered rule. With each event's open->close replaced by the SAME symbol's open->close on a random other holdout day, the gross fade still shows 0.1354pp (t 2.707), 0.1209pp (t 2.492), 0.0714pp (t 1.37) across seeds 1-3 (390 days, 21,479 events). The selected names (volatile, news-prone, >= $5) lose to SPY intraday on ordinary days, so a fade of them 'works' without the news or the gap; the registered statistic cannot separate the event from the population. Even that population drift (~0.1pp gross) sits below the charged cost (half-spreads + 0.05pp + 0.10pp borrow). No real event outcome was computed.

preregistered.interimKill: none — one run over a fixed holdout

decisionRule.pass: A variant with >= 200 days, net mean > 0, t >= 2.0, and net mean > 0 in BOTH halves by date. PASS adopts NOTHING: the missing piece is the real borrow cost and availability of these names, which a quote feed cannot show; a PASS routes to the operator as a candidate for a short-side paper test at a broker that reports borrow (fees and locate), registered separately.
decisionRule.fail: Otherwise DID NOT PASS: R13's losing pattern does not survive as a tradeable fade at an executable entry and measured cost; the R13 line is closed and no other gap threshold, window or filter is to be run on the holdout.

preregistered.readCondition: After the news crawl completes and the leak test passes: node backend/r141-r13-fade.js (refuses unless R141 is registered).
preregistered.expectation: I expect it not to pass: the likely reasons R13's loss looked large (a thin opening print; entering at the price that defined the event) are exactly what flatter a fade, and the rule removes both.
knownWeaknesses: BORROW: 0.10pp per day is a flat guess. Hard-to-borrow gappers can cost far more, or be unshortable; a PASS does not show they could be shorted.
SHORT-SIDE EXECUTION: shorting into a morning gap risks halts, squeezes and locate failures that a bar test does not see.

These members signal rarely and hold for months to years; a per-trade mean treats a two-year hold and a two-day hold alike, so the statistic is dominated by holding length and extreme tails and its t is not reliable. A time-weighted return series is the standard statistic for a strategy and is well behaved on noise.

Cause: positions still open on the last bar were DROPPED. Rare-exit rules close mainly after a favourable move (an overbought exit after a rally, a reversal after a trend), so the positions left open at the end were disproportionately the losers — dropping them selected on outcome. Trend followers show the mirror image. TradingView's own equity includes open profit; the fix marks every open position at the last close and counts it.

preregistered.rule: Daily SPY and TLT closes (Alpaca SIP, adjustment=all), common dates only. Signal days = the last 5 trading days of each calendar month whose trading days are all known (a later-month date exists, or the loaded window ends on that month's last calendar day; an in-progress month signals nothing). On signal day t: drift = (SPY[t]/SPY[pme]-1) - (TLT[t]/TLT[pme]-1), pme = last trading day of the previous calendar month; only closes at or before t are used. drift > 0 -> SHORT SPY / LONG TLT equal dollar; drift < 0 -> LONG SPY / SHORT TLT; drift = 0 -> flat. The position is held for the NEXT trading day u = t+1 close-to-close: gross = pos x ((TLT[u]/TLT[t]-1) - (SPY[u]/SPY[t]-1)). All other days flat.

preregistered.expectation: Prior leans DID NOT PASS. The paper reports a real month-end reversal in equity-minus-bond returns, but the per-trade effect it documents is small relative to daily SPY-TLT spread volatility (~1.5%), the ETF/duration proxy dilutes it, and 57 holdout months give little power. A PASS would need a net mean of order tens of bps per trade, persistent in both 2022-2024 and 2024-2026.
knownWeaknesses: The paper's evidence is strongest when the equity-bond drift is LARGE (threshold / big-deviation months) and uses futures and broad bond indices; this rule trades every month on the sign of any drift, so small-drift months add noise and cost.
TLT is a ~17-year-duration Treasury ETF, not the aggregate bond portfolio a 60/40 fund holds; its volatility dominates the spread and dilutes the rebalancing signal.
Equal dollar legs are not volatility-matched; the spread's variance is driven by TLT in rate shocks (2022) and by SPY in equity shocks.
Rebalancing timing is heterogeneous (calendar vs threshold, month vs quarter end); a fixed last-5-days window and one-day hold may miss when the flow actually trades.
The paper was circulated in 2025, so part of the holdout is post-publication; any crowding would work against the rule.
Only ~5 trade days per month: 60 discovery and 57 holdout monthly observations; a true effect of a few bps per trade is below the resolution of a 1.70 t bar.
The 2022+ holdout has a positive stock-bond correlation regime unlike most of 2017-2021.
Cost of 0.02% per leg ignores short-borrow fees on SPY/TLT and assumes close fills (MOC).
SPY and TLT verified complete against the official calendar (2,506 of 2,506 sessions).

The literature reports a large announcement-day premium through ~2011-2015 that has visibly faded since publication; expect the holdout net mean to be small and the plain t well below 1.70 (DID NOT PASS is the more likely outcome, perhaps 75-80%). Close-to-close timing mixes the pre-announcement morning (Lucca-Moench drift is concentrated in the 24h BEFORE 2pm, largely on day t-1) with the 2pm reaction and afternoon reversal; the rule does not capture day t-1 afternoon, where much of the documented pre-FOMC drift lived.
The pre-FOMC/announcement premium is documented to have weakened after publication (Lucca-Moench note it faded post-2015); the discovery and holdout windows both lie in the post-publication era.

Baseline is the mean of the prior 20 non-event days: in trending or high-volatility regimes (e.g. 2020, 2022) that mean is noisy and adds variance to each meeting's excess; it also still contains other macro-announcement days (CPI, NFP), so the test is FOMC-vs-other-days, not announcement-vs-quiet-days.

2020 contributes only 7 scheduled meetings (03-17/18 cancelled); the emergency 2020-03-03 and 2020-03-16 reactions are excluded as events by design, which removes the largest FOMC-driven moves of the sample.
adjustment=all makes returns total-return; the ex-dividend day of SPY occasionally coincides with a statement day, a small mechanical effect equal on both sides of the baseline on average.
Plain t assumes meetings are independent; the NW lag-3 t is reported as a check but is not the bar.

Quintile sort among names with a finite signal (>= 100 required); LONG top quintile, SHORT bottom quintile, equal weight; hold close me[t] -> close me[t+1]; a name that stops trading is held at its last close. DISCLOSED DEVIATION FROM R161 (2026-09-23): the $5 price floor is replaced by a 60-day MEDIAN dollar-volume >= $5M screen. The floor was a look-ahead on an adjustment=all panel (a pre-split price is divided by later split ratios, so whether a name cleared $5 in 2017 depended on splits that had not happened yet). The replacement admits genuinely low-priced but liquid names (sub-$5 stocks with >= $5M/day) that R161 excluded, so this universe is not identical to R161's and INTRA results are not a strict decomposition of R161's MOM12_1 row.

Panel is anomaly-cache-v2: 309 names with a >+300% one-day move are kept up to the day before that move and then leave the panel like a delisting (held at last close); v1 dropped them entirely (a look-ahead). The jump rule itself is a data-quality heuristic chosen on the whole 2016-2026 sample; a genuine >+300% day is also cut, so the panel slightly under-represents extreme winners after their jump.

Dividend adjustment (adjustment=all) still scales historical prices by later dividends; dollar volume (price x share volume) is invariant to split adjustment but NOT exactly to dividend adjustment, so the $5M median screen carries a small residual dependence on later dividends (a few percent for high-yield names).
Cost model is a flat 0.25% per unit turnover; no short-borrow fee, which understates the short leg's cost for hard-to-borrow losers.
The paper documents the effect largely on pre-2020 US data; post-publication decay (McLean-Pontiff) is the default expectation for the holdout.
R161 already read plain 12-1 momentum (MOM12_1) on the same panel and discovery window; INTRA is a decomposition of that signal, so its multiplicity family overlaps R161's momentum rows.

v2 panel truncation censors the +300% jump of a held name (flatters the short leg). preregistered.expectation: Low. The paper finds a positive spread in the long CRSP sample, but this test uses a liquid top-1,500 universe, a noisier consolidated open, and a fully post-publication holdout, after costs. Prior: small positive gross (well under 0.5%/month), net near zero; probability of clearing net NW t >= 1.70 with both halves positive roughly 10-20%.
knownWeaknesses: The raw monthly frequency is used, as briefed; the paper's headline analysis may also use a variant (e.g. an abnormal frequency relative to the stock's own history) and firm-level controls in Fama-MacBeth regressions — a quintile sort on raw frequency is a simplification.

Opening price is the Alpaca SIP daily bar open (first consolidated print), not the primary-exchange opening auction price; the overnight/intraday split is noisier than CRSP-based open prices, which biases the signal toward noise and the test toward failure.

Universe: the $5 price floor was REMOVED (2026-09-23) because adjustment=all price levels at t depend on later splits (look-ahead); it is replaced by a split-invariant liquidity screen (60-day median dollar volume >= $5M) plus the top 1,500 by 60-day mean dollar volume. This admits low-priced but liquid names the old floor excluded, so the universe differs from R161's. It is still large and liquid; the paper reports the effect is stronger where arbitrage is costlier (small, illiquid, high-uncertainty firms), which this universe mostly excludes.

Dollar volume is split-invariant but not perfectly dividend-invariant: adjustment=all back-adjusts prices for later dividends without scaling volume, so historical dollar volume is shaded down by the cumulative future dividend yield (a few percent), which can move names near the $5M median cut or the top-1,500 boundary.

FREQ is a discrete count ratio (hits over ~19-23 days), so many ties sit at quintile boundaries; ties are broken by a fixed symbol hash (not size, not return), which adds some arbitrary membership noise.
Post-publication: the working paper circulated before 2022 and the JFE article appeared in 2022; the whole holdout is post-publication, so decay is expected.

Panel v2 (anomaly-cache-v2): 8,144 names (2,715 delisted kept); 309 names are TRUNCATED at their first >+300% one-day move rather than dropped, and 612 remain too short to include; survivorship is reduced, not eliminated. The truncation date is set by that future jump, so a name held into its jump month is held at its last close before the jump: the +300% day itself is excluded from whichever leg held it (a right-tail outcome removed; direction of bias on the spread is unknown). Adjusted (adjustment=all) open and close share the same daily factor, so ex-dividend and split days are handled.
Flat 25 bp per unit of turnover; no borrow fee or hard-to-borrow constraint on the short leg; equal weighting.
The final holdout month (2026-09) is partial (through 2026-09-22); the holdout has about 57 months, so power against a small true effect is limited.
v2 truncation censoring: only AMC (2021-01) and WOLF (2025-09) were in the universe in their cut month; disclosed.
Dollar volume on adjusted prices embeds later dividends; disclosed.

preregistered.expectation: Prior: weak-positive gross concentration (a few bps/day) consistent with the Etula et al. cash-demand story, but likely below the 1.70 bar at n=56 after decay; a DID NOT PASS is the base case.
knownWeaknesses: Single instrument, one number per month: ~60 discovery and 56 holdout units, so power is low — a true effect of a few bps/day can fail the 1.70 bar.
The effect is famous and documented since 1987; post-publication decay (McLean & Pontiff 2016) predicts a smaller holdout effect than the literature.
The window here is 6 days (-3..+3); the classic Lakonishok-Smidt / Ariel window is -1..+3. This is a fixed choice per the brief, not tuned, but it differs from some papers.

The statistic compares TOM to non-TOM days of the SAME month, so it measures return concentration, not the tradable long-TOM/cash P&L; the tradable TOM-window return is reported as weightless context only.
Holdout 2022-2026 contains the 2022 bear market and a rate regime unlike the 1926-2005 samples of the source papers; month-end rebalancing flows (pension, index, 60/40) may now be front-run.
Cost of 2 bps round trip ignores the opportunity cost of cash vs T-bills for a standalone strategy; irrelevant to the difference statistic.
Holiday-shortened or event-closed months (e.g. 2018-12-05, 2025-01-09 closures) shift calendar positions by a day; handled by using SPY's actual trading days.
The 2022-01 holdout unit uses the last three trading days of 2021-12 (discovery calendar) — data flows forward only, never holdout into discovery.

Coverage check tolerates missing weekdays (re-review 2026-09-23); verified the same night that SPY daily bars cover all 2,506 official Alpaca calendar sessions 2016-10-01..2026-09-22 with none missing, so the shift cannot occur on this data.

preregistered.expectation: Skeptical. Huang et al. (2020) find own-asset time-series predictability weak once the pooled mean is removed, and trend-following had a lost decade 2012-2021 outside 2014 and 2020. The holdout contains 2022 (a strong trend year: short bonds, long dollar/commodities), which favours the rule, and 2023-2025 whipsaws, which hurt it. Prior: net mean near zero or slightly positive, NW t well under 1.70, most likely DID NOT PASS; a PASS would most plausibly be carried by 2022 alone, which the both-halves rule is there to catch.
knownWeaknesses: Alpaca SIP history starts 2016-01-04, so the 12-month lookback first exists at the 2017-01-31 formation: discovery covers Feb 2017..Dec 2021 (59 months), not Jan 2017.

The spread equals -2 x the vol-scaled return of the ETFs currently flagged negative, so its power comes only from months with short flags; in long bull stretches most ETFs are long and the spread is near zero.
Signal uses raw total return, not return in excess of cash (MOP use excess returns). With cash near 5% in 2023-2024, a bond ETF slightly below cash reads positive here and negative in MOP.

16 highly correlated ETFs (3 US equity, 2 foreign equity, 4 bond, 2 credit-ish, 3 commodity, REIT, dollar) are far fewer independent bets than the 58 futures of MOP; ETF index-tracking products (USO, UNG, DBC) carry roll costs baked into their prices.
Holdout is 57 monthly observations; NW t with n~57 and lag 3 has mild size distortion (controls measure it on the bootstrap null).
Short leg assumes free borrow and no short-rebate drag; cost of 5 bps per unit turnover is generous for these liquid ETFs but excludes borrow fees (notably UNG/USO at times).
Monthly rebalance on the first session's open, not the month-end close; a 1-session implementation lag versus the paper's month-end execution.
Vol scaling uses a simple 60-day sample sd, not MOP's exponentially weighted estimator (60-day center of mass).

(a) Leak test: iid bootstrap null (each stock's daily gross returns resampled WITH replacement inside its listed span, arithmetic drift removed, close path rebuilt, rbar recomputed from bootstrapped returns; seed 1601). The bootstrap pool and the drift estimate use ONLY returns dated <= 2021-12-31; every return/close after that date is blanked in the null, and names with fewer than 20 pre-cut returns are blanked rather than left on their real returns. GROSS |NW t| < 2 required. In the null the entry is the bootstrapped close at t (real opens belong to the real path). (b) Positive control: sort on the realised holding return itself (peek); GROSS NW t >= 5 required. Both bars compared UNROUNDED. Both must pass before --discovery runs. Written to data/hunt/SALIENCE-controls.json (spec SALIENCE-controls-v2, with raw t values).
preregistered.costModel: R161: 0.25% x (long-leg turnover + short-leg turnover) per month; turnover = share of each leg's names new versus the previous month's leg; first month charged as full build (turnover 2).

decisionRule.pass: A clearing hypothesis earns a forward paper test (registered separately) — nothing is traded on a backtest.
decisionRule.fail: DID NOT PASS: closed on these data.

preregistered.readCondition: node backend/hunt/SALIENCE.js --controls; --discovery; --holdout (once).
preregistered.expectation: Weak. The published spread is concentrated in small/illiquid stocks and overlaps short-term reversal and MAX; in a liquid top-1,500 universe with next-open entry and 0.25% per unit turnover (ST quintiles turn over heavily month to month, likely 1.2-1.6 of 2), the net holdout spread most likely sits near zero. Prior probability of PASS at t >= 1.70 with both halves positive: roughly 10-15%.
knownWeaknesses: Universe is the top 1,500 by dollar volume behind a split-invariant liquidity screen (60-day median dollar volume >= $5M); Cosemans-Frehen report the effect strongest in small, illiquid, high-limits-to-arbitrage stocks, so the liquid universe may shrink or kill it.

The dollar-volume screen REPLACES the former close >= $5 price floor (removed 2026-09-23 because adjusted price levels at t depend on later splits: a look-ahead). Without a price floor, low-priced names with enough dollar volume are eligible; this departs from R161's original eligibility and admits some sub-$5 stocks (wider spreads, which the flat 0.25% cost may understate).

Panel is anomaly-cache-v2: 309 names are truncated the day before their first +300% one-day jump (treated as a recycled-ticker splice or bad adjustment) and then leave the panel like a delisting, held at their last close. The truncation date is itself defined by a later price, so a name held through a genuine +300% day is exited at the prior close: this caps a long-leg winner and spares a short-leg loser (a small bias toward the long-low / short-high spread only if such jumps fall more on high-ST names).

ST is strongly related to the 1-month return (short-term reversal) and to MAX/skewness lottery measures; this test does not orthogonalise ST against STREV1M, MAX or IVOL (all in R161), so a PASS would not separate salience from reversal.
Entry at the next open (not the formation close) deliberately forgoes the bid-ask bounce component of short-term reversal; this differs from R161's close-to-close convention and from the paper.
Market reference rbar is the equal-weight mean of the survivorship-reduced panel (common stocks only, |r| < 0.5 guard), not CRSP's full cross-section.

Paper parameters theta = 0.1 and delta = 0.7 were taken from the brief and the Bordalo-Gennaioli-Shleifer calibration; the full paper text was not retrievable here (web search confirmed only the abstract-level construction: salient daily returns over the past month, high ST -> low future return).
Tie rule (mean weight over tied positions) is our choice; the paper does not specify one. Ties are essentially absent for real returns.
Equal-weight long-short spread; value-weighted results in the paper are weaker. Short-leg borrow costs are not modelled beyond the flat 0.25% turnover charge.
Holdout's last month (2026-09) is partial (through 2026-09-22), as in R161.
Single bootstrap seed for the leak test: about 5% chance of a false FAIL on pure noise.
v2 truncation censoring: only AMC (2021-01) and WOLF (2025-09) were in the universe in their cut month; disclosed.

Dollar volume on adjustment=all prices embeds the cumulative factor of dividends paid after t (volume is split-adjusted only); universe membership near the $5M screen and the rank-1,500 margin depends mildly on future payouts; not removable without per-name dividend history (re-review 2026-09-23).

preregistered.rule: Panel data/anomaly-cache-v2 (adjusted daily close/open/volume, look-ahead-safe truncation). Universe on day t: >= 260 prior closes and 20-day median dollar volume >= $25M. Signal at close t: (a) 12-1 month return (close[t-21]/close[t-252]-1) in the top 30% of the day's universe; (b) close above both its 50- and 200-day averages; (c) close 5%-20% below its 252-day highest close; (d) at least one close-to-close gain >= +5% in the last 10 sessions; (e) RSI(14) between 45 and 70. Selection: on the first trading day of each week, up to 3 new names from the prior session's signals, highest 12-1 return first, not already held; entry at that day's open; max 40 open positions. Exit: the first close >= entry x 1.15 -> sell at the next open; else 365 calendar days -> next open; a name leaving the panel is sold at its last close. No stop. Book: 40 equal slots (1/40 of equity each at entry, cash otherwise); costs 10 bps per side.

preregistered.multiplicityFamily: LVN-4 — swing size k in {3, 5} x ATR(14) on 5-minute bars, x venue {US index ETFs pooled (SPY, QQQ, IWM), BTC/USD}. Primary: k=3 on the ETF pool.
rule: Bars: 5-minute. ETFs: Alpaca SIP, regular session only, 2018-01-02..2026-08-31. BTC/USD: Coinbase 5-minute candles, 24h, 2021-01-01..2026-08-31.

Swing: a ZigZag on 5-minute closes with reversal threshold k x ATR(14). The CURRENT swing runs from the last confirmed pivot A to the running extreme B since A, and is live once |B - A| >= k x ATR at B.
Profile: every bar from A to B spreads its volume evenly across its high-low range into 24 equal price bins over [min(A,B), max(A,B)].
LVN: among the bins between 20% and 80% of the swing, the one with the least volume, and only if that volume is below half the median bin. No qualifying bin, no trade.

Entry: a resting limit at the LVN bin's midpoint, placed at the bar that sets B. It fills when a later bar trades through it, at the limit, or at that bar's open if the bar gaps past it. Direction = the swing's direction (up-swing -> long).
HTF bias: longs only if the last completed 1-hour close is above its 50-period EMA; shorts only if below.
Cancel: a new extreme beyond B (the swing extends; recompute), a confirmed reversal pivot, or 15:30 ET for ETFs.
Stop: the LVN bin's far edge minus 1 x ATR(14) for a long (mirror for a short). Target: B. Both tested on later bars; if a bar touches both, the stop wins.
Exit: stop, target, or flat at 15:55 ET for ETFs (no overnight holds); BTC has a 24-hour time exit. One open trade per instrument.
Costs: ETFs $0.02 per share round trip plus half the typical spread (1 cent) each side, in R. BTC 10 bps per side.
preregistered.statistic: Net R per trade. Per SESSION (ET date; the ETF pool sums its three instruments), the mean net R of that day's trades; t over sessions. Split: discovery 2018-2022 (ETF) / 2021-2022 (BTC); primary read on the HOLDOUT 2023-01-01..2026-08-31.

preregistered.multiplicityFamily: CHATTER-16 — legs {S1 Reddit stock spike, S2 Stocktwits new-trending, S3 Reddit crypto spike} x horizons {S1,S2: 1/5/20 trading days; S3: 1/5 days} = 8 cells, each read two-sided (momentum or fade) = 16. Primary: S1 at 5 days.
rule: Snapshot for day D = data/social-mentions/<D>.json (ET date). A name enters on D only if it is a US-listed stock or ETF with an Alpaca SIP daily bar on D and a raw close >= $2 (crypto: a Coinbase <COIN>-USD product).
S1 (Reddit stock spike): ApeWisdom all-stocks row with mentions >= 20, rank <= 100 and mentions >= 3 x max(mentions_24h_ago, 3).
S2 (Stocktwits new-trending): in D's trending list and absent from the previous recorded day's list (first eligible D = 2026-09-25).
S3 (Reddit crypto spike): ApeWisdom all-crypto row with mentions >= 10 and mentions >= 3 x max(mentions_24h_ago, 3); ticker XXX.X -> Coinbase XXX-USD.
Entry: stocks at the next session's open (D+1 open, raw SIP); exit at the close h trading days later. Crypto: 00:00 UTC open of the UTC day after the snapshot; exit h days later at 00:00 UTC.

Control (stocks): for each signal name, 5 names drawn at random (seed = hash of D and the name) from D's ApeWisdom all-stocks rows that did NOT spike and pass the same listing and price screen — already retail-followed names, so the test isolates the SPIKE, not being talked about at all. Crypto control: BTC.
preregistered.statistic: Per signal day and cell: mean over that day's signal names of (signal return - mean control return). Newey-West t over signal days with lag h-1 (overlapping holds). Two-sided: a positive t says chatter predicts continuation, a negative t says it marks the top.

decisionRule.pass: A cell whose |t| >= bar with >= 40 signal days: register a forward paper test of that direction (buy or fade) through the Alpaca mirror, operator's word.
decisionRule.fail: DID NOT PASS: retail chatter spikes carry no measurable next-day to next-month information beyond being talked about; the recorder continues as data.

The rule was written to avoid discretion (a mechanism table fixed in advance, a numeric t threshold on pre-2023 data, a seeded tie-break), but the mechanism table itself was written by someone who had read the sealed verdicts.
Library streams are regenerated by emitters, not by the sealed scripts themselves; a stream whose reproduction check fails is excluded by rule (c), which may drop a real edge.

Event strategies (month-end, FOMC, expiry) are active a few days a month; equal risk sizes them by their active-day volatility, so a combination can hold much idle cash. That is a real feature of the book, not a flaw of the test.
US-equity and crypto calendars are mixed; crypto dates are UTC days, SPY dates are sessions — the regressors are slightly asynchronous.
Alpha betas are estimated on the holdout itself (standard for an alpha test, but the betas are not point-in-time).
The t >= 1.0 threshold is permissive by design (weak edges are the point); the protection is the holdout, the best-of-2 bar and two library-based controls.
Holdout 2023-2026 is one regime (a strong equity bull market with a 2025 tariff shock); few independent regimes.

controls.shuffle: component labels shuffled across dates: on every holdout date each of the k component slots is filled by a distinct library strategy ('ok', live on that date) drawn at random; same weighting (a slot's σ is the drawn strategy's own point-in-time σ) and same alpha t. 200 seeded draws; the verdict variant's true t must be strictly greater than the draws' 95th percentile.

controls.peek: positive control: the selected components with every daily return replaced by max(r, 0) (outcome look-ahead), same weights; alpha t must be >= 3 or the pipeline is not trusted (validity gate).

ensembleSpecDetail.validity: Seal only if: k >= 2 components selected; SPY and BTC regressors present on every holdout date they should be; both control distributions hold 200 finite draws; peek t >= 3. k < 2 = VOID (reported, not sealed, the registration stays open for a larger library).
