rule: Universe (fixed, current large caps + index ETFs — survivorship disclosed): SPY, QQQ, IWM, AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, AMZN, META, GOOGL, TSLA, AMD, AVGO, NFLX, JPM, BAC, XOM, CVX, UNH, LLY, COST, WMT, HD, V, MA, ORCL, CRM, ADBE, INTC, CSCO, PEP, KO, DIS, BA. Alpaca SIP bars, regular session only, 2018-01-02..2026-08-31; 15-minute bars fetched directly (timeframe 15Min), 1-hour bars aggregated from them on the clock hour.
Indicators per timeframe: session-anchored VWAP (typical price x volume from 09:30), EMA(9) of closes (continuous across sessions), ATR(14).
STEP 1 acceleration: bar s's high is at least 2.0 x ATR(14) above BOTH that bar's VWAP and EMA(9), and is the highest high of the last 10 bars.
STEP 2 the candle: bar s is a shooting star — upper wick >= 2 x |body|, upper wick >= 50% of the bar's range, lower wick <= 25% of the range.
STEP 3 trapped buyers: bar s's volume >= 1.5 x the mean volume of the prior 20 bars.

EXECUTION: a sell-stop one cent below bar s's low, live for the next 3 bars; fills at the stop, or at a bar's open if it gaps below. Stop: one cent above bar s's high. Target: entry - 2R (R = stop - entry). Stop and target tested on later bars (stop first if one bar touches both); flat at 15:55 ET if neither. One open trade per symbol. Mirror long: all conditions reflected (low stretched below VWAP and EMA9, hammer with lower wick >= 2 x body, buy-stop above the high).
Costs per trade: $0.02 per share round trip plus 0.03% of price per side for stop-order slippage, expressed in R.
preregistered.statistic: Net R per trade; per ET session the mean net R of that session's trades; t over sessions (Newey-West lag 1). Discovery 2018-2021 inspected only for pipeline sanity; the verdict is the holdout. Reported: 3R target variant, win rate, trades per month, gross.

rule: Universe: the 80 names in data/r147-earnings (built for R147, not chosen for this test).
Contract filter on signal day d: DTE 1..45 calendar days; OTM by at least 2% of the underlying's RAW close on d (call strike >= 1.02 x close, put strike <= 0.98 x close) and at most 25%.
Size filter: contract volume on d >= 500 AND premium = volume x price x 100 >= $500,000.
Direction per name-day: net premium = sum(call whale premium) - sum(put whale premium) over qualifying contracts; > 0 bullish (long), < 0 bearish (short). One signal per name-day.

Trade: enter the underlying at the OPEN of d+1, exit at the CLOSE of the 5th trading day counted from d+1 (d+5 close). Signed raw return (long for bullish, short for bearish), split-adjusted prices, minus 20 bps round trip.

Unusual (R271 version, no open-interest history on Alpaca): volume on d >= 5 x the contract's mean daily volume over the 10 prior trading days (days with no bar count as 0) AND the contract has at least 3 prior trading days of bars. Price = the bar's volume-weighted price (vw).

Collection: contracts from Alpaca /v2/options/contracts (status inactive + active), expirations 2024-02-01..2026-09-25, strikes within +/-30% of the underlying's raw close 45 calendar days before expiry (or its first available close); daily bars from /v1beta1/options/bars. rule: Weekly. Signal from closes up to the LAST session of each week; position held from the NEXT session's OPEN to the open of the session after the following week's last session (open-to-open). Alpaca SIP daily bars, adjustment=all (total return).

V2 TREASURIES: if IEF's (10y proxy) return over the prior 20 sessions (the prior month) > TLT's (30y proxy) -> hold SPY next week; else hold IEF.

V3 LUMBER/GOLD: if lumber futures (Yahoo LBR=F continuous, close) return over the prior 65 sessions (13 weeks) > GLD's -> hold SPY next week; else hold IEF. Window starts when 65 sessions of LBR=F exist (from ~2022-11).

preregistered.rule: Underlying: SPX same-day expiry (SPXW). Entry clock: one iron condor per hour from 10:00 to 15:00 ET (six/day), never closer than 30 minutes apart; skip an entry if the prior hour's condor is still open on both sides and would push gross risk past the cap. Structure: sell the put and the call whose delta is closest to 12 (band 10-15), buy wings 30 SPX points further out; if the two sides' credits differ by more than 25%, move the richer side's short strike one strike toward ATM so credits are ~equal. Target credit per side $1.00-$2.00 (x100). Management: a separate stop on EACH short leg at a mark equal to the TOTAL condor credit (so one side stopping out ~breaks even on the whole trade); profit target: buy back a short leg at $0.05; otherwise hold to expiry. Stops tighten linearly after 13:00 to (credit x remaining-time fraction, floor 0.5x credit). Sizing: 1 condor per $25k NAV per entry; daily loss cap 2% NAV (no new entries after). Cost: charged at full crossing of the modelled SPX bid-ask per leg at entry, at stop, and at target; $0.65/contract commission + SPX fees.
preregistered.mechanism: Paid liquidity provision in 0DTE SPX: sells gamma to same-day directional buyers (retail 0DTE call/put buyers and dealers hedging) at 10-15 delta, six times a day, and pays for tail risk with a stop that is itself a bet on continuous intraday markets. The breakeven stop converts the structure into a short-strangle-with-a-trailing-cutoff; the payer is the 0DTE option buyer's expected loss (documented at the aggregate level by Cboe/academic 0DTE studies). Structural, but the stop pays the spread twice on 60% of trades.

preregistered.rule: DATA: Alpaca SIP historical TRADES (older than 15 minutes, so allowed on our plan) for SPY and QQQ, regular hours 09:30:00-15:59:59 ET. Trades carrying SIP condition codes for out-of-sequence, extended-hours/form-T, derivatively-priced, or average-price prints are excluded; the builder fixes and lists the exact codes in the script header before the read. SIGNING (tick rule, trades only; no quotes): a trade above the last different price is a buy (+size), below it a sell (-size), equal = the previous sign; the first trade of the day is unsigned. CUMULATIVE DELTA CD(t) = sum of signed size since 09:30. 5-minute bars (OHLC) are built from the same trades. SIGNAL (bearish divergence): at the close of a 5-minute bar ending between 10:00 and 15:00 ET whose HIGH exceeds every earlier high of the session, if CD at this bar's close is BELOW CD at the close of the bar that set the previous session high -> SHORT at the next bar's open. Mirror (bullish divergence): new session LOW with CD ABOVE its value at the previous session low -> LONG at the next bar's open. At most one signal per side per session (the first). EXIT: the close of the 6th bar after entry (30 minutes) or the 15:55 ET price, whichever comes first. No stop, no target. COST: $0.01 per share per side (spread + fees) charged on every entry and exit. WINDOW FALLBACK (declared now): if fetching the full two years of trades would take more than 3 hours, the read uses the most recent 250 sessions ending 2026-09-29; the builder says which was used.
preregistered.statistic: Per-session net return of that session's divergence trades (sessions with >= 1 signal), one-sample t over SESSIONS, per symbol.

controls.control: SAME rule WITHOUT the delta condition: fade the first new session high/low after 10:00 regardless of CD. The divergence arm's mean must EXCEED the control's mean, or the delta adds nothing.
controls.placebo: Delta labels shuffled across the session's new-extreme events (>= 500 draws): the true divergence mean must beat the placebo's 95th percentile.
controls.halves: first/second half of the window must share the sign.

decisionRule.pass: PASS only if t >= bar AND the divergence mean beats the no-delta control AND the placebo p95 AND both halves share the sign. A PASS proposes a forward paper test (Alpaca paper, same rule) — operator's call.
decisionRule.fail: DID NOT PASS: aggressor-signed delta adds nothing tradeable at this horizon on the index ETFs; recorded with the control comparison.

preregistered.name: Fade YouTube stock-pick calls: bet against the direction of single-stock calls in the titles of the most-subscribed stock-pick channels
preregistered.status: REGISTERED 2026-10-01 — historical, read once; builder assigned
preregistered.parent: Operator 2026-10-01 (Agent Reach discussion): 'how do we use it to make money' -> 'yes install it and register the test'. Motivation: academic work on finfluencers (StockTwits) reporting that most are worse than random and that a contrarian strategy earned positive abnormal returns; never tested here.
preregistered.multiplicityFamily: YT-FADE — R303 alone; 2 cells (hold 5 / hold 20 sessions). FOLLOW is the mirror of FADE, not a separate cell.
preregistered.rule: TOOL: yt-dlp only (official build), anonymous. NO cookies, NO login, NO proxy; if YouTube answers with a sign-in / 'confirm you're not a bot' wall the run STOPS and the test is CANNOT MEASURE (never bypassed). CHANNELS (frozen by rule, chosen before any outcome is seen): run yt-dlp search 'ytsearch100:' for each of these queries — 'stocks to buy now', 'best stocks to buy', 'stock picks this week', 'stocks I'm buying', 'growth stocks to buy', 'stock to buy before it explodes'. Collect the uploading channels; keep channels that appear in >= 2 of the 6 result lists; drop news/media outlets (CNBC, Bloomberg, Yahoo Finance, Fox Business, WSJ, Reuters, MarketWatch, Benzinga, Barron's, Investor's Business Daily, Morningstar, The Motley Fool's corporate channel is KEPT as it publishes picks) and channels with < 100 videos; rank by subscriber count (yt-dlp channel_follower_count); take the top 20. The list is written to data/training/r303/channels.json BEFORE any title is parsed. VIDEOS: every upload of those channels (long-form and Shorts) whose upload timestamp falls in 2023-01-01..2026-08-28. Titles via --flat-playlist; the precise timestamp (yt-dlp 'timestamp', else 'release_timestamp', else upload_date at 00:00 ET + 1 day) fetched per candidate video. CALLS (from the TITLE only, mechanical, frozen before returns): tickers = $TICKER tokens, or uppercase 2-5 letter tokens that are US common-stock symbols (Alpaca assets, active + inactive; ETFs/ETNs/funds/trusts excluded) and not on a common-word stoplist (A, I, IT, ON, NOW, ALL, ARE, BIG, CAN, FOR, NEW, ONE, SO, AI, DD, CEO, USA, GDP, CPI, FED, IPO, ETF, ATH, EPS, YOLO, etc.), or a company-name match (first distinctive word of the Alpaca asset name, >= 4 letters, not a dictionary word). Direction: SHORT-call if the title has a negative keyword (sell, selling, sold, short, bearish, crash, avoid, warning, dump, overvalued, bubble, collapse, 'don't buy', 'stay away', 'get out'); else LONG-call if it has a positive keyword (buy, buying, bought, bullish, 'to buy', load, loading, accumulate, undervalued, explode, skyrocket, soar, moon, '10x', '100x', millionaire, rally, breakout, 'next nvidia', 'huge upside', 'all in', 'best stock'); else no call. A title naming several tickers makes one call per ticker. Index/ETF-only titles make no call. PRECISION GATE (before any return is computed): the builder hand-labels a random sample of 200 extracted calls (ticker AND direction). Precision < 80% = CANNOT MEASURE. The extractor is frozen after this check; no change after returns are seen. TRADE: entry = the first regular-session OPEN strictly after the upload timestamp; exit = the CLOSE of entry session + 4 (cell H5) or + 19 (cell H20). FADE return = -direction x (stock return - SPY return over the same open->close span). Prices: Alpaca SIP daily, adjustment=all; delisted names kept (inactive assets). Calls on a name already called by the same channel in the previous 5 sessions are dropped (duplicate). COST: 0.20% round trip on every call, plus short borrow at 3%/yr pro rata on the short leg (FADE of a long call is short the stock).
preregistered.statistic: Weekly calendar-time fade return: for each ENTRY week, mean over channels with calls that week of (mean net FADE return of that channel's calls entered that week). One-sample t over weeks 2023-01..2026-08; Newey-West lag 1 for H5, lag 4 for H20 (overlapping holds). Cell = H5 or H20; the headline is the better cell (bar is best-of-2).

controls.placebo: PLACEBO: each call replaced by a random US common stock from the same 60-session dollar-volume decile, same entry timestamp and direction; 500 draws of the whole call set; the observed weekly-mean fade must exceed the placebo p95.
controls.halves: First and second half of the weeks with calls, reported; both must share the sign.
controls.mirror: FOLLOW (= -FADE before costs, charged its own costs) reported beside, not a cell.
controls.concentration: share of calls and of the fade P&L in the 10 most-called tickers, and per-channel fade means, reported (no selection on them).

decisionRule.pass: PASS only if the better cell's net t >= bar AND the placebo is beaten AND both halves are positive. A PASS proposes a FORWARD paper test on the same 20 channels' new uploads (operator's call); nothing is adopted or funded.
decisionRule.fail: DID NOT PASS: recorded with the numbers; the card closes unless materially new evidence appears.
decisionRule.cannotMeasure: CANNOT MEASURE if: a YouTube sign-in/bot wall blocks the pull (never bypassed); < 1,000 calls in the window; < 100 weeks with calls; or extraction precision < 80% on the 200-call hand check.

knownWeaknesses: Deleted videos: channels remove embarrassing calls, so the surviving record flatters the callers. This biases AGAINST the fade (a PASS is conservative) and FOR the follow mirror.
Channel survivorship: today's most-subscribed channels are survivors; same direction as above.

Title edits: YouTubers retitle videos after the fact ('I told you...'); we only see current titles. Edits after a correct call bias against the fade; edits that add a ticker after a move could add look-ahead in either direction. Disclosed, not measurable.
Title-only calls miss calls made only inside the video; transcripts are not used (cost and noise).

Short borrow on hyped small caps can cost far more than 3%/yr and some names are not shortable: this flatters the fade. The builder reports the fade restricted to the top-1,000 names by dollar volume beside the headline.
Heavy concentration in a few names (NVDA, TSLA, PLTR...) is likely: weekly clustering handles time, not cross-name concentration; the concentration control is reported.
The six search queries and the top-20 cut are choices; they are fixed here before any data, and no other list will be tried.

preregistered.rule: Breaker as configured at registration: lib/risk-policy.js breakerMode 'observe'; capped-exposure ceiling $25,000 (25% of the $100k book); realized day loss -$2,000. HALT DAY = an ET session with a HALT/WOULD-HALT event in data/circuit-breaker.json; halt time = the day's FIRST event. REFUSED-IF-ENFORCED tickets = canonical SIGNAL tickets (lib/reconcile.js cleanEraLedger().signals, assertReconciled) opened that day at or after the halt time. A day enters once it is 7 calendar days old (about 5 sessions, so its tickets have settled); days with no such ticket are counted separately and carry no value.

controls.timeMatched: signal tickets opened >= 09:45 ET on non-halt days (per-day means) — separates the breaker condition from time of day
controls.sameDay: tickets opened before the halt on the same day
controls.marketDay: CONTROL tickets after the halt (the market-day effect; if they lose as much, the loss is the day, not the signals)
controls.dollars: refused-ticket P&L in dollars beside R

bar.oneSided: negative: verdict ENFORCE WARRANTED needs t <= -tRequired

preregistered.configGuard: A halt event naming another ceiling or loss threshold, or breakerMode other than 'observe', freezes the day count at the first night the change is seen (persisted). The read is then taken on the days before it, or the operator mints a successor.

decisionRule.pass: ENFORCE WARRANTED: t <= -bar over the first 30 halt days. Recommends switching breakerMode to 'enforce' — the operator's call (it also cuts the board's evidence by the refused share).
decisionRule.fail: NOT WARRANTED: observe mode stays; the breaker remains a reported risk flag. The operator may still enforce on risk grounds — this test only answers whether the refused tickets lose.

Equity rMult is gross of cost (2026-09-30 audit settle#3): refused equity tickets look better than they are, which biases AGAINST 'enforce warranted'.
Tickets still open after 7 days (long R14-style holds) are not in A_d; if losers are held longer, A_d is flattered. The output reports per-day counts.
Enforcing would also refuse CONTROL tickets, cutting every board test's sample; that cost is not in this statistic and belongs to the operator's decision.
Halts cluster on high-exposure days that may be bad market days in general; the control-tickets diagnostic is reported to separate that.

preregistered.rule: Population: every R21 wing (live and R21 shadows) in data/wing-marks.jsonl. Window E = the last session before the monthly expiration (third Friday) close -> the first session after it close; window C = the same weekdays one week earlier (sessions found from the marks themselves, so a holiday shifts to the adjacent session). A wing enters a window if it has an RTH mark on both end dates and expires AFTER the window's end date. dR = (last RTH mid on the start date - last RTH mid on the end date) / spread width (strikes parsed from the OCC symbols); positive = the short wing gained. Per cell (CALL wings, PUT wings) and expiration: D = mean dR(E) - mean dR(C), only when each window has >= 5 wings of that cell. No orders, no new positions: it reads marks the book already records.
preregistered.statistic: Per cell: one-sample t of D over monthly expirations from 2026-10 (unit: expirations). Best-of-2 cells; positive direction only.

controls.pairing: window C (one week earlier, same weekdays) is the control inside every observation
controls.liveOnly: D on live wings only (shadows excluded) reported beside
controls.counts: wings per window per cell reported

decisionRule.pass: PASS if either cell's t >= bar with a positive mean over the first 12 expirations. Proposes an R21 timing rule (favour holding short wings across the monthly-expiration weekend) as a registered OP proposal — the operator's call; nothing changes in the sleeve automatically.
decisionRule.fail: DID NOT PASS: R299's effect does not show in the wings we sell; R299 stays a single-stock finding with no use in this book.

R299 measured ATM next-month delta-hedged calls; R21 sells un-hedged 25-delta weekly verticals, so the dR also carries the underlying's weekend move. Pairing against the prior weekend removes the average weekend effect but not this weekend's market move; that is noise, not bias.

preregistered.rule: DATA: Coinbase Exchange public hourly candles (api.exchange.coinbase.com/products/{BTC-USD,ETH-USD}/candles, granularity 3600; open/high/low/close/base volume), UTC hours; gaps left as gaps. PIVOTS: an hourly bar is a pivot HIGH if its high is the highest of the 24 bars before and the 24 after (pivot LOW likewise with lows); a pivot becomes KNOWN only 24 bars after it (no look-ahead). Pivot weight = that bar's base volume divided by the asset's trailing 30-day median hourly volume (so regimes are comparable). STRENGTH PROFILE at hour t (built only from pivots known by t-1): price bins of 0.1%; each pivot adds its weight to every bin within +/-1% of its price (overlap summed); weight x 2 while the pivot is UNTESTED (price has not traded through the pivot price since it became known), x 1 after the first touch; exponential decay with a 4-day half-life from the pivot time. Normalised by the maximum bin within +/-10% of the prior close. LEVEL = a local maximum of the profile with normalised strength >= 0.5. The REFERENCE resistance (support) at t = the strongest level above (below) the prior close within 5%. CELL REV (levels hold): the first hour whose high reaches the reference resistance (low reaches the reference support) since that level became the reference -> FADE from the level price: short at a resistance, long at a support; exit at the close 24 hours later. One event per level per UTC day. CELL BRK (breaks continue): the first hourly CLOSE more than 0.25% beyond the reference level -> enter at that close in the break direction; exit at the close 24 hours later. One event per level per UTC day. COST: 0.20% round trip per event (taker-like spot cost on Coinbase), no funding (spot).
preregistered.statistic: Per UTC day with events: mean net event return (BTC and ETH pooled). One-sample t over days, registered window 2021-01..2026-09; best-of-2 cells.

preregistered.rule: UNIVERSE (fixed today): the 32 non-stablecoin USD pairs Alpaca can trade on 2026-10-01 — BTC ETH SOL XRP DOGE ADA AVAX LINK LTC BCH DOT UNI AAVE SHIB PEPE BONK WIF TRUMP HYPE RENDER POL YFI XTZ BAT CRV SKY FIL GRT LDO SUSHI ARB ONDO — priced from Coinbase Exchange hourly candles (X-USD); a coin Coinbase does not list, or before its first Coinbase candle, simply has no events (reported). SURGE (the wave starting), on the close of hour t, all inputs from bars <= t: hourly return >= 3 x the coin's trailing 7-day (168 h) hourly return standard deviation, AND hourly volume >= 3 x its trailing 7-day median hourly volume, AND the close is above the prior 24-hour high. At most one entry per coin per 24 hours. ENTER LONG at the close of hour t (taker). EXITS (the bail), evaluated on hourly closes from t+1, hard cap 48 hours:   TRAIL: exit at the first close more than 1.5 x the entry-time 24-hour ATR (hourly true ranges, mean over 24 h) below the highest close since entry;   FADE: exit at the first hour whose volume falls below 1.0 x the trailing 7-day median hourly volume (the wave losing participation), or at TRAIL's stop if that comes first;   T6: exit at the close of t+6 (a fixed early bail). COST: 0.50% round trip per trade (Alpaca crypto taker 0.25% per side; spread not added separately — disclosed).

preregistered.rule: TRADES: exactly R307's surge entries (same 32 coins, Coinbase hourly candles, same surge rule, one per coin per 24 h, long at the surge hour's close, 48 h hard cap, 0.50% round trip) — reuse backend/r307-ride-the-wave.js's entry logic and candle cache. LABEL (training only): at each hour h = 1..47 of a trade, y = 1 if no later close inside the 48 h window exceeds the close at h (the crest has passed), else 0. FEATURES at hour h, all from bars <= h: return since entry; drawdown from the highest close since entry; hours since entry; hours since that highest close; hour-h volume / 7-day median hourly volume; mean volume of the last 3 hours / the entry hour's volume; std of the last 6 hourly returns / the 7-day hourly std; close / mean close of the last 24 h - 1; hourly RSI(14); BTC's return since entry (BTC's own trades use ETH); the surge hour's return in sigma units; UTC hour of day; weekday. Standardised with training-set statistics only. MODELS (the 2 cells): LOGIT = L2-regularised logistic regression (lambda 1.0); GBM = gradient-boosted depth-2 trees, 200 rounds, learning rate 0.05, min 50 rows per leaf. Both implemented in plain Node (no Python on this host). WALK-FORWARD: for each test year Y in 2021..2026, train on every trade whose 48 h window closed before Jan 1 of Y (expanding window from 2019), then freeze the model for all of Y. POLICY: from h = 1, exit at the close of the first hour whose predicted probability of 'crest passed' is >= 0.5; otherwise at the 48 h cap.

Alpaca SIP daily bars, adjustment "all" (as R150). RSI(5) = Wilder's RSI, length 5, on daily closes. ENTRY at the close of day t when ALL FOUR hold, using bars <= t only: (1) RSI5[t] < 30; (2) RSI5 down for the third day in a row: RSI5[t] < RSI5[t-1] < RSI5[t-2] < RSI5[t-3]; (3) RSI5[t-3] < 60; (4) close[t] > SMA200[t]. Long only; one position per symbol at a time (a signal while already long is ignored). EXIT at the close of the first day u > t where RSI5 crosses above 50: RSI5[u] > 50 AND RSI5[u-1] <= 50. preregistered.evidenceStart: historical: positions decided at each month end from the first month all three currencies have spot and 3-month rates plus 12 months of history (expected 2000-07) through 2026-09; FORWARD record (reported, weightless) from the 2026-10 month-end decision
preregistered.rule: DATA (FRED): spot DEXUSEU (USD per EUR), DEXUSUK (USD per GBP), DEXSZUS (CHF per USD, inverted to USD per CHF); 3-month interbank rates IR3TIB01USM156N, IR3TIB01EZM156N, IR3TIB01GBM156N, IR3TIB01CHM156N (OECD, monthly averages). Month-end spot = last available daily fixing of the month. For months after a rate series ends, the last value is carried forward SHIFTED by the change in the same country's daily policy/overnight rate since then (US DTB3, EUR ECBDFR, GBP SONIA IUDSOIA if available else carried flat, CHF carried flat) — disclosed per month. RETURN of holding 1 unit of USD-vs-foreign exposure for month m (excess return, covered interest parity, i.e. what an FX forward/future earns): short foreign (long USD) = (S[m-1]/S[m]) * (1 + rUS[m-1]/1200) / (1 + rF[m-1]/1200) - 1; long foreign = the reciprocal minus 1; S in USD per foreign unit; rates are the PREVIOUS month's values (known at the decision). DIRECTION (carry): at month end m-1, gap = rUS - rF. gap > 0 -> candidate SHORT foreign; gap < 0 -> candidate LONG foreign; |gap| < 0.25 pt -> flat. TREND FILTER (Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen 2012, 12-month): hold the candidate only if that same position's cumulative excess return over months m-12..m-1 is > 0; otherwise flat. PORTFOLIO: the three currencies equally weighted (a flat leg contributes 0); monthly rebalance at month end. COST: 0.03% per unit traded at each position change + 0.01% per held leg-month (futures roll and spread).
preregistered.statistic: Unit: calendar MONTH. Per month the portfolio net excess return (mean of the three legs). Headline t = Newey-West (lag 1) over months.

controls.placebo: RANDOM DIRECTION: the same legs active in the same months with the direction drawn at random (1,000 draws, seeded); the observed mean must beat the placebo p95.

controls.halves: first and second half of the months; both must be positive.
controls.post2008: months 2009-01 onward (the zero-rate era where S6 found DM carry dead) must have mean > 0.
controls.reported: each currency alone; unfiltered carry (no trend filter); the 6-currency G10 pool (+ JPY, CAD, AUD from cached FRED spot + OECD rates) as context; worst month and worst 12 months (crash risk: CHF 2015-01, GBP 2016-06, 2008); cost at 2x; share of months active; the rate-fill months listed.

knownWeaknesses: Europe was chosen because today's gap is wide (US 4.00 vs ECB 2.50, CH ~0) and the dollar rose over the last year; the 26-year history is the test, but the question itself is conditioned on the present.
S6 (seen) found a cross-sectional developed-currency carry basket lost 2007-2026; R312 is time-series (per currency vs USD) with a trend filter — different, but overlapping data.

Synthetic returns via covered interest parity on OECD monthly-average 3-month rates; real forwards/futures differ by the CIP basis (tens of bp a year for EUR and CHF since 2008, in the direction that FLATTERS a long-USD carry) — the forward futures record measures it.

Monthly-average rates lag the true month-end rate by about half a month; the daily rates were observable in real time, so this is noise, not look-ahead — but it is noise in the carry sign near zero gap (hence the 0.25 pt dead zone).
Carry crashes are rare and large (CHF +20% in a day on 2015-01-15); 26 years holds few of them, so the t-stat understates tail risk; worst month and worst 12 months are reported.
Trend and carry often point the same way; the carry-adds control is the only thing separating them.

amendments.was: short foreign (long USD) = (S[m-1]/S[m]) x (1 + rUS/1200) / (1 + rF/1200) - 1, i.e. F/S1 - 1: the long-USD return measured in the FOREIGN currency; placebo = random direction at its own turnover cost; leak precondition = the registered shuffle alone
amendments.becomes: return:usd-numeraire — short foreign = 1 - S1/F, the USD profit per USD of notional that a short 6E / 6B / 6S future earns; long foreign unchanged (S1/F - 1); the 12-month trend filter compounds these returns. placebo:same-cost — the random-direction placebo is charged the OBSERVED cost series, so it differs from the rule in direction only; the observed mean must exceed its 95th percentile. leak:registered-else-uip-null — the read precondition is the registered leak test (|t| < 2); if it fails while the no-edge-null leak test (seed 1, the USD-fair null) passes, that is the registered shuffle's known construction bias and the read proceeds; if both fail the read is held for code review.
amendments.why: The registered short-side formula overstates every short month by (1 - x)^2 / x relative to the USD result of the futures position the test says it measures; the operator's account is in dollars. The same-cost placebo isolates the one thing the rule claims (direction). The registered shuffle keeps the real rate income, so its t centres near +0.5 with no premium at all: it measures carry, not a leak. Outcome-blind calibration by the runner under this set (2026-10-11 controls run): whole-rule false pass 0.3% (permutation), 0.8% (with replacement), 1.5% (sign-flip) against a 7.5% tolerance; registered leak t 1.098, USD-fair leak t -0.954, positive control passes.

preregistered.rule: Long only. Universe: data/r147-universe.json (100 names) + SPY QQQ IWM DIA XLK XLF XLE XLV XLY XLP XLI XLU XLB XLRE XLC. Enter when close > SMA200, close < SMA5, RSI(2) (Wilder) < 10; exit when close > SMA5. One lot per symbol per arm ($1,000 notional in whole shares, min 1, skip above $5,000); a lot still open from R151 occupies its arm x symbol cell until its own exit. Arm A: signal at ~15:40 ET with the latest IEX trade as the close proxy; entries and exits are DAY MARKET orders sent in the close-arm window (close-25 to close-10 min ET). Arm B: signal on the official daily bar; DAY MARKET entries and exits queued pre-open (08:00-09:25 ET) for the next open. Arm C: signal as B; entry = DAY limit at the signal close (unfilled = no trade); exits = DAY MARKET queued pre-open. No market-on-open/close order is ever sent. Fills are reconciled from filled_qty and filled_avg_price, never status alone: a partial entry opens the lot at the filled quantity; an exit that does not complete leaves the remainder EXIT-OWED, re-sent as a day market order at the arm's next order window whatever that day's signal says (client_order_id -S2, -S3 ...). Late-send guard: the close-arm sends nothing once ET is past close-5 min and the pre-open nothing from 09:30 ET (a DAY order sent after the close would queue for the next open, and one sent after the bell would fill intraday, either way under the wrong arm's label); an order not sent is not a trade, and an owed exit stays owed. Alpaca PAPER main account only; client_order_id r311-<arm>-<sym>-<yyyymmdd>-<B|S[n]> for R311 lots; a lot's exits always carry its own test's prefix, so an inherited R151 lot exits as r151-<arm>-<sym>-<yyyymmdd>-S[n] and every r311- order at the broker is R311's.
preregistered.statistic: Per trade, ONE TRADE = ONE ENTRY LOT: broker exit fill / broker entry fill - 1, where a lot exited in parts uses the quantity-weighted mean of its exit fills (Alpaca charges no commission; spread and slippage are inside the fills). Unit: ENTRY SESSION — per session the mean return of trades entered; t across sessions. Only rows with test "R311" whose entry client_order_id starts r311-, entries filled 2026-10-05..2026-10-16. Any quantity still open at the read, or exited after 2026-10-16, is marked at the 2026-10-16 official close (SIP daily bar, raw) and counted with markedAtEnd: true (R151's mark-open-lots amendment, carried over). Secondary: A minus B on the same symbol and signal date; C's fill rate; partial entries; broker rejects.

UNKNOWN is never DID NOT PASS.

knownWeaknesses: R151's 7 sessions void: R151 ran 2026-09-24..2026-10-02 on market-on-open/close orders that Alpaca paper barely fills (opg buys 0 full / 4 partial / 36 none of 40; cls buys 6 / 5 / 19 of 30; opg sells 1 / 4 / 7 of 12; cls sells 0 / 2 / 4 of 6) and its reconcile logged 6 partial exits as unfilled. It recorded 1 completed trade in 7 sessions. That record is frozen and never read; R311 starts fresh on 2026-10-05 and inherits from it only the runner and the R151 lots still open.

ARM A IS NO LONGER A CLOSING-AUCTION TRADE: a day market order in the close-arm window fills ~10-25 minutes before the close at the then-current quote. A measures the rule traded at its proxy moment (closer to its signal price), not Connors' MOC implementation; A minus B is now '~15:40 vs next open', not 'close vs open'.
PROXY CLOSE (as R151): arm A decides on the latest IEX trade at ~15:40 ET; a few signals will differ from the official-close rule.

INHERITED R151 LOTS (35 open after the one-time reconcile, 8 of them exit-owed) share the account and occupy their arm x symbol cells until their rule exits; R311 cannot enter those cells meanwhile (one lot per symbol per arm). They are managed with the same day orders; their exits carry r151- client_order_ids (the lot's own test) and test "R151" ledger rows, so a by-prefix audit of r311- orders at the broker sees R311 alone; the reader also excludes them by test AND entry prefix.

EXIT-OWED RE-SENDS are an execution choice made here: an exit the rule fired but the broker did not complete is re-sent at the next window whatever that day's signal says (R151 instead re-evaluated the signal). Closer to the backtest's exit, but not R151's behaviour.

ONE ACCOUNT FOR EVERYTHING (as R151): wash-trade refusals are possible when an owed exit and an entry, or a working C limit and an A sell, meet in one symbol; buying power can run short (R151 logged 10 '403 insufficient buying power' refusals on 09-30 and 10-01). Every refusal is logged (order-rejected) and reported; a refused exit stays owed.
PAPER FILLS ARE SIMULATED by Alpaca from the live quote; day market fills at the open may be more generous than a real open.
UNDER-POWERED (as R151): 10 sessions at ~3 entries a session.
LONG ONLY, ONE REGIME; AUDIT-MOTIVATED lineage (R150 audit -> R151 -> R311).

preregistered.rule: DATA: Robert Shiller's public monthly dataset (ie_data.xls; S&P composite price P, dividends D, earnings E, CPI, 10-year yield GS10, monthly total bond returns). SIGNAL at month end m: EY = E(m-3) / P(m) (trailing-12-month earnings lagged 3 months for reporting delay) vs GS10(m). POSITION for month m+1: STOCKS (S&P total return: price + D/12) if EY > GS10/100, else BONDS (the dataset's 10-year total bond return). No cost (monthly switches, index proxies; switches counted and reported).

knownWeaknesses: Expectation is DID NOT PASS (Asness 2003); the test exists to answer the operator's question with data.

Look-ahead built into Shiller's file, which the structural leak test cannot see. E and D are interpolated Dec -> Dec from ANNUAL figures through 1933 (682 of 682 months on the line). From 1926 E is interpolated between quarter-end figures (784 of 800). GS10 moves by a constant step from one January to the next within every calendar year through 1952 (82 of 82 years). So E(m-3) carries weight on figures published after m: before 1934 the year's annual figure, published the next year; after 1926 a quarter-end TTM figure 1-2 months before its publication. Before 1953, GS10(m) carries up to 11/12 weight on the next January's yield. Example: E(1922-03) = 0.39 = 0.29 + (3/12)(0.69 - 0.29), where 0.69 is the 1922 annual figure. The 3-month lag is only an approximation of reporting delay. The rule stays frozen; the E(m-6) version is reported, and it clears only the quarterly part.
The comparison is to stocks, not 60/40; 60/40 is reported.
1,860 overlapping-signal months: NW lag 6 and the block placebo handle persistence.

amendments.why: Pre-read review of the runner (2026-10-02) found the registered calendar halves gate degenerate on the frozen signal's shape. This was established from the shape only, with no returns. Switch minus stocks is 0 in every stock month. The frozen signal holds BONDS in 394 of 1,862 holding months: 3 fall in 1871-1948 (1922-04..06), 391 in 1967-12..2026-06, and none in 1949 to 1967-11. So the first-half gate is three 1922 months averaged over 932, and the second-half gate has the same 391-month numerator as the post-1965 gate, which counts one gate twice. The runner requires at least max(24, 10% of 394) = 40 bond months in each half. The 1922 spell exists only because of look-ahead in Shiller's interpolated E: E(1922-03) already contains 3/12 of the 1922 annual figure, published in 1923. CALIBRATION: controls run, runner sha256 b4dd2b88a576ef4f6ca285f8de4c110e4908ca0e8e108963410a0871858b5e07, cache sha256 044196dafe44c3030b2facbdea023975b3f6aa68b4e52f8f9bafc403e19589c1. Nine no-edge families were used; each row is judged by the full rule with its own 1,000-draw placebo. Four random-shape families are the builder's. Five real-shape families hold the frozen shape fixed and scramble the returns: rotation by 120..N-120 with at most 25% of the real bond months' returns reused, stationary block bootstrap with mean block 12, and iid Student-t(4). Whole-rule false pass, registered / amended: geomKept 0.0% / 0.0% (n 1000); geomFree 2.1% / 2.3% (n 1000); spellKept 0.0% / 0.0% (n 1000); spellFree 1.3% / 1.3% (n 1000); rotKept 0.0% / 0.0% (n 1157); rotFree 0.1% / 0.5% (n 1157); bootKept 0.0% / 0.0% (n 1000); bootFree 1.6% / 3.0% (n 1000); studentFree 2.0% / 3.2% (n 1000). The worst is 2.1% registered and 3.2% amended (studentFree, Wilson 95% upper 4.48%), both under the 5% limit. On real-shape no-edge rows that clear mean and t, the calendar halves gate keeps rotFree 33% vs 100% (n 9), bootFree 43% vs 91% (n 58), studentFree 59% vs 100% (n 56) (calendar vs bond-month): on this shape the calendar gate is a coin flip on three months, not a stability check. POWER: real shape, synthetic edge added to the bond months of premium-free block-bootstrap returns, 1,000 draws per level, registered / amended / no halves gate: achieved t p50 1.722: 20.2% / 35.5% / 36.5%; achieved t p50 2.505: 40.6% / 65.6% / 66.4%; achieved t p50 2.845: 48.0% / 77.9% / 78.4%. Those synthetic edges include the 1922 months; on the real 1922 returns the registered first half may be decided against any plausible edge. DISCLOSURE: while auditing the interpolation, the reviewer printed P for 1922-03..06, so the reviewer knows the sign of the registered calendar first-half gate. The reviewer reports it negative (about -0.01%/month, which only an edge above about 3%/month in those three months could flip). The reviewer states nothing from the 391 post-1965 bond months was seen. The repairer computed no statistic of the real switch and printed no price, return or yield in any bond month. The amendment keeps the 1922 months: they stay in bond-month half 1 (3 of 197). No gate other than the halves gate changes, and the bar, rule and population are unchanged. The runner HOLDS the read until a ruling is recorded. Either ruling unlocks it: this amendment, or an explicit pre-evidence runnerGates ["registered"] to read the gates as written (that rule is calibrated at 2.1%).

Membership history from Nasdaq's annual reconstitution press releases (public). Prices: Alpaca SIP daily (adjustment all) incl. delisted names. COST 0.10% round trip per leg.

A roll is declared only inside a listed contract's roll slot: the sessions after the previous listed delivery month's last-trade bound up to its own, bound = an upper bound of the contract's last trading day under the exchange spec (COMEX/NYMEX metals, LE and GF the end of the delivery month; CBOT/KC grains and oilseeds the 14th; HE the 17th); CL NG HO RB (every month listed; last trade in the month before delivery: CL <= the 22nd, NG <= the 29th, HO/RB the last business day) use the calendar month restricted to the days CL 10-25th, NG HO RB 15-31st. Table fixed in the runner (ROLL_SPEC; listed months/bound): CL every month, days 10-25; NG every month, days 15-31; HO every month, days 15-31; RB every month, days 15-31; GC GJMQVZ/end; SI HKNUZ/end; HG HKNUZ/end; PL FJNV/end; PA HMUZ/end; ZC HKNUZ/14; ZW HKNUZ/14; KE HKNUZ/14; ZO HKNUZ/14; ZS FHKNQUX/14; ZL FHKNQUVZ/14; ZM FHKNQUVZ/14; LE GJMQVZ/end; HE GJKMNQVZ/17; GF FHJKQUVX/end. At most one roll per slot, at the session whose overnight gap |open/prev close - 1| is largest relative to the trailing-250 median gap of the same break type; a slot whose bound is after the last bar gets none. Every earlier price is multiplied by open/prev close of that session. Roll cost of 2 sides x (1 tick + $2.50) at each declared roll inside a holding window. Release = Friday 15:30 ET of T's week, moved to the next business day >= Monday only for a federal closure Wed-Fri (a Friday without a session — Good Friday — does not move it; entry is then the Monday session, as registered). Reports CFTC published late are not traded: as-of 2013-10-01..2013-11-05, 2018-12-24..2019-03-05, 2023-01-31..2023-03-14 (ION), 2025-09-30..2025-12-16. Universe = candidate roots with a >= 8-year continuous front run (no gap > 10 days, >= 90% of reference sessions, ending >= 2026-09-30) and >= 8 years of legacy COT spreading overlapping it; a root whose COT stops leaves the cross-section at that date (19: CL NG HO RB GC SI HG PL PA ZC ZS ZW KE ZL ZM ZO LE HE GF). CANNOT MEASURE if < 15 roots qualify. Calibration: whole-rule false pass <= 5% on each of deranged SP labels on the real path (deranged within each week's names, 200), the placebo family (200), arithmetic-zero-drift scrambles (100) and a roll-leak family (100: the same scrambles with the real roll factors re-inserted and re-detected). Drift-kept scrambles (60), the drift-kept floor, a gross placebo, a persistent-rank placebo and a leave-one-root-out t are reported beside the verdict. Rule, statistic, bar, placebo, halves and cost otherwise unchanged.
amendments.why: Schwab pricehistory serves only its continuous front series (probed 2026-10-03, cache sha256 c399afa1d148): for every served root <M>27 returns closes identical to /ROOT and <M>24 returns no candles, so the registered construction qualifies 0 of 27 roots and the registered read is CANNOT MEASURE. Audit of 2026-10-03 on the builder's front-series construction, repaired here: (a) the forced one-roll-per-calendar-month detector declared >= 84 false rolls/yr on 14 of 18 roots, erasing real overnight gaps (CL +11.46% on 2026-03-02) and over-charging roll cost (~0.011%/wk, ~0.17 t); the detected roll factors line up with SP (leaving 48% of them in moved t by +0.185, SE 0.018, across 100 paired no-edge worlds). The auditor's month-before-delivery table, checked against Schwab's gaps (price only), misses Schwab's other conventions (LE rolls in the last days of the month before the contract month in about half the years; HE rolled a month early in 2008-10; GC/HG/SI sometimes in the first days of the delivery month); last-trade-bounded slots cover them with the same count of declared rolls (one per listed contract) and leave fewer large gaps undeclared on the 15 non-energy roots (z >= 15: 170 vs 268 for the month table). No month table can fix the every-month energies (the lead example, CL +11.46% on 2026-03-02, is one): their slot is restricted to the days before the last trading day (CL 10-25th, NG HO RB 15-31st), so the largest weekend news gaps (CL 2020-03-09 -20.9%, 2022-03-07 +5.5%, 2023-04-03 +5.8%, 2026-03-02 +11.5%; HO/RB 2021-05-10) stay in the returns and the in-window roll-sized gap is removed. Roll-leak family, paired with the arithmetic-zero-drift scrambles: mean change in t -0.027 (SD 0.201, SE 0.0201), re-detected share of the real rolls 0.547. Reported sensitivity: with half of the real roll factors forced to stay in the returns, t moves by -0.689 (SE 0.0394) — the roll factors are anti-aligned with the SP book, so rolls the detector misses understate SP rather than flatter it. (b) CFTC published the as-of 2023-01-31..03-14 reports on 2023-02-24..03-21 (ION) and the runner traded them on their nominal Fridays. (c) CFTC does not delay the release for Monday or Tuesday holidays (2026 schedule; 2025 table: as-of 11-10 -> 11-14); 108 weeks entered a session late; Good Friday (CFTC publishes) also delayed entry a session. (d) The 2025 catch-up ended with the as-of 2025-12-16 report (CFTC table of 2025-12-09); as-of 12-23 was on the normal schedule. (e) ZO was dropped from all 18 years because its COT stops 2026-09-01. (f) Drift-free scrambles removed the log drift, leaving +sigma^2/2 a day against a book short the high-vol roots; derangements cut from a global permutation let 0.19% of name-weeks keep their own SP. Front-series universe 19 roots, 916 weeks from 2008-06-30. Whole-rule false pass with the registered gates: deranged 2.5%, placebo family 0%, arithmetic-zero-drift 0%, roll-leak 0% (drift-kept 13.3%, reported; with the optional floor token every family <= 5%, drift-kept 5%). preregistered.rule: POPULATION: every US Treasury nominal coupon auction (2y, 3y, 5y, 7y, 10y, 20y, 30y) in TreasuryDirect's auction-results feed, original issues and reopenings alike, over the window above. TIPS, FRNs and bills are excluded. INSTRUMENT MAP (fixed): 2y+3y -> SHY | 5y+7y -> IEI | 10y -> IEF | 20y+30y -> TLT. TRADE, per auction: PRE LEG short the mapped ETF at the close of the second session before auction day (T-2) and cover at the auction-day close (T0); POST LEG long at the auction-day close (T0) and sell at the close of the second session after (T+2). Both legs are taken for every auction; the auction's net is the sum of the two legs' net returns. Sessions are Schwab daily bars; if a leg's session is missing, that auction is dropped and counted. COST: 2 basis points per side crossing (8 bps per auction over the four fills) plus 1 basis point per calendar day of short borrow on the PRE leg. Positions are equal-weight by dollar notional, one unit per auction.

controls.cost2x: the same trades at twice the cost model (4 bps per side, 2 bps per day borrow): cluster mean > 0.

decisionRule.pass: PASS only if >= 300 auction-week clusters AND cluster mean net > 0 AND t_NW >= 2.217 AND the shifted-calendar placebo gate clears AND the hold-the-instrument gate clears AND the non-auction-week control is flat AND both halves > 0 AND the 2x-cost mean > 0 AND the leak calibration is <= 5% AND the positive control passed. A PASS proposes a forward paper arm sized as a candidate THIRD LEG beside Plan E (20-30% of risk budget) — the operator's call, never automatic.
decisionRule.fail: DID NOT PASS: the auction concession is not harvestable through duration ETFs after costs on 2002-2026 data; the mechanism is closed at this implementation and the third-leg search moves to the next candidate.
decisionRule.cannotMeasure: CANNOT MEASURE if < 300 clusters, if TreasuryDirect coverage gaps exceed 5% of auctions, or if the leak test or positive control fails.

knownWeaknesses: The ETF era starts mid-2002 and IEI only in 2007, so the headline n is below the ~2,300 auctions the raw calendar offers; the 2y/3y and 5y/7y buckets are shorter than the 10y.

R184 tested the 10y/30y subpopulation and DID NOT PASS at the test level; its short-pre cell at t 2.354 is the motivation for this test and is counted in the family. If the pooled result is carried entirely by that subpopulation, this is a re-read of a seen cell and must be reported as such.

Duration ETFs across buckets are highly correlated, so the four buckets are far from four independent bets; the auction-week cluster unit is the control for that and the bar is still paid at variants 4.
The Federal Reserve was the dominant buyer in 2009-2014 and 2020-2021, which could create or destroy the concession; an era-excluded read is reported but the primary includes those years.
TLT's duration is much longer than a 20y auction's and SHY's much shorter than a 3y's; the map is a liquidity choice, not a duration match.
The PRE leg requires borrow on every auction; borrow was cheap and available for these ETFs historically, but the 1 basis point per day charge is a model, not a measurement.
The 20y tenor was reintroduced in 2020, so that bucket mixes a 2002-2009 history with a 2020+ one.
Settlement-date versus auction-date conventions differ by tenor; the rule anchors on AUCTION date, and any auction whose results were published after the session close is dropped and counted.
preregistered.readCondition: --read once, after --selftest passes and every control above has run (shifted-calendar placebo, hold benchmark, non-auction-week control, leak calibration <= 5%, positive control). The read is sealed the same day through the read-test ritual.

The read reports the result with and without those auctions; the registered statistic is the one WITH them.

Readings fixed by the runner where the text was open (its header notes N1-N16), confirmed here before any outcome: the statistic's week is the week of the AUCTION date (as knownWeaknesses says the rule anchors); each bucket starts with its ETF's first full year — SHY / IEF / TLT auctions from 2002-07-01, IEI from 2007-01-01; an auction with no closing time in the feed (150 before 2008-04) is kept on a regular session and dropped on an early-close session; the leak shuffle moves whole auction weeks to other weeks of the same calendar year, weekday kept; the placebo moves each cluster as a block to an eligible non-auction week of the same year, its 95th percentile is sorted[475] of 500 and the paired difference uses the mean of the 500 placebo values; the hold benchmark is charged no cost; 'TreasuryDirect coverage gaps' means records the feed cannot place or qualify; a leak calibration above 5% reads HELD and a single-shuffle failure reads CANNOT MEASURE.

amendments.why: Outcome-blind, on synthetic no-edge prices laid on the real auction dates (200 shuffles, runner build 2026-10-11): net of cost the non-auction gate held on 0% of shuffles and the single-shuffle t was -2.66 (failing on 96.5% of shuffles), so the test could never be measured; at zero cost the gate held on 97.5% and the single-shuffle t was 0.43. And with the control anchored on every session of a non-auction week its windows overlap the auction weeks beside it, so a real effect leaks into the control: the gate held on 97% / 77% / 13% of shuffled calendars at 1x / 2x / 4x a planted effect — a control that fails harder the truer the hypothesis is.
amendments.disclosed: Written after the runner's synthetic calibration was seen and before any real outcome. Known before the read: even at zero cost the rule has a narrow detection window on synthetic prices (a small planted effect mostly fails the hold gate), so a DID NOT PASS will not exclude a small effect. The registered expectation of about 700 auction-week clusters is 632 in the data (the floor is 300).

It chose no other.

(a) Published results, read by every agent: Thompson, Pontiff, Patro and co-authors (18.2% a year long-short, 1984-2011, before costs), Flynn, the U.K. tenths, the industry report on tenders, and the open-ending study's table of attacked funds' discounts before and after an attempt.
