CONSEQUENCE: rule [6](h) keeps every signal of 2008-09-01..2008-12-31 and 2020-02-01..2020-04-30 out of every gated number.

(c) Levels: price under half of NAV for HFRO (326 rows, 2024-2026), DMA (43 rows, 2023) and four preferred funds on 2008-10-09 and 10-10; over double for GUT (307 rows) and PGP (87 rows). No fund is named in the rule.
(d) One 2012 unit trust chosen by a z-score rule: unit price 10.0000 at the start and 9.1358 at maturity, without its distributions.

(e) Counts, dates and clock times from the skeptics' checks: shares of repeated NAV rows; 0 no-volume next days in 78,674 eligible fund-days; split-event dates and ratios; when Yahoo showed a day's NAV on 2026-10-12.
(f) The recorded statuses of two house tests named in nearestHouseTests.
(g) By the registrar who wrote this entry: no series, cache or outcome was opened; one public paper was opened to read what its cost table measures (rule [12]).
rule: [0] WHAT IS TESTED. One paper book on history, in two spans fixed here; one rule; nothing searched; this test places no order. THE BOOK: a $100,000 account; at most 24 positions of $4,000 each, whatever the book has made or lost; long only; no borrowing; idle cash earns nothing in the statistic. Each half of a calendar month (the 1st to the 15th; the 16th to the end) opens at most 1 position, counted by the SIGNAL day (rule [8]), so purchases are spread evenly over the year.

[1] DATA. Yahoo Finance chart API v8, daily rows (interval 1d, events div and split), one cache per symbol, fetched once on or after 2026-10-15 and frozen by hash before any statistic is computed. P[t] = the RAW close of the fund's price symbol and V[t] its volume; N[t] = the RAW close of the NAV symbol the frozen list names for that fund (never built as X + ticker + X), after rule [4]. The adjusted close is never used. Market days = the dates on which ^GSPC has a row. A null row is a missing row; nothing is ever carried forward. A NAV symbol is accepted only if Yahoo types it MUTUALFUND on exchange NAS with zero volume and open = high = low = close on every valued row.

[2] UNIVERSE. The funds of the frozen list (the public list as of 2026-10-09 = docs/fund-discounts/2026-10-12/scout-universe.json, sha256 9a5524e7e8f0ae299a4f18eb078adc0ae6c0f7ea54ed8d08ed6aba28b240fee8) that have both series, a NAV symbol accepted under [1] and no term date on that list: 298 funds (63 municipal, 112 taxable bond, 85 US equity, 38 foreign equity). No fund is dropped whole for its levels and no fund is named in this rule. A fund with a term date cannot be bought, be a placebo or be a control.

[3] SUSPECT ROWS AND WRONG PRINTS. NAV series: a row that is 1.3 times or more, or 1/1.3 or less, of the previous valid NAV row, on a day the price changes by under 15%, is SUSPECT. Price series: a row that is 1.9 times or more, or 1/1.9 or less, of the previous valid price row, on a day the NAV changes by under 15%, that no split event dated within two market days explains, is SUSPECT. FOR A DECISION on a day s (a signal, eligibility, a lookback window, a placebo day, a control day) the screen is run on the series cut off at s: a fund cannot signal, be a placebo or be a control on a SUSPECT day or on the 3 market days after it, and a SUSPECT row is taken out of a window only once a row within 15% of the value before the step, among the next 3 valid rows, is dated s or earlier. Nothing dated after s decides anything on s. FOR MEASUREMENT (fills, month-end values, the yardstick) the screen is run on the whole series: a SUSPECT row followed within 3 valid rows by a row within 15% of the value before the step is a WRONG PRINT and is removed with the rows between; an entry due on a removed row is no trade, for the real book, the placebo and the control alike; an exit or a month-end due there uses the last valid row before it. A SUSPECT NAV row that is not undone is an UNVERIFIED EVENT on its date unless rule [4] classifies it. No price row is ever removed for a step under 1.9 times, whatever the price does next.

[4] UNITS. For each split event on the price symbol (date T; k = the factor Yahoo applies to earlier prices for it) the one-day NAV step q = N[t] / N[previous valid row] is looked for on each of the five market days T-2..T+2. LARGE event (|ln k| > 0.10): if exactly one of the five days has |ln q - ln k| <= 0.10, the NAV history was not adjusted and every NAV row before that day is multiplied by k; if none of the five has |ln q| > 0.10, it was already adjusted and nothing is done; anything else is an UNVERIFIED EVENT at T. SMALL event (|ln k| <= 0.10: rights offerings and spin-offs shown as ratios such as 1008:1000): always an UNVERIFIED EVENT at T, because the series cannot show whether the NAV was adjusted.

[5] DISCOUNT AND Z. A row is VALID when both closes are finite and positive after [3] and [4] and 0.5 <= P/N <= 2.0. d[t] = P[t] / N[t] - 1 on valid rows. For a day s the window is the 252 market days strictly before s (s is not in its own window); it needs at least 230 valid rows; m[s] is their mean and sd[s] their sample standard deviation (n - 1), which must be above zero; z[s] = (d[s] - m[s]) / sd[s]. VALID governs signals, windows, placebo days and control days only: money is counted on the price symbol's close on every market day that close exists with volume above zero, whatever the asset value says, and the only price rows ever taken out of the money are wrong prints under [3].

[6] ELIGIBLE on s. Every input is dated s or earlier, except ex-dates, which are announced in advance. (a) history: at least 756 valid rows strictly before s. (b) the rows of s and of the market day before s are both valid, and V[s] > 0. (c) fresh NAV: N[s] is not the third or later row of a run of identical NAV values; s is not a FEED-FREEZE day (the share of the universe's valued funds with N[s] = N[s-1] is at least 40% and at least twice the median of that daily share over the 252 market days before s); and s is not a BOND-HOLIDAY day (the NYSE is open and the US bond market is closed: the second Monday of October, and 11 November, or 12 November when the 11th is a Sunday). (d) daily NAV: the NAV differs from the previous row on at least 100 of the 252 rows ending at s and on at least 8 of the 21 rows ending at s. (e) liquidity: the median of as-traded close x as-traded volume over the 30 market days ending at s is at least $400,000 (a market day with no price row counts as $0) and the as-traded close on s is at least $5.00 (as-traded = Yahoo's value with every later split ratio undone). (f) events: no UNVERIFIED EVENT is dated in the 252 market days before s or on s; a LARGE unverified event makes the fund not eligible from its first row until 252 market days after it; no SUSPECT row on s or on the 3 market days before it. (g) ex-dates: no distribution of 1% of the price or more has its ex-date, on the price symbol's list, within the 3 market days ending at s or the 3 after s. (h) s is not in a SEEN WINDOW: 2008-09-01..2008-12-31 or 2020-02-01..2020-04-30 (a scout saw price moves of those weeks before registration: seenBeforeRegistration). (i) the fund is not under a quarantine written by the pre-read gates IDENTITY, SECOND SOURCE or EX-DATE ALIGNMENT (controls.validity), each of which reads levels and counts only.

[7] SIGNAL on s: the fund is eligible on s, AND z[s] < -2, AND z of the market day before s < -2, AND d[s] < 0 whichever way every UNVERIFIED EVENT dated after s is resolved (d[s] is computed with the NAV rows before that event multiplied by its k, and not multiplied; the test must hold both ways), AND the fund is not held and has no entry pending.

[8] WHICH SIGNAL IS TAKEN. Days are processed in order. In each half-month at most one signal is taken: on the first signal day of the half-month on which the book will have a free place at the entry close (places are counted from the exits SCHEDULED for that close, as known the evening before) and no position has yet been opened from that half-month, the fund with the lowest z[s]; ties go to the larger 30-day median dollar volume, then to the ticker in alphabetical order. A taken signal whose entry finds no fill under [9] leaves the half-month open to a later signal day. If a scheduled exit finds no traded close, the book may hold 25 positions until it does; the read counts how often. A position belongs to the half-month of its signal day s, not of its fill day. After a failed fill the half-month re-opens only for signal days after the market day on which the failure is known. That day is the last close [9] allows (the third market day after s) or, where a wrong print voided the fill, the date of the row that proves it, whichever is later; until then the entry is pending.

[9] ENTRY. Buy $4,000 at the close of e = the first market day after s (the SECOND market day after s for a LATE REPORTER, controls.validity) provided the fund has on e a price row with volume above zero that is not a wrong print; if not, the next such row within 3 market days of s; otherwise no trade. The order is a market-on-close order sent before the exchange's cut-off, decided from values that were public before that session opened.

[10] EXIT. Sell at the close of x = the 252nd market day after e (the next price row with volume above zero if that day has none). Nothing else ends a position: no stop, no target, no exit on any signal. On the last market day of a span every open position is sold at that close. One position per fund at a time.

[11] MONEY. Shares = 4,000 / P[e]. A position's price dollars = shares x (P[x] - P[e]) + shares x every distribution on the price symbol's dividend list whose ex-date is after e and on or before x (the distributions the position was entitled to; cash, not reinvested; amounts in the price's split units), less cost.

[12] COST per round trip c, half charged at each fill on that fill's dollar value: c = the larger of the fund's class cost and 2 times the fund's own measured spread. Class cost: municipal 0.80%, taxable bond 1.08%, US equity 1.02%, foreign equity 1.36% (twice the one-way costs printed in Cherkes, Sagi and Stanton 2009, Table 2, panel c). Own spread: the median of (ask - bid) / mid at 15:30 New York over at least 10 regular sessions, one-sided books dropped, from the house quote source, recorded before the cache is frozen. A fund that source cannot quote — and every fund, if no such table covering at least 80% of the universe exists when the cache is frozen — is charged 1.5 times its class cost. Commission $0. The cost changes what a fill is CHARGED and nothing else: no clause that decides a trade reads it. The placebo pays NO cost.

[13] SPANS. DISCOVERY: signal days and fills 2003-01-02..2011-12-30; return months 2003-01..2011-12 (108). HOLDOUT: 2012-01-03..2026-09-30; return months 2012-01..2026-09 (177). Each span's book starts with no position and is sold out on its last market day, so no position and no fill crosses a span and every fill is charged inside its own span. No row dated after 2026-09-30 enters any statistic; later split events are read for [4] and [7] only. Discovery starts 2003-01-02 because that is the first January by which every fund whose NAV history begins in the 1998-1999 load (67 funds, a count from the frozen list) can have the 756 rows of [6](a); before it too few survivors can signal for a book to choose among them. The spans split at the end of 2011 because that is where the published record stops.

[14] NO SETTING CHANGES ANY OF THIS. The runner takes no flag, setting or environment variable that changes a number of this rule or of the statistic. Any later run of this rule with one of them changed, on either span, is a new member of the family at the bar for the new count (multiplicityFamily).

published: discount = price / asset value - 1 (Morningstar via Fidelity 2012; Cherkes, Sagi and Stanton 2009)
lookback one year, taken as 252 market days (Morningstar's worked examples and its own z-statistic; three other published lookbacks exist and none was examined)
entry at z less than -2 (Morningstar via Fidelity; BlackRock)
756 valid rows of history (Malkiel and Xu 2005: at least three years of data)

liquidity floor: median daily dollar volume of the prior 30 trading days at least $400,000 and price at least $5 (Guggenheim's unit-trust screen; its third leg, assets of $100 million, has no point-in-time source and is left out; PARTLY published: the trust applies the floor monthly where this test applies it daily)
class cost: twice the one-way trading costs of Cherkes, Sagi and Stanton 2009, Table 2, panel c — in that paper's words, 'the one-way cost for municipal bond funds averaged 0.4%'
houseTiedToAPublishedFact: hold 252 market days and no other exit (Thompson held a year; Pontiff's horizon is twelve months)
the spans split at December 2011 (the last month of the last published sample)
numbers.houseSingle: every other number of rule, statistic, controls and bar: named once, before any series was read for outcomes (those listed in seenBeforeRegistration[0] were set with the scout's screens in view), and never varied. See knownWeaknesses, HOUSE CHOICES.
numbers.paceChoice: Half-month, not month or week, so that 24 positions of $4,000 each stay near 1% of a floor-liquidity day; no other pacing was run.

timing: close[s], volume[s]: public 16:00 New York on s; first use: the signal of s.
NAV[s]: public after the close of s (by the next morning on Yahoo as seen on 2026-10-12; timed per fund by V6); first use: the signal of s, never before the session of s+1.
the 252-day window for s: ends the day before s.
a wrong print: known from the day its return is on the tape; windows from that day on, never earlier.
a split ratio: used for unit conversion only; the level test of [7] must hold whichever way a later unverified ratio is resolved.
the order: sent on s+1 before the closing-auction cut-off; filled at the close of s+1 (s+2 for a late reporter), on a row with volume.
NAV on the fill day and after: a yardstick only; the clean measurement starts at the first fresh value on or after the fill.
list membership, asset class, cost group, term flag, late-reporter flag: 2026 knowledge — which funds exist, their group, a later fill. Named as today's knowledge in knownWeaknesses.
own spread: measured in 2026 before the cache is frozen; the money charged only.
preregistered.lookAheadDiscipline: This is a rule on public fund series, not a model on the board's entry features, so the board's feature manifest does not apply; its purpose is met by V2 (the as-of replay on the real series, zero mismatches), by the selftest's future-poison case and by rule [3]'s cut-off screen.
preregistered.statistic: Clustered by calendar month — one number per month, never per trade and never per fund. For each return month M of a span, on the fixed $100,000 book: G(M) = [the real positions' GAP DOLLARS in M, minus the costs of the real fills in M] minus [the placebo's gap dollars in M, at NO cost, averaged over 500 seeded draws]. HEADLINE = the mean of G over ALL the span's return months (a month with no position counts), in dollars a month per $100,000, with its Newey-West t (Bartlett weights, lag 4; the house formula of backend/lib/tv-pit-panel.js nwT). ONE t decides: the holdout's. In words: what the rule's choice of days added in the gap between price and asset value, after paying its own trading costs, over being in the same funds the same number of times for the same length of time on days picked by chance, which costs nothing.

definitions.gapDollars: For a position and a month it is open in, with a = its CLEAN START if that falls in the month, else the last market day of the month before, and b = its CLEAN END if that falls in the month, else the last market day of the month: gap dollars = shares x P[a] x [ (P[b] + Dist) / P[a] - (N[b] + Dist) / N[a] ], where Dist = the distributions per share the position was entitled to with ex-date after a and on or before b. It is the price return minus the asset-value return over the same days, in dollars: the market, the asset class and the fund's borrowing cancel. It is the same days' asset value, not a drift estimated from signal days, and the raw price dollars are printed beside it on every line (house rule on signal-dependent drift).
definitions.cleanStart: the first market day c on or after e on which the fund has a price row with volume above zero and a NAV row that differs from the previous valid NAV row, that is not a BOND-HOLIDAY day, not on or within 1 market day of any ex-date, and not within 3 market days of the ex-date of a distribution of 1% of the price or more. c must be within 5 market days of e; otherwise the position has NO CLEAN SERIES: its gap dollars are $0 in every month, it still pays its costs, and it is counted. Nothing ever moves a start back before e. Price and NAV are both taken at c. The price dollars always start at e.
definitions.cleanEnd: the exit day x, moved BACK when needed to the last market day before it that has both rows, is not the third or later row of an identical NAV run, is not a BOND-HOLIDAY day and is clear of ex-dates by the same margins as the clean start. The price dollars always end at x.
definitions.monthEnds: inside a holding, a month-end whose NAV row is null, or is the third or later row of an identical NAV run, or is a BOND-HOLIDAY day, moves back to the last market day that is none of those, for price and NAV both; the next month starts there, so the months still multiply to the whole and nothing is measured against a frozen value. No NAV is ever filled in from another day.
definitions.unverifiedEventInAHolding: a position-month that contains an UNVERIFIED EVENT is computed twice, with the NAV before the event multiplied by its k and not multiplied, and the LOWER gap dollars are used. Counted and reported; never void.
definitions.placebo: For each real position of a fund f and each of 500 draws (generator mulberry32, seed 20261012 + 1000 x span number + draw number; discovery is span 1, holdout span 2): one day t drawn evenly from the market days of the span on which f is eligible under [6] and d[t] < 0 as in [7] — the signal's own conditions with the two z tests taken out. Same entry rule [9], same exit rule [10], same $4,000, same clean start, clean end and month-ends, NO cost. Within a draw a fund's placebo positions never overlap (redraw up to 200 times; else the slot is dropped in that draw and counted). The placebo does NOT share the half-month pacing or the 24 places; with about one year per hold the real book's cap binds and pins each purchase to the sale of the position bought a year earlier. S5 checks that calendar by rank only: an effect the shifted books share still passes about half the time.
definitions.priceDollarSeries: D(M) = [the real positions' price dollars in M after costs] minus [the placebo's price dollars in M at no cost]. BOOK(M) = the real book's price dollars after costs, alone: it includes what the funds themselves earned. YIELD(M) = the part of the real gap dollars that needs no move in the gap: the sum over open positions of shares x Dist x (1 - P[a] / N[a]), the extra yield of buying below asset value.
definitions.monthEndMark: A position is marked at every price row with volume above zero, however bad the level; a fund with no such row on a month's last market day is marked at its last one.

bar.statistic: Newey-West (Bartlett) t, lag 4, of the mean over calendar months of G, clustered by calendar month
bar.source: max( lib/null-bar.js nullBar({variants:1, n:177, trials:20000, rng:mulberry(20261189)}).p95 = 1.6862 ; nullBar({variants:1, n:177, trials:400000, rng:mulberry(20361189)}).p95 = 1.6512 ; Newey-West lag-4 null p95 over 50000 trials of the same noise, mulberry(20461189) = 1.6785 ; the higher of the two drafts' saved bars (1.727, 1.684) = 1.727 ), rounded up to 3 decimals = 1.727
bar.sourceDiscovery: max( lib/null-bar.js nullBar({variants:1, n:108, trials:20000, rng:mulberry(20261120)}).p95 = 1.6762 ; nullBar({variants:1, n:108, trials:400000, rng:mulberry(20361120)}).p95 = 1.6599 ; Newey-West lag-4 null p95 over 50000 trials of the same noise, mulberry(20461120) = 1.7293 ; the higher of the two drafts' saved bars (1.721, 1.708) = 1.721 ), rounded up to 3 decimals = 1.73
bar.raisedInTheRead: At each read the bar in force is the LARGEST of tRequired, the V10 worlds' 95th percentile (below) and the 95th percentile of the same Newey-West t over 20000 seeded resamples (mulberry32 seed 20261012 + span number) of that read's own months of G, drawn with replacement in blocks of 13 months (the 12-month hold plus one) after their mean is subtracted. It is computed inside the read before the verdict line, printed beside the registered number, and can only raise the bar: months that are not all alike (a few blow-out months) make a plain bar too easy. The bar in force is also never below the 95th percentile of the deciding t over that span's V10 no-edge worlds, computed in --controls before the real book is touched. It can only raise the bar.
bar.why: ONE variant: one rule is registered and no number of it was searched (numbers). Unit months, the statistic's clustering unit. The t always has every return month of the span (177 in the holdout), so n is that count. Four numbers and the highest binds, so neither simulation luck nor a choice between the two drafts' saved tables can lower it. The function is seeded here, so a second run prints the same bar; it is not to be re-drawn with another seed. THE BAR OWES DEPENDENCE, NOT COUNT: about fifty numbers of the rule are chosen, but a family size counts looks at outcomes and none has been taken, so it stays 1 (a best-of-35 bar would be about 3.0 and would price the count of choices); what the bar owes is for the months being dependent, because a 252-day hold sits in about twelve consecutive months while the t uses lag 4, so the bar in force is raised by blocks of 13 months and by the V10 worlds (synthetic noise with a 12-month overlap and no edge passes 1.727 at lag 4 in about 17% of draws; made numbers, not data).

signGates: Each is the mean over the holdout's 177 months and must be ABOVE $0 (S5: above the median of the shifted books' means). They gate on sign or rank, not on a t; the no-edge worlds measure how often the whole rule passes by chance.
S1 MONEY: D, all price dollars after costs against the no-cost placebo. A stale, late or wrong asset value can make a pointless trade but cannot be booked as profit here.

S2 AFTER THE FIRST MONTH: G21 = G with every position (real and placebo) measured only from the close of the 21st market day after its entry; the real book still pays all its costs (the entry half in the month the measurement starts). Bounce, late marks and stale values live in the first days.

S3 US CLOCK: G without the positions (real and placebo) of funds in the foreign-clock classes: Asia Equity, Emerging Market Equity, Single Country Equity, Global Equity, Global Allocation, Global Income, Emerging Market Income. Their asset values are struck hours before the US close.

S4 WITHOUT THE FUND'S OWN ASSET VALUE: GPEER = G with each position-month's asset-value return replaced by the equal-weight mean asset-value return, over the same days, of the eligible funds of its cost group that have no open real position (at least 3 such funds, else that position-month is left out and counted), for real and placebo alike. A discount that closes because the fund's own asset value fell to the price pays the holder nothing; this version cannot count it.

S5 CALENDAR: the holdout mean G per position opened must exceed the median of the same figure over label L12's 500 month-shifted books (each moved by k whole months), which keep the real book's pacing, cap and day-in-month. k is drawn evenly from 1 to the span's months minus 1 (mulberry32, seed 20266012 + span number). A shifted signal day must meet the placebo's conditions ([6], d < 0, fund not held); else the next such day of its half-month; else dropped with its placebo slots. Shifted books pay [12]'s costs. S5 compares mean G per position opened (the span's monthly mean of G divided by the positions opened). On a made world 100 shifted books are used, as the placebo uses 100 draws. It asks whether the calendar that the half-month rule and the 24 places impose, and not the z-score, carries G.
labels: Printed with every read; none can change the verdict; a label that looks better than the rule is exploratory and needs its own registration on data it has not seen.

L1 WHICH FUND (the level twin). For each real position (fund f, signal day s) the control funds are every other fund that on s is in the same cost group, eligible under [6], has |z| <= 1, has a discount within 0.02 of f's and no open real position; each is entered and sold at the same closes. Monthly series of the real position's gap dollars minus the mean of its controls', before cost; mean and Newey-West t. t at or above the bar: 'the reading that is unusual for this fund carries it'. Mean above zero, t under the bar: 'what the z-score adds beyond a wide gap on the same day is not shown'. Mean at or below zero: 'the book passed on wide gaps and dates; the z-score adds nothing', and any forward test is drafted on the level rule as a fresh registration. Fewer than 50% of positions matched: CANNOT SEPARATE. The share of G that came from matched positions is printed.

L2 FIRST MONTH. G21's own t is printed. The words 'still there after the first month' are used only when it is at or above the bar; otherwise the first line adds 'outside the first month the effect is not shown on its own; a late asset value is not ruled out as its source'. The first 21 days' dollars are printed apart.

L3 COST. G and its t at twice and at three times the charged cost. If the t at twice is under the bar the PASS line reads 'PASS at the registered cost only, not at double; cost in stress was not measured'.
L4 LAG. The same t at lag 0 and at lag 12. If the lag-12 t is under the bar the verdict line adds 'not at lag 12'.
L5 WITH THE SEEN EPISODES. Every gated number a second time with signals of the two SEEN WINDOWS allowed, labelled 'with the two seen episodes; weightless'.

L6 MIRROR. The first 21 market days after entry for the rule, against the first 21 after a rich reading (z above +2 for two days), sign reversed. Data faults and bounce are symmetric; if the two are the same size, the first month is faults and bounce.

L7 AFTER A CUT. Signals within 63 market days after a regular distribution at least 10% below the one before it at the same frequency (ex-date on or before s), against all other signals: count and dollars of each.

L8 THE OPERATOR'S EXIT. The same entries, each sold at the close of the first market day AFTER a day t on which d[t] is at or above the lookback mean as it stood on the signal day (d[t] is known that evening, so the sale is the next close), with the same 252-day cap: gap dollars and price dollars after costs. Labelled 'the rule as the operator put it; not what was tested'.
L9 SAME BET AS THE ETF DIP-BUY? The correlation of monthly G and D with R313's monthly net series over their common months, and the share of entries made within three sessions of an R313 entry day.

L10 SURVIVORSHIP TABLE, and no single haircut. Per calendar year: the funds able to signal, beside the Investment Company Institute's year-end count of listed closed-end funds where one is on file (2007: 659; 2011: 628; 2019: 494; 2023: 401; 2024: 382; straight-line between them, marked approximate). And the headline recomputed three ways, the missing funds weighted year by year by the missing share: (i) their positions earned what the survivors' did; (ii) 6 points a year less; (iii) 6 points a year more (6 points is the published one-year difference between all funds an activist attacked and the survivors among them, 142 US equity funds, 1988-2002).
L11 REGIMES AND BAD DAYS. BOOK, D and G in the months SPY fell, was within 2% of flat, and rose; and on the worst 5% of SPY days of the span.

L12 SHAPE. By month since entry 1 to 12; by cost group; by entry month of the year and entry half-month; the best 5% of months' share of the total; where the real book's mean sits among 500 books whose signal calendar is the real one moved by one random whole number of months, the same for every fund, wrapping inside the span (the percentile is a label; the median of these books is the gate S5).
validity: Each runs before the read it guards. A failure is CANNOT MEASURE for that span, recorded; it is never amended so that it passes, and the remedy is a successor registration counted in the family. Each prints counts, dates, clock times, lists and pass or fail — never a mean return of the real book.
V1 SELFTEST: --selftest ends 'ALL n PASSED' on the frozen build; the count of cases never falls (RUNNER-SPEC.md lists them).

V2 AS-OF REPLAY on the real series: for at least 2000 sampled (fund, day) pairs per span, the signal, z and eligibility computed from the series cut off at that day equal those from the full series. Zero mismatches. Only the count is printed.

V3 DATA SCREENS: every split event classified (repaired, already adjusted, unverified small, unverified large); unit repair finds MGF, MIN, FAX, BKT, NCV, NCZ, IAF, AWP, BRW and SABA unadjusted and leaves CLM, TYG, SRV and ADX alone (unit facts the data scout established); volume is in the price's split units (30-day median dollar volume within a factor of 2 across each large split, else quarantined around it); for every split of ratio 1.5 or more the median of distribution / close over the six distributions before and the six after agree within a factor of 1.5, else the fund's positions before the event are void; a fund-year with fewer distributions than its stated frequency implies is named and the read is printed with and without it. Printed and written into the controls file: every unverified event with its size, every fund and fund-day removed because of a LATER event (each read prints those two counts beside its headline), every fund named for more than 1% of rows outside the band, every fund whose NAV history starts more than three years after its launch.

V4 EX-DATE ALIGNMENT: for every distribution of 1% of the price or more, whether the NAV fell by at least half the amount within one market day of the price's ex-date. A fund with more than three misses is named and its signals within ten market days after any distribution are void. Counts only.

V5 IDENTITY: every fund whose price or NAV series begins more than 60 days before the list's inception date, whose first price row is later than both 1999-01-01 and one year after that inception date, or whose NAV symbol is not X + ticker + X is named; for each, the gap on five dates either side of each join is set against the second source; a fund that cannot be confirmed is used only from the later of the inception date and the last unexplained join.

V6 PUBLICATION CHECK: on 3 market days on which both the stock and the bond market are open, every NAV symbol is asked for at 17:30, 18:30 and 20:30 New York and at 08:30, 12:00 and 15:30 the next market day; recorded per fund: the first look at which the daily row for day D has a value; and, for a seeded sample of 40 funds, the first look at which the live quote differs from the row for D-1 (context only; it decides nothing). A fund with no value for D at 15:30 on D+1 on 2 of the 3 days is a LATE REPORTER: its entries (real, placebo and control) are at the close of the second market day after the signal, in both spans. If more than 5% of the funds are late reporters, every entry in the test moves to the second close. DATE CHECK (needs the operator's yes; the public list's terms are unread): on five evenings the list is fetched once and each fund's NAV and its stated date are looked up on Yahoo's rows for that date and the market days either side; a fund whose value sits on another day's row on three of the five is a LATE REPORTER too. Levels and dates only; the list's discount, z-score and return fields are never read. A late-reporter flag is today's knowledge applied backward; it can only delay a fill.

V7 SECOND SOURCE (levels only): every fund's gap on each Friday of the public list's weekly history against the runner's gap that day; a fund passes at 95% of Fridays within 0.5 point, else it is quarantined. For the earlier years, 30 funds drawn by seed, plus every fund whose units were repaired under [4], are set against the net asset value and market price per share in the fund's own shareholder reports on EDGAR: two period-ends in 2003-2011 and two in 2012-2020 each (for a repaired fund, two before its split): within 1 point on 95% of them, or the read is CANNOT MEASURE (data); a repaired fund that fails is quarantined before its event and listed with the funds removed for a later event. If the operator declines the public list's site, the EDGAR sample is doubled and the read's first line says 'one source after 2020'.

V8 SUSPICIOUS-SIGNAL AUDIT (prints no return): per span, the 40 real signals with the largest one-day change in the gap on the signal day are listed (fund, date, the two levels) and each is set against the second source or the fund's own notice. A signal whose gap that day is off by more than 2 points is void and counted. More than 8 void of 40: CANNOT MEASURE (data) for that span.

V9 ATTRITION BY STATE (counts only; wording, not a gate): on the two archived copies of the public list (2018-03-30 and 2021-05-04) each fund is placed by that list's own one-year z-score and discount into the rule's state (z below -2 and below asset value), the twin's state (z between -1 and +1 and below asset value) or neither; printed per state and copy: how many are gone from today's list, after a rename map built by hand. Fields kept: ticker, z-score, discount; no return is read. If the gone share of the two states differs by more than 15 points on either copy, the read's first paragraph says 'the placebo does not share the rule's survivorship; funds in the rule's state left the list more (or less) often'.

V10 NO-EDGE WORLDS: 200 per span. A no-edge world: for each market day ONE sign, +1 or -1 with equal chance (seeded), is drawn once and applied to every fund's change in ln(P/N) on that day; nothing is shuffled; each path starts at the fund's real first value and is not pinned at its last; a row that wanders outside the band of [5] is invalid, as in the real data (no reflecting wall); the NAV, the distributions and the events are kept and the price is rebuilt. Gate: the deciding t is at or above the bar in at most 16 of the 200 worlds, and the WHOLE decision rule passes in at most 10. The same worlds record how often discovery's mean is above $0. Every false-pass rate, standard deviation and power figure of this test is taken from these worlds (100 placebo draws and 100 month-shifted books on a world, 500 of each on a real read). The 95th percentile of the deciding t over these worlds is written to the controls file and enters the bar in force (bar.raisedInTheRead); it can only raise it.

V11 FAULT WORLDS: on each of 200 no-edge worlds per span, faults are put back by seed, with no edge: (i) on 1.9% of fund-days the NAV is held at the previous value for one to three further rows; (ii) for municipal, loan and foreign-clock funds, on days the price moves more than 2% the NAV's own move is spread over the next three rows; (iii) 30 NAV prints per span that are 1.15 to 1.29 times the true value for one or two rows; (iv) for 2% of distributions the NAV falls one market day after the price; (v) half the class one-way cost of bounce, with a random sign, on every close. Gate: the whole decision rule passes in at most 10 of the 200 fault worlds, and the mean across them of the headline is at or below $0 (with no edge the book should lose its costs; faults must not buy them back). The 1.9% is measured; the other rates are single house choices.

V12 POWER: (a) planted worlds: the no-edge world plus the published speed — each day each fund's gap is pulled toward its trailing 252-day mean by 1 - 0.5^(1/162) of the distance (a half-life of 7.7 months). Gate: the deciding t is at or above the bar in at least 10 of 20 such worlds, else CANNOT MEASURE (power) and the real book's dollars are not computed for that span. (b) recorded, not gated: with 0.2%, 0.34%, 0.78% a month (three published sizes) added to every real position-month of a no-edge world, the share of worlds in which the WHOLE decision rule passes, per span and for discovery-then-holdout together. (c) inside each read, after the lock and before the real statistic: sigma = the standard deviation over months of G for books whose signal calendar is the real one moved by one random whole number of months (500 seeded shifts, each against the placebo mean); smallest effect found four times in five = (bar + 0.8416) x sigma / sqrt(months).

V13 SAMPLE: holdout at least 100 completed round trips and a position open in at least 120 of 177 months; discovery at least 60 and 72 of 108; in each span no more than 10% of real positions without a clean series. From the real trade list --controls writes and prints these counts and nothing else: no date, no fund, no z, no dollar.
V14 PLACEBO SANITY: one placebo draw against the mean of the others shows a t at or above the bar in at most 3 of 20 draws.

V15 CACHE: fetched on or after 2026-10-15 (ten market days after the holdout's last day); the last 10 market days of the span are fetched a second time 10 market days later and the two copies compared (count of changed rows, no values); a fund with a changed row is listed before the read. Rows dated 2012-01-03 or later are cached in separate files: the loader hands them to the holdout read only after its lock file is written, and to --controls only through functions that return counts, flags, and pass or fail on made worlds. The holdout read, after its lock and before the real book, runs V2, V12(c) and V13 on the holdout rows and stops at CANNOT MEASURE if one fails.

V16 TOO GOOD OR TOO BAD: a discovery mean of G or of D above $1,517 or below -$1,517 a month per $100,000 (18.2% a year, the largest published gross long-short figure), or a discovery t above 6 or below -6, puts the read on HOLD: the 20 largest positions by absolute dollars, gains and losses alike, are checked by hand against a second source. Any artifact among them: CANNOT MEASURE on this runner, the holdout stays locked, and a repaired pipeline is a new registration in this family.

preregistered.interimKill: There is one interim look and it is the discovery read: the holdout is not read, and stays locked, if discovery is DID NOT PASS, CANNOT MEASURE or an unresolved HOLD. Inside a span there is none: each span is one historical read. Before any read, a failed validity gate stops that span at CANNOT MEASURE; the runner refuses a read unless the controls file says every gate passed on the same frozen cache hash. The build never runs a read: --read is in the build loop's forbidden list.

decisionRule.discovery: ONE read of 2003-2011, sealed the same day. PROCEED only if every validity gate passed for discovery and the mean of G over its 108 months is above $0. Its t is printed against 1.73 and does not gate: nothing is fitted in discovery, it only shows the pipeline points the right way in the years the published studies cover, on a third of the funds that existed. Mean at or below $0: DID NOT PASS at discovery — 'in 2003-2011, on survivors, the book did not earn its costs in the gap over holding'; the holdout is never opened by this test. A validity gate failed: CANNOT MEASURE; the holdout stays locked.
decisionRule.pass: PASS only if ALL hold: (1) every validity gate passed, in both spans; (2) discovery sealed PROCEED; (3) holdout: the Newey-West lag-4 t of G is at or above the bar in force (tRequired 1.727, or the higher number of bar.raisedInTheRead); (4) holdout S1: mean D above $0; (5) holdout S2: mean G21 above $0; (6) holdout S3: mean G on US-clock funds above $0; (7) holdout S4: mean GPEER above $0; (8) holdout S5: mean G per position opened above the median of the same figure over L12's 500 month-shifted books. The read's first lines then say, with their own numbers: 'On funds that survived to October 2026, from 2012 to September 2026, with signals of 2020-02 to 2020-04 left out because a scout saw those weeks (and 2008-09 to 2008-12 in discovery), a 24-place $100,000 book of funds below asset value and two standard deviations cheap against their own year made $G a month in the gap after its costs, more than the same funds held from random days for nothing (t against the bar). Of the book's gap dollars $YIELD a month is the extra yield of buying below asset value, which needs no move in the gap. From the 21st day on: $G21. In funds priced on the US clock: $GUS. Without the fund's own asset value: $GPEER. In all price dollars against the placebo: $D. The book's own dollars were $BOOK a month, which includes what the funds themselves earned; its worst month was $W. The figure set against the operator's $500-a-month catalogue line is the SMALLEST of G, G21, GUS and D. On survivors; from $A(ii) to $A(iii) if the missing funds differed by six points a year either way; which is true cannot be measured on this data.' If label L5's mean G is at or below $0, the first line adds 'turns negative when the seen weeks are allowed'. Then the labels L1 to L12 and the dollar table. A PASS adopts nothing, sizes nothing and moves no money. It goes to three independent refuters, and it PROPOSES — the operator decides — a forward paper test as its own registration: the 359-fund list frozen 2026-10-09, every fund followed to its end, first-seen asset values only, live spreads stamped at each fill, no purchase of a term fund within 504 market days of its term date, the first order placed with the operator watching.
decisionRule.fail: DID NOT PASS if discovery's mean G is at or below $0, or any of conditions (3) to (8) fails. First line: 'Not demonstrated, with signals of 2020-02 to 2020-04 left out because a scout saw those weeks (and 2008-09 to 2008-12 in discovery): after its costs the book's gap dollars did not beat holding the same funds [or: the t cleared and the check named here did not]. Point estimate $G a month per $100,000 (t against the bar). The smallest planted size the whole rule found four times in five was X [or: none of the three published sizes].' Where the whole rule finds 0.78% a month in fewer than half the planted worlds the line ends 'under-powered, not disproven'. $0 is put on the idea; no forward test is proposed; closed for this paced book (one purchase a half-month); a book free to load up after a blow-out was not tested. If label L5's mean G is at or below $0, the first line says so. Not demonstrated is not disproven.
decisionRule.nearMiss: A t below the bar in force by any margin is DID NOT PASS. The comparison is made on the unrounded t; both are printed to three decimals. There is no second read, no other lag, no other month minimum, no trimming and no re-drawn bar. A miss within 0.05 of the bar is reported in the same words as any other miss, with the effect the whole rule finds four times in five beside it. It opens nothing and proposes nothing.
decisionRule.cannotMeasure: CANNOT MEASURE if a validity gate fails, the sample minimums are not met or the power gate fails, for the span concerned. Recorded with the counts; nothing concluded; the gate is never changed so that it passes. The remedy is a successor registration, counted in the family.
decisionRule.hold: HOLD under V16 (a discovery result too good or too bad to be read without a hand check). It ends as PROCEED, DID NOT PASS or CANNOT MEASURE by V16's own words, never by a changed rule.
decisionRule.dollarTable: Printed at every read, per span, every figure with the command that prints it: dollars at risk per position ($4,000) and at the busiest moment; G, G21, GUS, GPEER, D, BOOK and YIELD in dollars a month per $100,000, each at 1, 2 and 3 times the charged cost; gross gains and gross losses; wins and losses with the average win and the average loss; total cost paid; the worst month and the worst run of months; the average number of positions and the share of months with all 24 places taken; positions without a clean series; open positions sold at the span's end; the same for the placebo mean; the worst-5%-of-SPY-days column.

preregistered.readCondition: ONE discovery read, then — only on a sealed PROCEED — ONE holdout read; each only when ALL hold: (1) this entry is in preregistered[] and the runner's frozen constants equal parameters{} (the runner refuses otherwise); (2) the runner was built by the standard build loop (builder, separate checker, independent reviewers with mutation tests on made series only) with --read forbidden to the build; (3) the cache was fetched on or after 2026-10-15 and frozen, and ONE dated pre-read note, appended to amendments[] (kind 'hash-note'; it changes no commitment), carries the sha256 of the cache manifest and of the controls file (which holds every list the validity gates wrote: unit classes, quarantines, late reporters, the cost table in force); (4) --selftest ends 'ALL n PASSED'; (5) --controls wrote V1 to V15 for that span, all passed, on that same cache hash; (6) the clock is outside 13:50-15:50 MT on a trading day; (7) the date is on or before 2027-01-31 for discovery. Both reads are sealed the same day by the main loop (docs/server/seal-gated-arms.cjs; discovery and holdout are two arms). The runner prints and never seals. A second read of a span refuses.
knownWeaknesses: SURVIVORSHIP, first and worst, and no historical read on this data can repair it. Every fund in the test is alive on 2026-10-09. Of the 528 funds on the same public list in March 2018, 228 (43%) are gone by ticker; of the 467 in May 2021, 143 (31%). At the end of 2011 the test sees about 38% of the funds the industry body counted; in 2003 every fund in it has by construction lived 23 more years. Funds leave in four ways and they do not push the same way. Open-endings, liquidations, conversions and term ends pay asset value, and tender offers pay near it on part of a position: both are missing, both are a discount buyer's best outcome, and in the one published comparison (142 US equity funds, 1988-2002) a survivors-only sample understated the fall in attacked funds' discounts by about 6 points in the year after an attempt. Mergers into sister funds are about neutral. Funds that collapsed and were then merged or wound up are a dollar loss that is missing. So for the gap the missing funds more likely hide an edge than fake one, and for a dollar result the collapsed funds flatter it. None of this is measured on this universe. The placebo shares the survivors' average drift and does not share the link between 'cheap against its own year' and 'later died'; V9 counts that link on two dates and the read says what it found. Only a forward test on the list frozen now can settle it.

THE COST IS AN ASSUMPTION for every year but this one. The class costs are estimates for 1986-2004 by fund type (Hasbrouck's effective-cost estimate divided by price, as that paper describes it; one-way, doubled here); the municipal figure is confirmed by the paper's own sentence and the other three are read from its table row in its sector order. The own spread, if recorded, is measured in 2026 and applied backward, and can only raise a charge. No historical quote exists here. Signals bunch in stress, when real spreads are several times normal. The fill is the close as it printed WITHOUT our order: the size of the closing auction in these funds is not known, and a $4,000 order may be a large part of it.

THE SERIES ARE TODAY'S VERSION, not what was published each evening. Rows of this history were rewritten after the fact: FAX, NCV and SABA show asset values in post-split units months before their splits; 155 of 320 NAV histories start more than 90 days after the price; an asset value sent late or corrected later sits in the history as if it had been there that evening. How often an ordinary value was restated is not known at registration. A cleaned history shows a tidier gap than a trader saw. Only a recorder of first-seen values measures this, and only from the day it starts.

PUBLICATION TIME IS PARTLY AN INFERENCE. The 20:00 New York deadline is documented for open-end funds; closed-end values travel the same service. On 2026-10-12 Yahoo's daily series showed no value for the day by 17:43 New York in 46 of 46 funds, and its time stamps on Friday's values were Monday morning. V6 times it per fund in 2026 and moves late reporters to the second close; that is today's behaviour applied to 2003.

THE GATED NUMBER IS NOT A POSITION ANYONE CAN HOLD. The asset value cannot be sold short; a fitted basket of indexes leaves about 29% of the variance of a fund's asset-value return unhedged in the one study that tried. G says the gap moved; only D and BOOK are money, and D gates on sign only.

LATE AND STALE ASSET VALUES can still fake part of G. Municipal bonds, loans and foreign holdings are priced by services that lag the market. The two-day confirmation, the next-close entry, the fresh-NAV tests, the clean start, S2, S3, S4 and the fault worlds each remove part. A value that moves a little every day while lagging the market by weeks is not seen by any rule here.

A DISCOUNT IS MOST EXTREME WHEN IT IS DESERVED: a distribution about to be cut, a rights offering, borrowing costs above yield, a tender that has just ended, a normal level that has shifted for good. The series see none of these in advance and there is no stop. Tender offers pay near asset value on part of a position and are in no series: each one missed understates a holder's result by about 0.4% of the position for a 5% tender and about 2% for a 25% tender, and they follow the wide discounts the rule buys.

IT MAY BE THE HOUSE'S DIP-BUY AGAIN. A fund two standard deviations cheap is nearly always one whose price just fell faster than its holdings, bought from the same seller on the same bad days as an ETF dip-buyer's entries, in a security that costs many times more to trade. The gap statistic, S2 and L9 speak to it; none is a proof of independence.

HOUSE CHOICES. Six numbers are published (the discount formula, the one-year lookback, less than -2, three years of history, the liquidity floor in part, the class cost). The one-year hold and the 2011/2012 boundary are the house's, each tied to a published fact. The rest are house choices, each named once here before any series was read for outcomes and never varied: today outside its own window, 230 rows, two days of confirmation, below asset value, the next-close entry, 24 places of $4,000, one purchase a half-month, lowest z first, the screens of [3], [4] and [6], the clean start and end, the 2003 start, lag 4, and every number of the controls. None was searched. These were set with the data scout's full-history screens in view and are disclosed as such (seenBeforeRegistration): the price factor 1.9 (above the largest real one-day move it saw, 1.74 times), the NAV factor 1.3, the band 0.5-2.0 and the 15% and three-row undo test, the freeze and weekly-NAV tests, and the two window dates. Another writer would have another test; the result is about this book.

THE FIXED ONE-YEAR HOLD IS NOT THE OPERATOR'S RULE. He said 'sell when the gap closes'. That exit is label L8 only. A pass here does not show his version pays; his version turns over more and costs more.

THE BOOK TAKES FEW OF THE SIGNALS. One purchase a half-month from a universe of hundreds: the book usually takes the first signal day of each half-month, and the lowest z of that day. The result says little about the average signal, entries sit near the 1st and the 16th, and the book cannot load up after a market-wide blow-out (two purchases a month at most). The half-month rule and the 24 places are this registrar's own, written to stop a fixed one-year hold from locking every purchase to the anniversary of the span's first days (early January, when year-end selling is said to leave discounts wide); no skeptic reviewed that clause before registration; the experiment-registrar did, and its fixes (rule [8] on which half-month owns a position, the sign gate S5, and the placebo's wording) are in this entry.

SEEN MATERIAL. Published results, one unit trust's price path, two crisis days and a list of extreme levels were seen before registration (seenBeforeRegistration). Signals of the two seen windows are out of every gated number, which gives up the largest episode of the holdout: that is what seeing it cost. Positions opened before a window are still measured through it. It is still not a blind test.
DISCOVERY IS A SIGN SCREEN, NOT A BAR, on the thinnest, most survivor-heavy years. With no effect it lets the test through a share of the time that V10 records; the holdout bar alone carries the 5%.

THE PLACEBO DOES NOT SHARE THE PACE, AND S5 ONLY HALVES THE HOLE. Any 252-day hold spans each calendar month once, so the t is fair on the calendar in the main; but the pacing, the 24-place cap and the day in the month are the real book's alone, and S5 checks them by rank only: an effect the shifted books share (a gain made by the pace itself) still passes S5 about half the time.
FIVE SIGN GATES AND ONE T. The conjunction is strict on purpose and will fail a real but modest effect more often than a single gate; V12 measures how often, and a miss says so.

MONTHS ARE NOT INDEPENDENT for a book that holds for a year. Lag 4 and the block-resampled bar help and do not cure it; market-wide discount regimes last longer than four months, and the spans hold only a handful of them.

LABELS APPLIED BACKWARD. The list, each fund's asset class and cost group, the term flag and the late-reporter flag are today's. A fund that once had a term and dropped it is treated as never having had one. The $400,000 floor is a 2012-2016 number applied flat to 2003. Unit repair is by rule; small ratios cannot be verified (1.8 points in GAB, 3.5 in GGZ and 4.75 in RIV among the funds read so far; most split lists are unread until --controls lists them).
TWO UNDOCUMENTED ENDPOINTS. Yahoo's chart API and the public list. Either can change or block without notice; neither site's terms of use were read.
TAXES AND CASH ARE IGNORED. Distributions and gains are taxed and municipal income is not; idle cash earns nothing here.
PAPER IS KINDER THAN A MARKET. Any forward test that follows must price fills at recorded quotes, not at a paper account's own fills.
preregistered.wouldEstablish: For funds that are alive in October 2026, in 2012 to September 2026 and with the same sign in 2003 to 2011: this exact book's gap dollars, after its trading costs, beat the same funds held from random days for nothing, at a bar fixed before any series was read for outcomes; with the price dollars also ahead, the effect still there after the first month, in funds priced on the US clock, when the fund's own asset value is taken out of the yardstick, and against the middle of 500 books on its own calendar moved by whole months; without the two episodes a scout saw. It would be the first test on data after 2011 that the house knows of, and it would say a forward paper test is worth its years.
preregistered.wouldNotEstablish: That it holds for all funds, the dead included; that the operator's own exit pays; that it works now or will (the z-score is printed free on a public site and three activists hold shares in 44% of funds); that $100,000 of real money would get these fills or these costs; that it is a second bet beside the house's dip-buy winners; anything about another lookback, hold or book size; any sizing. A miss would establish only 'not demonstrated on these funds under these controls, to the size the power line states' — not that it is impossible.

preregistered.origin: Outside-model candidate slate 2026-10-15 (backend/data/xai-strategy-hunt-grok-4.7.json). The model was given this desk's exclusion list, cost reality and size test, and returned five candidates with its own priors. It is a flaw and idea generator here, never a verdict: a calibration the same day (backend/data/xai-refuter-calibration-grok-4.3.json) scored it 2 of 6 on naming known defects and it wrongly condemned 1 of 2 sound controls, so its 13% and 12% priors carry no weight in these registrations.
preregistered.name: Capped-call hedge chase — hold the stock only while it trades between a disclosed capped call's lower strike and its cap
preregistered.status: REGISTERED 2026-10-15 — historical, read once; builder assigned
preregistered.parent: Outside-model candidate 2026-10-15, 'Capped-call hedge chase'. Untested here; not in the exclusion list the model was given.
preregistered.multiplicityFamily: FORCED-HEDGE — R356 alone. The rule is taken VERBATIM from the external proposal (band = lower strike to cap, 20-day dollar volume over $20m, at most 8 names, most recent deal per issuer); no parameter was searched by us, so the bar is single-variant. Any later variant of the band or the universe owes a best-of-N bar and a new id.
preregistered.evidenceStart: historical, not yet fetched: convertible note issues with a concurrent capped call, 2016-01-01..2026-09-30, from EDGAR. No filing list and no price series for this population has been pulled as of registration.
preregistered.rule: POPULATION: US-listed issuers whose 8-K or prospectus supplement discloses a convertible note priced with a CONCURRENT CAPPED CALL, 2016-2026, where the filing states both the lower strike (the conversion price) and the cap price. One deal per issuer, the most recent, so no issuer contributes twice. UNIVERSE FILTER at each entry: 20-day average dollar volume above $20,000,000 on the day before entry. POSITION: hold the common stock, equal weight, on every session whose PRIOR close sits strictly between the lower strike and the cap; exit at the close of the first session whose close leaves the band; at most 8 names held at once, and when more qualify, take the 8 with the largest 20-day dollar volume. Decisions use completed closes only. COST 17 basis points per side, the desk's MEASURED equity crossing cost, not a modelled spread.
preregistered.statistic: HOLD-RELATIVE and that is the headline: for each calendar month, (the band book's net return) minus (the net return of holding the SAME names at the same weights continuously from each deal's pricing date to its cap expiry). Unit: CALENDAR MONTH, because names overlap in time and share market beta, so trades are not independent. Headline t = Newey-West lag 1 over months. The band book's own absolute return is REPORTED, never the headline.

controls.placebo: SHIFTED-BAND PLACEBO: the identical rule on a band of the same width placed 20% above the real cap, where no hedging obligation exists, same names, same costs, 500 draws; GATE: the real monthly paired difference exceeds the placebo p95.
controls.holdBenchmark: the primary statistic IS the hold comparison; the gate is its Newey-West t over months.
controls.marketBeta: the band book minus a beta-matched SPY position over the same months, reported, to show the difference is not simply market exposure.
controls.halves: months split at the median date; both halves' mean difference > 0.
controls.cost2x: 34 basis points per side: monthly mean difference still > 0.
controls.leakTest: deal dates shuffled within calendar year across issuers (keeps the era, destroys the link to the specific deal), >= 200 shuffles; the whole decision rule's false-pass rate must be <= 5% or the read is HELD for an amendment.
controls.positiveControl: months whose own realised difference > 0: t_NW >= 3, else CANNOT MEASURE.
controls.reported: the band book's absolute return; number of deals and of name-days; time in market; the result excluding 2020-2021; per-issuer contribution and the largest single name's share; sensitivity to the 8-name cap.

bar.statistic: Newey-West t, lag 1, on the monthly hold-relative difference
bar.source: max(NW lag-1 sim n=48 seed 356 p95 1.719, nullBar variants 1 n=48 p95 1.654)

preregistered.interimKill: none (single historical read). CANNOT MEASURE if fewer than 24 months carry a live deal.

decisionRule.pass: PASS only if >= 24 months with a live deal AND >= 30 distinct issuers AND the monthly mean hold-relative difference > 0 AND t_NW >= 1.719 AND the shifted-band placebo gate clears AND both halves > 0 AND the 2x-cost mean > 0 AND the leak calibration <= 5% AND the positive control passed. A PASS proposes a forward paper arm only; sizing and funding remain the operator's.
decisionRule.fail: DID NOT PASS: the dealer's hedge chase inside the band is not harvestable in the common stock after measured costs; the mechanism is closed at this implementation.
decisionRule.cannotMeasure: CANNOT MEASURE if the filings do not yield >= 30 issuers with both strikes stated, if price coverage gaps exceed 5% of name-days, or if the leak test or positive control fails.

knownWeaknesses: The 'obligation' is the weakest in the slate: a bank hedges a short call spread dynamically and chooses its timing, venue and instrument. It is not obliged to buy at any particular price on any particular day, unlike an index fund at a reconstitution close.
The hedge may be in options or a basket rather than the single name, in which case the flow never touches the stock.
Survivorship: issuers that were acquired or delisted mid-band must be included at their delisting price or the sample is biased upward.
Convertible issuers skew to high-growth names in a window containing 2020-2021; the excluded-era read is reported for that reason.
Band membership is mechanically correlated with the stock having risen since issue, so the naive version is a momentum bet; the hold comparator is what removes that, and it is the whole test.
Capped-call terms are sometimes stated only in an exhibit, so a hand-checked subsample is needed to confirm the parser.
preregistered.readCondition: --read once, after --selftest passes and every control has run, sealed the same day through the read-test ritual.

preregistered.name: Mortgage convexity hedge flow — follow the forced duration hedge on large yield moves while the mortgage rate sits near its own trailing average
preregistered.status: REGISTERED 2026-10-15 — historical, read once; builder assigned · AMENDED 2026-10-15 (R357-A1-statistic-asymmetry: statistic asymmetry disclosed; bar and gates unchanged)
preregistered.parent: Outside-model candidate 2026-10-15, 'Mortgage convexity hedge flow'. Untested here. Adjacent in asset class to R180/R186 (month-end Treasuries), which are SEPARATE mechanisms (calendar flow, not convexity) — correlation to the Plan E Treasury leg is a REQUIRED reported quantity, see controls.
preregistered.multiplicityFamily: FORCED-HEDGE — R357 with two declared arms (yield-rise and yield-fall), so a best-of-2 bar. The zone width (75 basis points), the lookback (36 months), the trigger (5 basis points) and the hold (2 sessions) are taken VERBATIM from the external proposal and were not searched by us; any later change to them owes a new id.
preregistered.evidenceStart: historical, not yet fetched: 2016-01-01..2026-09-30. The mortgage and yield series exist in backend/data/training/fred/ for other tests; no series has been read for THIS rule as of registration.
preregistered.rule: ZONE: the Freddie Mac 30-year mortgage rate (FRED MORTGAGE30US, weekly, carried forward) lies within 75 basis points of its own trailing 36-month average, computed from strictly earlier observations. TRIGGER: on any session inside the zone where the 10-year Treasury yield (FRED DGS10) moved more than 5 basis points versus the prior session. POSITION, taken at that session's cash close: if the yield ROSE, be SHORT duration; if it FELL, be LONG duration. Exit at the close two sessions later. One position at a time; a new trigger while in a position is ignored. INSTRUMENT: IEF, the liquid seven-to-ten year Treasury fund, because the desk's futures store holds front-month continuous bars only from 2024-07-29 and cannot serve this window. COST 4 basis points per side on IEF. The futures expression is NOT tested here and would be a new registration.
preregistered.statistic: HOLD-RELATIVE and that is the headline: (the triggered book's net return) minus (the net return of holding IEF continuously over the identical sessions), per EPISODE, then averaged within WEEK. Unit: WEEK cluster, because triggers arrive in bursts around the same macro events. Headline t = Newey-West lag 1 over weeks. The triggered book's absolute return is REPORTED, never the headline.

controls.placebo: OUT-OF-ZONE CONTROL: the identical trigger and hold on sessions where the mortgage rate is OUTSIDE the 75 basis point zone, where the convexity story does not apply; GATE: the in-zone weekly mean exceeds the out-of-zone mean, and the difference's t >= the bar. If the effect is as strong outside the zone, the mechanism is not convexity.
controls.holdBenchmark: the primary statistic IS the hold comparison.
controls.shuffled: trigger days shuffled within calendar quarter, 500 draws: observed weekly mean exceeds the shuffled p95.
controls.planECorrelation: REQUIRED REPORT: correlation of this stream to PLAN-E-TSY and to PLAN-E-CORE over the common window, and separately on Plan E's worst 5% of days. A leg that is simply more of the book's largest existing bet is not a diversifier, whatever its t.
controls.halves: weeks split at the median date; both halves' mean > 0.
controls.cost2x: 8 basis points per side: weekly mean still > 0.
controls.leakTest: the yield series block-shuffled in 30-day blocks (keeps persistence, destroys the link to the mortgage zone), >= 200 shuffles; whole-rule false-pass rate <= 5% or the read is HELD.
controls.positiveControl: episodes whose own realised difference > 0: t_NW >= 3, else CANNOT MEASURE.
controls.reported: each arm separately (rise and fall), since one may carry the whole result; episodes per year; the 2020 and 2022 subsamples; the result with a 1-session and a 3-session hold, as sensitivity only, never as the headline.

bar.statistic: Newey-West t, lag 1, on the weekly hold-relative difference
bar.source: max(NW lag-1 sim n=200 seed 357 variants 2 p95 1.982, nullBar variants 2 n=200 p95 1.94)

preregistered.interimKill: none (single historical read). CANNOT MEASURE if fewer than 60 week clusters carry an episode.

decisionRule.pass: PASS only if >= 60 week clusters AND >= 150 episodes AND the weekly mean hold-relative difference > 0 AND t_NW >= 1.982 AND the in-zone effect beats the out-of-zone control at the bar AND the shuffled placebo p95 is beaten AND both halves > 0 AND the 2x-cost mean > 0 AND the leak calibration <= 5% AND the positive control passed. Even on a PASS, a correlation above 0.5 to the Plan E Treasury leg on its worst 5% of days DISQUALIFIES it as a diversifying leg, and it may then only be considered as a replacement for part of that leg, never as an addition.
decisionRule.fail: DID NOT PASS: convexity hedging flow is not harvestable through a liquid Treasury fund at this horizon after costs; the ETF expression is closed. A futures expression with lower cost would be a new registration and needs a history this desk does not hold.
decisionRule.cannotMeasure: CANNOT MEASURE if fewer than 60 week clusters, if the FRED series have coverage gaps exceeding 2% of sessions, or if the leak test or positive control fails.

knownWeaknesses: The instrument is a proxy: the real hedging flow is in Treasury futures and swaps, and IEF's cost and duration differ from a ten-year future's. A null here does not close the futures version.
Mortgage convexity hedging is a well-documented, widely-watched flow, so any easy part of it is likely competed away; the desk's own base rate for published effects is poor.
The 36-month trailing zone is adaptive and will label different eras differently; the out-of-zone control exists to test whether the zone is doing any work at all.
2020-2021 Federal Reserve purchases dominated this market and may create or destroy the effect; both subsamples are reported.

The two arms are not symmetric in the mechanism: extension on a rise is the forced one, shortening on a fall is more discretionary, so a result carried entirely by the fall arm is evidence AGAINST the stated mechanism and must be read that way.
This sits in rates, where the funded book already carries its largest bet, so even a clean pass may add no diversification; that is why the Plan E correlation is a gate and not a footnote.
preregistered.readCondition: --read once, after --selftest passes and every control has run, sealed the same day through the read-test ritual.

amendments.legalBecause: no evidence has been read: no --read has run, no headline statistic exists, and R357 has no seal
amendments.found: the R357 builder and its independent checker, 2026-10-15
amendments.defect: The registered primary is (timed book) minus (holding IEF continuously). The fall arm's position IS long IEF, so for those episodes the difference is identically -(2 x cost), about -8 basis points, regardless of the market. 125 of 240 episodes and 108 of 218 week clusters are pure fall-arm, so the headline is carried entirely by the rise arm and the statistic's no-effect null is centred near t -2.46 (p95 about -0.89), not 0.
amendments.effectOnDifficulty: STRICTER, not looser: the registered bar of 1.982 sits about 2.87 t-units above that null, giving the test an empirical size under 0.5% against a nominal 5%. The 110 rise-carrying weeks must average about +7.85 basis points merely to bring the headline to zero.
amendments.unchanged: The primary statistic, the clustering unit, the bar of 1.982, every gate and both decision branches stand exactly as registered. Nothing is loosened.
addedRequirements: The read record MUST carry the empirically calibrated critical value of the registered statistic beside the registered bar, so that a large negative t is read as the structural constant it is and not as evidence against the mechanism.
The read record MUST state the fall-arm share of episodes and of week clusters, and the break-even the rise arm has to clear.
A DID NOT PASS must say explicitly whether the headline fell short of 1.982 while still beating the statistic's own empirical null, because those are different findings.
amendments.knownWeaknessAdded: The hold-relative comparator is ill-posed for a two-sided rule: one arm's position is the comparator itself. A correctly specified successor would compare against a direction-matched placebo rather than a fixed long, and would be a NEW registration with its own bar, never a re-read of this one.

alsoRecorded.planEDisqualifier: Returns tri-state and is currently NULL, undecided. R357 is flat on 82% of sessions, so a stress slice is mostly structural zeros that drag Pearson toward 0 and the registered 0.5 threshold could never fire. On the 3 traded days inside the Treasury leg's worst 5% the correlation is +0.8169, which is 3 observations and therefore noise. The disqualifier is NOT cleared; it is undecided, and a pass must say so.
alsoRecorded.outOfZoneGate: In-zone and out-of-zone share only 3 of 218 week clusters (in-zone is 2016-19 and 2025-26, out-of-zone almost entirely 2022-24, with no in-zone episode at all in 2023), so the gate cannot separate 'the zone matters' from 'those years differed'. It still decides as registered; the read must disclose the era split.
alsoRecorded.positiveControl: The registered positive control is outcome-dependent and therefore runs inside --read; it is near-vacuous by construction and is a machinery check, not evidence.
alsoRecorded.costModel: 4 basis points a side with no borrow and no spread on a short IEF position is optimistic; the registered 2x control is the answer and is reported, not adjusted.
